Les expressions d’intérêt doivent être déposées ou transmises par courriel à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous au plus tard le 05 Octobre 2026 à 16 h 00 mn GMT. procnotices.notice_text:
DIRECTION GENERALE                                                                                                   N’Djaména, le 14 septembre 2026

CELLULE D’EXÉCUTION DE PROJETS

PASSATION DES MARCHES

N°012/TchadElec/DG/CEP /PM/2026

 

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊT

SÉLECTION DE CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

Recrutement d’un consultant individuel, expert senior résident en ressources humaines, organisation et conduite du changement, chargé d’accompagner au quotidien la Direction des Ressources Humaines de TchadElec

Pays :

République du Tchad

Entité :

Cellule d’Exécution des Projets de la Tchadienne d’Électricité (CEP–TchadElec)

Projet :

Projet d’Accroissement de l’Accès à l’Énergie au Tchad (PAAET)

Référence du projet :

P174495 – Don IDA D985-TD

 

La République du Tchad a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour la mise en œuvre du Projet d’Accroissement de l’Accès à l’Énergie au Tchad (PAAET) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du contrat relatif au recrutement d’un consultant individuel, expert senior résident en ressources humaines, organisation et conduite du changement, chargé d’accompagner au quotidien la Direction des Ressources Humaines de TchadElec.

La transition institutionnelle de la SNE vers TchadElec implique une amélioration concrète de l’organisation interne, de la gestion des effectifs, des compétences, des procédures RH et de la conduite du changement au sein de l’entreprise.

La Direction des Ressources Humaines est appelée à jouer un rôle déterminant dans la structuration de l’organisation, la professionnalisation des équipes, la clarification des responsabilités, la gestion prévisionnelle des emplois et compétences et la mise en place d’outils modernes de gestion du personnel.

La mission vise à mobiliser un expert senior résident, à plein temps, placé aux côtés du Directeur des Ressources Humaines, afin de l’accompagner dans les dossiers quotidiens, l’organisation du travail, l’amélioration des outils RH, la préparation des décisions et le transfert de compétences aux équipes internes.

La mission est prévue pour une durée de douze (12) mois, à plein temps, avec une présence régulière et effective à N’Djaména auprès de TchadElec et, plus particulièrement, auprès de la direction bénéficiaire.

L’objectif général de la mission est d’accompagner, au quotidien et à plein temps, le Directeur des Ressources Humaines de TchadElec dans le renforcement opérationnel de la fonction RH, de l’organisation interne et de la conduite du changement.

De manière spécifique, la mission portera notamment sur :

  • Appuyer quotidiennement le Directeur des Ressources Humaines dans l’organisation, le suivi et la priorisation des activités de la Direction ;
  • Contribuer à la finalisation ou à la mise à jour de l’organigramme, des fiches de poste et des responsabilités ;
  • Appuyer la cartographie des effectifs, des compétences et des besoins de renforcement ;
  • Contribuer à la mise en place d’outils de gestion prévisionnelle des emplois et compétences ;
  • Appuyer l’amélioration des procédures RH : recrutement, formation, évaluation, mobilité, discipline et gestion administrative du personnel ;
  • Accompagner la préparation d’un plan de formation prioritaire et d’un dispositif de suivi ;
  • Appuyer les actions de conduite du changement liées à la réforme de TchadElec ;
  • Assurer un coaching opérationnel et un transfert de compétences aux cadres et agents RH.

La mission sera conduite dans une logique d’accompagnement quotidien, de proximité, de pragmatisme et de transfert de compétences. L’expert n’aura pas vocation à se substituer aux responsables internes de TchadElec, mais à les appuyer dans l’exercice effectif de leurs responsabilités et dans la montée en compétence progressive des équipes.

La langue de travail est le français.

La Cellule d’Exécution de Projets de TchadElec invite les consultants individuels admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus.

Le consultant devra disposer au minimum des qualifications suivantes :

  • Diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 en ressources humaines, organisation, management, droit social, administration, psychologie du travail ou domaine équivalent ;
  • Au moins quinze ans d’expérience professionnelle en gestion des ressources humaines, organisation, conduite du changement ou développement institutionnel ;
  • Expérience confirmée dans l’accompagnement opérationnel de directions rh ;
  • Expérience dans la restructuration, la modernisation ou le renforcement organisationnel d’entreprises publiques ou de grandes organisations ;
  • Expérience dans l’élaboration d’organigrammes, fiches de poste, cartographies de compétences et plans de formation ;
  • Capacité à accompagner les responsables rh au quotidien et à transférer des outils pratiques ;
  • Bonne connaissance des enjeux de gestion du changement ;
  • Excellente maîtrise du français écrit et oral.

Une expérience dans une société d’électricité, un service public ou une entreprise publique en réforme constituera un avantage.

Le dossier de manifestation d’intérêt devra comprendre :

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt ;
  • Un curriculum vitae détaillé et actualisé, daté et signé ;
  • Les copies des diplômes pertinents ;
  • Les références des missions similaires réalisées, en indiquant le client, le pays, la période, la durée de la mission, le rôle exact du consultant et les coordonnées de personnes de référence ;
  • Les attestations ou preuves d’expérience disponibles ;
  • Tout autre document permettant d’apprécier les qualifications et l’expérience du consultant.

Les consultants intéressés seront évalués sur la base de leurs qualifications générales, de leur expérience professionnelle pertinente, de leur expérience spécifique dans le domaine concerné, de leur capacité à assurer un accompagnement opérationnel quotidien, ainsi que de leur connaissance des entreprises publiques, sociétés d’électricité, services publics ou contextes similaires.

La sélection sera effectuée conformément aux dispositions du Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale applicable aux Emprunteurs dans le cadre du financement de projets d’investissement, selon la méthode de sélection de Consultant Individuel.

Les Termes de Référence détaillés peuvent être obtenus auprès de la Cellule d’Exécution de Projets de TchadElec à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous, pendant les heures ouvrables.

Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être déposées sous pli fermé ou transmises par courrier électronique au plus tard le 28 septembre 2028   à 15 h 30 mn, avec la mention :

« Manifestation d’intérêt pour le recrutement d’un expert senior résident en ressources humaines, organisation et conduite du changement chargé d’accompagner la Direction des Ressources Humaines de TchadElec »

Adresse de dépôt : Cellule d’Exécution de Projets de la Tchadienne d’Électricité (CEP TchadElec)

Adresse : Sis au Quartier Sabangali, derrière Le Lycée Technique Commercial de N’Djamena BP 286 TCHAD, Secrétariat de la Coordination Bâtiment A -Premier étage, Tel : (+235) 22 51 03 04 E-mail : pirect.cep@gmail.com

 

Les dossiers peuvent être déposés tous les jours ouvrables de 7h30 à 15h30, et le vendredi de 7h30 à 12h00.

Seuls les consultants sélectionnés à chaque étape du processus seront contactés aux adresses électroniques et numéros de téléphone indiqués dans leurs dossiers.

Le Directeur Général de TchadElec

 

SALEH BEN HALIKI

THE UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

                                                                                     MINISTRY OF WORKS

                                                                        TANZANIA NATIONAL ROADS AGENCY

                                                      TANZANIA TRANSPORT INTEGRATION PROJECT (TanTIP) – PROJECT ID: P165660

                                                                       REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

                                                        (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR ENGAGEMENT OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT FOR MONITORING OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE (GBV/SEA/SH) UNDER THE TANZANIA TRANSPORT INTEGRATED PROJECT (TANTIP) SUB PROJECTS; Tender; NoTR36/CCP/P165660/2026/2027/C/20

The Government of the United Republic of Tanzania has received a credit from the World Bank towards the cost of the Tanzania Transport Integration Project (TanTIP) which amongst others, comprises the upgrading of Iringa – Msembe (104 km) road and rehabilitation and improvement of Lake Manyara Airport. The Government, through Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS) intends to apply part of the credit proceeds to eligible payments under Contract for Consultancy Services for Engagement of Individual Consultant for Monitoring of Gender-Based Violence (GBV/SEA/SH) Under the Tanzania Transport Integrated Project (TanTIP) Sub Projects for which these Terms of Reference are issued.

One of the key social risks associated with large-scale transport infrastructure projects is Gender-Based Violence (GBV), including Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) and Sexual Harassment (SH). Such risks may arise due to labor influx, power imbalances, community-worker interactions, and inadequate awareness or enforcement of codes of conduct.

In line with national laws and policies of Tanzania, and applicable Environmental and Social Frameworks (including World Bank ESF where applicable), TanTIP has committed to the prevention, mitigation, and response to GBV risks. To ensure effective implementation of GBV risk mitigation measures, regular and systematic monitoring of GBV-related actions and outcomes is required. TanTIP is financed in part by the World Bank and is therefore subject to the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF). The ESF requires Borrowers to identify, assess, and manage environmental and social risks and impacts in a manner consistent with Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs).

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment are available on the following website www.tanroads.go.tz.
  2. The Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS) an Executive Agency of the Ministry of Works and Transport hereby invites Applicants to show their interest in delivering the Services described in the Terms of Reference.
  3. This Request for Expressions of Interest is open to: Individual Consultants.
  4. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Such information may include updated detailed CV duly signed and copies of academic, testimonial, and professional certificates. The interested Consultants should have the following qualifications and experience:
  1. Education
  1. He/She must have a university degree in Social Sciences, Anthropology, Gender, Social work, or related discipline. A Master's degree in the social sciences related to the above disciplines, or a related field is an added advantage.
  1. Professional experience
  1. He/She must have at least eight (8) years of cumulative experience in addressing social, resettlement, or gender issues with demonstration to practical experience applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, in particular ESS1, ESS2, ESS4 and ESS10, and the Bank's Good Practice Note on addressing SEA/SH in investment project financing involving major civil works;
  2. He/She must have at least five (5) years of demonstrated SEA/SH-specific experience on three (3) infrastructure projects under World Bank financed involving; supervising GBV prevention and response activities, conducting awareness campaigns on women's rights, gender equality, GBV, and/or reproductive health, considered an asset; and
  3. He/She must be computer literate with competency in word processing, spreadsheets, and slideshow/PowerPoint program, Internet and Intranet.
  1. Regional experience and Language and requirements
  1. He/she must have at least three (3) years working experience in developing countries; and
  2. He/she must be proficient in both written and spoken English and Swahili Languages.
  1. Government employees under Short-terms or Permanent Contract need not apply, as they are not eligible to participate in the selection process. Expressions of Interest from government employees will be eliminated from the selection process.
  2. The attention of interested individual consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seven Edition, September, 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  3. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seven Edition September, 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”) and Public Procurement Act No. 10 of 2023 and Public Procurement Regulations GN No. 518 of 2024 on “procedures for selection and employment of consultants.
  4. Expressions of Interest must be submitted through National e-Procurement System of Tanzania (NeST) (www.nest.go.tz) on or before 25th September, 2026 at 10:00 Hours East African Time. The Client shall not be held liable for any delays due to system failure beyond its control. Even though the system will attempt to notify the Consultants of any updates, the Client shall not be liable for any information not received by the bidder. It is the Consultants’ responsibility to verify the website for the latest information related to this selection process. Expression of Interests will be opened promptly thereafter through NeST.
  5. Any request for clarification with regard to this assignment shall be addressed through NeST not less than five (5) days before submission deadline. The Employer shall respond to clarifications received within three (3) working days from the date of receipt of the query. Expression of Interest not received through NeST shall not be evaluated irrespective of the circumstances
  6. Interested Applicants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours: 08:30 - 16:30 local time on Mondays to Fridays inclusive except on Public Holidays.

Rehabilitation of boreholes FH05 & FH06 – Calumue in Lubango

COMPETITION NO: 196W3/UCP/26

The Government of the Republic of Angola (GOA) has received funding from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the French Development Agency (AFD) to cover the costs of the Second Institutional Development Project for the Water Sector (PDISA 2) and intends to apply part of the resources to payments under the contract for the Rehabilitation of Boreholes FH05 and FH06 – CALUMUE in Lubango.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

NIGERIA

DISTRIBUTION SECTOR RECOVERY PROGRAM (DISREP)

CREDIT NO: 9206-NG

PROJECT ID No. P172891

Date: 14th September, 2026

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: Consultancy Services to Guide DisCos Submission of End-to-End Feeder Upgrade Project for DISREP

REFERENCE NO.: DREP-CQS-7A, 8A, 9A & 10A

The Federal Government of Nigeria has applied for financing from the World Bank through the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Distribution Sector Recovery Program (DISREP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. This assignment is to support DisCos in the preparation of technically sound, financially viable end-to-end feeder upgrade project submissions under DISREP. Qualified firms shall be invited to bid for services specified under. Firms may bid for all the lots, but no firm can win more than one lot.

The assignment is divided into the following lots;

  • Lot 1: Abuja, Kaduna and Kano
  • Lot 2: Jos and Yola
  • Lot 3: Eko, Ibadan and Ikeja
  • Lot 4: Benin, Enigu and Port Harcourt

The consulting services (“the Services”) include:

  • Feeder portfolio review and ranking based on Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA)
  • Standardized Technical Specifications and Bill of Engineering Measurement and Evaluation (BEME)
  • Costing and Benchmarking

The approximate effort level for the assignment is Four (4) Calendar months.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be accessed at TCN website.

The Transmission Company of Nigeria-Project Management Unit (TCN-PMU) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. General Experience: The Firm’s general experience and overall competence, including the relevance of the firm’s area of core business to the assignment envisaged;
  2. Relevant Assignment Experience: Firm’s experience implementing loss reduction and performance improvement projects for at least one Nigerian power distribution company.
  3. Technical and Institutional Capacity: Firm’s experience developing standardized frameworks, templates and toolkits for project preparation and review.
  4. Managerial Capacity: Firm’s experience managing large multi-year consulting assignments with multiple stakeholders.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th Edition (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultants Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 0900 to 1700 hours].

CONTRATAÇÃO DE CONSULTOR PARA ANÁLISE DE DADOS DO INQUÉRITO ANUAL ÀS EMPRESAS (IAE), NO ÂMBITO DA MELHORIA DAS CONTAS NACIONAIS

  1. O Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE) recebeu uma subvenção da Associação Internacional de Desenvolvimento (AID), instituição do Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto Regional de Estatísticas da SADC (PRESADC), e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para a contratação de um(a) Consultor(a) Individual – Especialista em Análise de Dados do Inquérito Anual às Empresas (IAE).
  2. Os serviços de consultoria (“Serviços”) visam analisar a coerência e consistência das variáveis captadas pelo IAE e as suas implicações para as Contas Nacionais, nomeadamente para o Produto Interno Bruto (PIB), reforçando a capacidade técnica do INE em análise e tratamento de dados empresariais, em alinhamento com o Sistema de Contas Nacionais (SCN 2008). Mais detalhes sobre os serviços e as responsabilidades da consultoria encontram-se nos Termos de Referência (TdR).
  3. Os requisitos de qualificação incluem: formação académica ao nível de Licenciatura, Mestrado ou Doutoramento em Contabilidade e Auditoria, Gestão de Empresas, Economia, Estatística, Administração de Empresas ou áreas afins; experiência comprovada no Fecho de Contas de Empresas (mínimo de 5 anos); familiaridade com o uso de estatísticas oficiais; domínio de ferramentas como Primavera, PHC ou similar, e Stata, EViews, R ou SPSS; capacidade comprovada de redacção técnica e apresentação de resultados a públicos institucionais; e experiência em transferência de conhecimentos e capacitação técnica.
  4. O Contrato terá duração de 7 (sete) semanas, a partir da data de celebração do contrato.
  5. Os(as) candidatos(as) interessados(as) e com o perfil requerido deverão submeter os seguintes documentos: Carta de Manifestação de Interesse, Curriculum Vitae, em língua portuguesa, cópias dos diplomas ou certificados de habilitações académicas, lista de publicações e/ou relatórios técnicos relevantes (quando aplicável), e indicação de três (3) referências profissionais que poderão ser contactadas no processo de avaliação.
  6. As candidaturas deverão ser entregues até às 15:00 horas do dia 29 de Setembro de 2026 no endereço Instituto Nacional de Estatística – Avenida 24 de Julho nº1989, Piso 09- Sala 0901, Cidade de Maputo. Email: presadc.concursos@gmail.com
  7. O consultor será seleccionado de acordo com os procedimentos do Banco Mundial definidos no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projectos de Investimento, 6.ª edição, Fevereiro de 2025, particularmente os parágrafos 7.36 – 7.37 sobre Selecção de Consultores Individuais. Os interessados devem prestar particular atenção na Secção III, parágrafos 3.15 a 3.17 do mesmo Regulamento, política sobre conflito de interesse.
  8. Os Termos de Referência e outros detalhes sobre a consultoria poderão ser obtidos no endereço acima e também estão disponíveis em www.ine.gov.mz/concursos. Intitulé de la Mission : AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR LA MISE EN PLACE D’UN SYSTEME DE MANAGEMENT DE LA QUALITE ET ACCOMPAGNEMENT A LA CERTIFICATION ISO 9001 : 2015.

N° de référence : BJ-WURI - BENIN-565335-CS-CQS du…………………

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du BENIN a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet d’identification unique pour l’intégration et l’inclusion en Afrique de l’Ouest (WURI) et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de consultant. 
  2. La mission du consultant (cabinet) consistera à mettre en place un Système de Management de la Qualité conforme à la norme ISO 9001:2015, couvrant l’ensemble des activités de l’ANIP, et à accompagner l’Agence jusqu’à l’obtention effective de la certification.

De façon spécifique, il s’agira de :

  • Réaliser un diagnostic complet de l’existant au regard des exigences de la norme ISO 9001 :2015 ;
  • Cartographier l’ensemble des processus métiers, supports et de pilotage de l’ANIP ;
  • Identifier les dysfonctionnements, les gaspillages (muda), les redondances et les activités sans valeur ajoutée ;
  • Proposer des actions de simplification, de standardisation et d'optimisation des processus avant leur formalisation dans le Système de Management de la Qualité ;
  • Mettre en place un Système de Management de la Qualité institutionnel ;
  • Formaliser la politique qualité de l’ANIP ;
  • Définir les objectifs qualité et les indicateurs de performance associés ;
  • Concevoir un système documentaire reflétant des processus optimisés et non la simple reproduction des pratiques existantes et conformes aux exigences de la norme ;
  • Renforcer le dispositif de gestion des risques et opportunités ;
  • Intégrer les principes d’amélioration continue dans les processus de l’Agence ;
  • Renforcer l’orientation usager et la culture qualité à tous les niveaux ;
  • Former les acteurs internes aux exigences de la norme ;
  • Former un pool d’auditeurs internes qualité ;
  • Réaliser les audits qualité internes préparatoires ;
  • Accompagner l’ANIP lors de l’audit de certification ;
  • Assister l’Agence dans le traitement des éventuelles non-conformités jusqu’à l’obtention du certificat ISO 9001 :2015.
  1. La durée de réalisation de la mission sera de douze (12) mois à partir de la date de notification de service, y compris les délais de validation et de livraison du rapport final.
  2. Le Coordonnateur National du Projet WURI BENIN, représentant l’Autorité Contractante, par la présente sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt, invite les consultants (cabinets) admissibles à présenter leur candidature pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus.
  3. A ce titre, les agences intéressées doivent fournir les informations indiquant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour exécuter les services. Le dossier de candidature comprendra :
  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt précisant la mission ;
  • Le registre de commerce ou tout autre document similaire pouvant prouver les années d’exercices

et domaines d’activité ;

  • Les références techniques accompagnées des preuves (attestation de bonne fin d’exécution ou procès-verbaux de réceptions).
  1. Le cabinet sera sélectionné par la méthode de « Sélection fondée sur les Qualifications de Consultant (QC) » décrite au paragraphe 7.11 du Règlement sur la passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale en date de septembre 2025. A l’issue de l’évaluation des références, le consultant ayant présenté le meilleur niveau de qualification et d’expériences en rapport avec la mission, sera invité à soumettre des propositions technique et financière puis à négocier le contrat.
  2. L’attention des agences intéressées est attirée sur les paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du Règlement sur la passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale, qui décrivent la politique de la Banque en matière de conflits d’intérêts.

Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements Project (VARS)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

Individual Selection of Consultant

Assignment Title:

ESMASP Project Officer

Duty Station:

PMU, Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources,

Port Vila, Vanuatu

Date of Publication:

15th September 2026

Deadline for submission:

29th September 2026 at time: 1400 Hours.

Reference Number:

VU-MLNR-568283-CS-INDV

1. BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT:

The Elol Etas Subdivision Marketing, Allocation and Sale Process (ESMASP) is the government-led process for the transparent marketing, allocation, and sale of residential lots in the Elol Etas (Etas Gardens) Subdivision. It is implemented by the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources (MoLNR), with operational and administrative support from the Project Management Unit (PMU) of the Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements (VARS) Project, financed by the World Bank. The ESMASP Office operates visibly as a MoLNR function, reinforcing that the subdivision is a Government of Vanuatu-led project.

The ESMASP is delivered by a three-person core implementation team the ESMASP Manager, an ESMASP Project Officer and an ESMASP Applications Officer supported by the VARS PMU and MoLNR and complemented by a defined set of allied in-house resources drawn from the PMU and the Ministry: nominated outreach leads, a pool of PMU interns providing outreach and intake support, in-house database, web-administration and IT support staff, and PMU vehicles. Public awareness, marketing and community engagement are delivered in-house by this team. Applications are received through a single, controlled channel in person at the ESMASP Office, where they are entered directly into the application system by ESMASP staff. Given anticipated oversubscription in the order of 20:1, the integrity of the selection process is the single most important deliverable of the ESMASP, and all positions carry explicit transparency, conflict-of-interest, and documentation obligations.

 The ESMASP Project Officer is responsible for the operational delivery of public awareness, marketing, and community engagement within the team, under the ESMASP Manager's direction. The role is centred on executing the outreach campaign directly, in line with the calendar, messaging and strategy approved by the ESMASP Manager - working with the allied outreach leads nominated from MoLNR and the PMU, the intern pool, settlement contact points and the Shefa Provincial Council.

2. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

To operationally deliver, under the ESMASP Manager's approved campaign strategy the community-facing public awareness and marketing campaign for the ESMASP including the settlement outreach calendar, session facilitation with allied outreach leads, approved Bislama messaging, priority-group outreach, support to central public events and media products, and workshop logistics and to operate the ESMASP grievance intake function to the standards of Appendix 8, so that outreach is accurate, accessible, consistent and well-documented, eligible households are informed and directed to the ESMASP Office to apply, and complaints are received, logged and acknowledged reliably across all channels.

4. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

Qualifications and Experience

  • Required: A diploma or bachelor's degree in a relevant field community development, social science, communications, public administration, project management or similar from a recognised institution; or a secondary school certificate (Year 12/13) combined with at least three to four years of relevant work experience in community engagement, public awareness campaigns, outreach coordination or project support.
  • Desirable: A bachelor's degree in the fields above; certificate-level training in project management, monitoring and evaluation, communications, or grievance redress/safeguards (including familiarity with World Bank Environmental and Social Framework requirements); or training in facilitation or community mobilisation.

Essential

  • Excellent Bislama plain-language communication, drafting, public speaking and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to present government messaging accurately and confidently to large and diverse community audiences.
  • Demonstrated experience planning and delivering community outreach, awareness, or information campaigns in Greater Port Vila or Shefa Province settlements, including coordination with local authorities and community leaders.
  • Demonstrated coordination and logistics capability, including organising community events or workshops (venues, transport, scheduling, equipment, monitoring) and coordinating the inputs of staff who are not under the Officer's direct line management.
  • Aptitude for grievance handling: sound judgement, impartiality, discretion, and accurate record-keeping in receiving and logging complaints.
  • Strong written reporting skills in English, including preparation of statistics, dashboards, or summary reports.
  • Competence in the Microsoft Office suite, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint, and other relevant programs for preparing materials, statistics, dashboards, and reports.
  • Ability to work with government, civil society, and community stakeholders, including local authorities in Greater Port Vila and Shefa Province, and with priority groups including women-headed households and persons with disabilities.
  • Integrity and willingness to sign and comply with the ESMASP Conflict-of-Interest Declaration, the outreach guardrails and documentation disciplines.

Desirable

  • Experience supporting donor-financed projects (e.g., World Bank), community engagement programmes, or grievance redress mechanisms.
  • Familiarity with the Greater Port Vila settlement context, warden and area-administrator structures, and provincial coordination arrangements.
  • Experience supervising or coordinating volunteers, interns, or junior staff in field settings.
  • A valid driver's licence.

5. REPORTING:

The Project Officer reports to the ESMASP Manager, who leads the ESMASP implementation team within the VARS PMU and owns the campaign plan and approved messaging. The Officer works alongside the ESMASP Applications Officer; coordinates the rostered inputs of the allied outreach leads; supervises interns assigned to session logistics; coordinates with settlement contact points and the Shefa Provincial Council; and draws on VARS PMU operational and administrative support, including vehicles and surge support during peak periods. The Officer has no authority to vary the scope or time limits agreed for allied staff; conflicts of priority are referred to the ESMASP Manager. The ESMASP Manager retains strategic ownership of the marketing and communications strategy, the campaign budget, and Project Steering Committee/World Bank liaison on marketing and outreach matters; the Project Officer delivers approved activities operationally in the community and has no authority to vary campaign strategy, budget allocations or approved messaging without the ESMASP Manager's prior approval.

6. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT:

Approximately fifteen (15) months (full sales and marketing process), full-time.

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges, and foster collaboration and cooperation in the pursuit of shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.  The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

Selection Method

Competitive Selection of an independent individual consultant, subject to procurement plan adjustment, justification, conflict-of-interest review, and World Bank no-objection requirements where applicable.

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address shared issues and support cooperation. PIF works through regional governance, shared resources and policy alignment to support economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises eighteen members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.

Participating Countries

The Pacific Island Countries participating in the regional project comprise Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu. This assignment provides country-specific support to the Republic of the Marshall Islands under the regional project.

Overall Project Objective

The Project Development Objective is to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries.

Project Length

August 2024 to September 30, 2030

Project Background

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) for the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project. The project supports participating Pacific Island Countries (PICs) to maintain continuous access to correspondent banking services, and to address underlying payment, regulatory and financial integrity constraints that contribute to de-risking in the region.

PICs are exposed to the withdrawal of correspondent banking relationships (CBRs) that underpin international trade, tourism, remittances, development finance, disaster relief, and humanitarian financial flows. The project provides a short-term CBR safety net while supporting the enabling environment and regional harmonization needed for a medium-term sustainable solution.

Component 2 of the project, Enabling Environment and Regulatory Harmonization, includes support for Payment System Oversight and Regulation. The relevant activity areas include payment systems regulatory harmonization, oversight of national payment systems, and collection of remittance and gender-disaggregated data on usage of financial services. Component 2 also supports payment systems strengthening, CBR Roadmap implementation, the CBR Resilience Index, and the feasibility work for the Pacific Payment Mechanism (PPM), which aims to aggregate payment flows and improve economies of scale.

The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is in the early phase of operationalizing the MAMI. In June 2026, the Governor of MAMI requested support for an advisor to assist with implementation of the Authority's operationalization strategy, including review and tailoring of recommendations from the IMF Monetary and Capital Markets Department technical assistance report, Operationalizing A New Monetary Authority. The request also highlighted the need to establish the national payment system in alignment with the World Bank CBR Strengthening Project's payment system harmonization roadmap.

The IMF report identifies several payment-related priorities for MAMI. These include the development of a National Payments Strategy (NPS), the establishment of payment operations and payment oversight functions, the creation of a stakeholder consultation mechanism and National Payment Council, the preparation of payment operations and oversight procedures, and the design of an Integrated Payment and Clearing System (IPCS) that can combine ACH, RTGS and instant payment functionality in a phased manner. The report also notes that RMI currently has no centralized payment system, that payment services are dominated by checks, that there is no e-money provider, and that electronic payments remain limited outside selected card and POS use cases.

This assignment is designed as payment systems technical assistance under the CBR Project’s Technical Assistance component. It is framed around the project's Payment System Oversight and Regulation activities and is expected to support MAMI in converting payment-related IMF recommendations into a practical work plan, institutional arrangements, operating procedures, oversight tools, stakeholder coordination mechanisms, and capacity building outputs.

Objective of the Position

The main objective of the Payments System Advisor to MAMI is to provide technical advisory support to MAMI for the establishment of a safe, efficient, inclusive and scalable national payments system and payment system oversight function, aligned with the CBR Project, the CBR Roadmap, regional payment system harmonization work, and the emerging design of the PPM.

The Advisor will review the payment-related findings and recommendations in the IMF MCM report and assist MAMI to translate the relevant payment system recommendations into a practical implementation approach for RMI. This will include helping MAMI distinguish payment system actions from broader central banking, governance, accounting, audit, reserve management, HR, communications and corporate services matters, and sequencing the payment system actions in line with MAMI’s institutional capacity, staffing plans and expected operational priorities.

In doing so, the Advisor will consider the small scale of the RMI financial sector, the dominance of checks, limited electronic payment usage, geographic dispersion, government payment needs, remittance costs, digital financial-service developments, and MAMI’s current staffing and institutional capacity.

Scope of Services

The selected Payments System Advisor will provide country-level, time-based technical implementation support for RMI on payment system matters. The work will be coordinated with the PIFS PMU, the PIFS Payment Systems Specialist, the World Bank payments team, IMF MCM and other technical assistance providers as relevant. The Advisor will carry out the following tasks, with timing and level of effort agreed through the 12-month implementation work plan and periodic work planning discussions:

i. Inception, work planning and IMF recommendation mapping

  • Review the IMF MCM report, MAMI Act and related institutional materials, the CBR Project Operations Manual, the CBR Roadmap, available PPM materials, and other relevant documents provided by MAMI, PIFS or the World Bank.
  • Prepare an inception report that identifies the payment-related recommendations requiring action by MAMI and separates them from broader central banking, governance, accounting, audit, reserve management, HR, communications, and corporate services matters.
  • Develop a 12-month implementation roadmap for the establishment of MAMI’s national payments function, with milestones, dependencies, counterpart responsibilities, expected outputs, sequencing assumptions, and coordination points with the World Bank, IMF and PIFS. The roadmap should be aligned with MAMI’s expected recruitment of the Banking Operations Department Executive Manager and Payment Systems Operations Manager, anticipated around December 2026 to January 2027, so that the Advisor’s support helps prepare for, onboard, and transition responsibilities to these key MAMI counterparts.
  • Prepare and periodically update the Advisor’s own assignment work plan, aligned with the 12-month MAMI implementation roadmap, counterpart availability, agreed priorities, in-country inputs, and monthly or quarterly work planning discussions with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank.
  • Tailor payment system recommendations to the RMI context, including market size, transaction volumes, institutional capacity, staffing constraints, remittance corridors, public sector payment needs, and affordability for banks and end users.

ii. Establishment of MAMI's national payments function

  • Advise MAMI on the operational setup, sequencing, staffing profile and accountabilities for its national payments function, including the Payment Operations Division (POD) and Payment Oversight and Policy Division (OVD) recommended by the IMF report.
  • Provide advice on the separation of payment system operations and payment system oversight responsibilities within MAMI’s payments mandate, including reporting lines, decision processes, internal coordination arrangements, and safeguards to manage potential conflicts between operational and oversight functions.
  • Prepare a short skills and capacity building plan for MAMI staff involved in payment operations, payment oversight, payment      collection, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Assist MAMI to define working procedures and decision flows for its payment system operational and oversight functions, including issue escalation, internal reporting, consultation with supervised or participating institutions, coordination with IT, risk, legal and supervision functions, and referral of matters requiring specialist technical or legal input.

 

iii. National Payments Strategy

  • Support MAMI to develop a National Payments Strategy that sets out a phased modernization agenda for RMI’s national payment system, aligned with the National Financial Inclusion Strategy and coordinated with related work under the CBR Project, regional payment system harmonization agenda, and emerging PPM design.
  • Prepare or support a baseline diagnostic covering domestic and cross-border payment flows, CBRs, government payments, remittances, check usage, card and POS usage, payment access, digital infrastructure, consumer needs, and data gaps.
  • Identify practical measures to increase use of electronic payments, reduce reliance on checks and cash where appropriate, improve government payment flows, support remittance cost reduction, and expand access to payment services for businesses, households and the public sector.
  • Support stakeholder consultations on the NPS, including preparation of consultation materials, meeting notes, issue logs and revisions to the strategy based on feedback received.

iv. Payment infrastructure and IPCS implementation support

  • Advise MAMI on a fit-for-purpose and phased approach to payment infrastructure modernization, including the IMF recommendation for an Integrated Payment and Clearing System combining ACH, RTGS and instant payment functionality.
  • Advise MAMI on the preparation, review and sequencing of high-level business requirements and implementation planning for any future IPCS, including initial electronic clearing for wire transfers and checks, check truncation, settlement arrangements, participant onboarding, service levels, operating schedules and support arrangements. The Advisor will help MAMI frame the requirements and coordinate specialist inputs but will not be responsible for preparing detailed technical specifications or system design documents unless separately agreed with PIFS, MAMI and the World Bank.
  • Assess the sequencing of ACH, RTGS and instant payment functionality based on RMI transaction volumes, costs, operational readiness, risk profile and user needs.
  • Advise MAMI on the issues that should be considered when planning future payment infrastructure, including payment messaging, straight-through processing, ISO 20022 readiness, data security, operational resilience, business continuity, disaster recovery, liquidity risk, settlement risk and participant default arrangements. Where detailed technical design is required, the Advisor will help MAMI identify the issues, review options, and coordinate inputs from specialist payment infrastructure, IT, cybersecurity or World Bank experts.
  • Provide payment system technical inputs to procurement documents, concept notes or options papers for the IPCS, as requested by MAMI and the PMU, subject to World Bank procurement rules and conflict-of-interest restrictions.

v. Payment system oversight, data and risk-based supervision

  • Support MAMI to define a payment system oversight framework covering objectives, scope, standards, tools, reporting, escalation, corrective actions and coordination with other MAMI functions.
  • Advise MAMI on the scope, structure and phased development of oversight procedures for risk-based monitoring of payment systems and payment service providers, including e-money and non-bank PSPs where relevant. The Advisor may prepare outlines, review drafts and support capacity building, but detailed supervisory manuals, examination procedures or legal instruments should be developed with appropriate specialist and legal input as required.
  • Advise MAMI on the payment data and indicators that should be collected for oversight and policy purposes, including payment volumes and values, failed transactions, settlement incidents, fraud, customer complaints, operational incidents, participation, concentration, liquidity risk, credit risk and operational risk. The Advisor may support the development or review of reporting templates in coordination with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank, but the final templates should be agreed by MAMI and aligned with wider project data requirements.
  • Provide technical inputs to and reviews of payment-related regulations, rules, circulars or supervisory guidance as requested, including on electronic payments, PSPs, system participation and operational risk. This role does not include drafting primary payment system legislation or formal legal opinions.
  • Align oversight tools with relevant international standards and guidance, including the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures, ISO 20022, risk-based supervision practices, consumer protection principles and cyber-resilience expectations applicable to payment systems.
  • Review USDM1-related payment system implications, considering existing RMI AML laws and regulations and MAMI’s current regulatory treatment of USDM1, and advise on whether any payment system oversight, interoperability, reporting, operational risk, consumer safeguard or AML/CFT coordination measures should be reflected in MAMI’s national payment system framework. The Advisor will not provide advice on the sovereign debt, securities law, issuance, redemption, collateral, reserve management or investment aspects of USDM1 except where these issues directly affect payment system oversight or integration.

vi. Coordination, consultation and National Payment Council support

  • Assist MAMI to establish a consultation mechanism with banks, government agencies, SOEs, card schemes, telecom operators, payment service providers, major users and other stakeholders involved in payments modernization.
  • Prepare draft Terms of Reference, membership options, work program and first-year agenda for a National Payment Council or equivalent advisory body.
  • Support MAMI in coordinating with the Ministry of Finance on payment-related services, including government payment flows, account information, reporting expectations, service levels, and inputs to any payment-related SLA or MOU arrangements.
  • Prepare stakeholder maps, consultation papers, meeting agendas, minutes and action trackers to support implementation of the national payments work plan.

vii. Alignment with the CBR Project and regional work

  • Coordinate closely with the PIFS PMU, PIFS Payment Systems Specialist and World Bank payments team to align RMI support with the CBR Project's Component 2 work program.
  • Support RMI inputs into CBR data collection, the CBR Resilience Index and the PPM feasibility and design process, including payment flow data, remittance information, CBR information and stakeholder feedback.
  • Assist MAMI to collect and improve relevant remittance and gender-disaggregated data on the usage of financial services, where feasible and agreed with the PMU and World Bank.
  • Identify areas where RMI can participate in regional harmonization work, including PSP licensing, QR code standards, open banking/open finance, cross-border interoperability and common principles for cross-border data sharing.
  • Coordinate with IMF MCM and other technical assistance providers, through MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank as appropriate, to reduce duplication, sequence inputs, and keep the assignment focused on payment system matters within the agreed CBR Project scope. Where feasible, the Advisor may support periodic coordination discussions, including around the Annual Meetings or Spring Meetings, if requested by MAMI, PIFS or the World Bank.

viii. Capacity building and knowledge transfer

  • Identify MAMI staff training needs, develop a multi-year training plan, and identify opportunities for training and knowledge transfer aligned with MAMI’s payment system mandate, staffing plan and future development priorities.
  • Prepare training materials, practical templates and work aids that MAMI staff can continue to use after the assignment.
  • Identify peer learning opportunities with regional central banks or payment system operators, including short technical exchanges or virtual clinics where appropriate.
  • Provide mentoring to assigned MAMI counterparts and support handover of tools, procedures and work plans before the end of the assignment.

Scope Exclusions

The assignment is limited to payment systems technical assistance and payment-related operationalization of MAMI. The Advisor will not draft the Payment Systems Act, amendments to the Monetary Authority Act, primary legislation, or formal legal opinions.

The Advisor will not provide general central bank advisory services on reserve management, fiscal agency, accounting, audit, human resources, communications, procurement, general governance, or corporate services except where those topics directly affect payment system operations, payment oversight, payment infrastructure or payment-related stakeholder coordination.

Time-Based Reporting Obligations and Expected Outputs

This assignment will be contracted on a time-based basis. Payments will be linked to approved timesheets, agreed input days, and eligible reimbursable expenses, not to a fixed-price deliverables schedule. The outputs listed below are expected working products and reporting instruments for managing the assignment, tracking progress, supporting quality review, and documenting knowledge transfer.

The Advisor will prepare and update working products in line with the agreed work plan and counterpart needs. These may include the inception note and 12-month payments work plan, IMF recommendation mapping, National Payments Strategy materials, payment function setup notes, National Payment Council materials, payment operations and oversight procedures, data templates, IPCS options and requirements notes, training materials, mission notes and handover materials.

Because the role is advisory and embedded with MAMI for a substantial part of the assignment, outputs may be revised or reprioritized during implementation with agreement from MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank. The Advisor will document changes through monthly activity notes, quarterly progress notes and the action tracker.

Reporting Obligations

The Payments System Advisor will work closely with MAMI on a day-to-day technical basis and will report administratively to the Project Coordinator within the PIFS PMU. Technical priorities, work planning, and expected outputs will be agreed with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank payments team. The Advisor will also coordinate with the PIFS Payment Systems Specialist and the RMI Country Coordinator as relevant.

The Advisor will submit monthly timesheets and short monthly activity notes to the PIFS PMU, with confirmation from MAMI of the main activities undertaken. The monthly activity note should summarize days worked, in-country and remote inputs, meetings held, outputs prepared, issues requiring decision, and planned activities for the following month. Technical outputs will be shared with MAMI and PIFS, and PIFS will share them with the World Bank for review or no-objection where required under the project arrangements.

The Advisor will maintain a short action tracker covering agreed activities, responsible counterparts, due dates, risks, dependencies and decisions required. The tracker will be updated at least monthly, and more frequently if requested by the PMU or MAMI. The Advisor will also provide quarterly progress notes against the 12-month payments work plan and a final completion and handover note at the end of the assignment.

Institutional Arrangements

This is a time-based individual consultant assignment contracted by PIFS through the PMU under the Pacific Strengthening CBR Project. The assignment will be undertaken for the benefit of MAMI as the primary country counterpart. The procurement approach is competitive selection of an independent individual consultant, subject to the approved procurement plan, applicable PIFS procurement procedures, conflict-of-interest review, and World Bank review or no-objection requirements where applicable.

The Advisor is expected to spend significant time in Majuro during the assignment, estimated at 50-60 percent of total input days, especially during inception, stakeholder consultations, NPS preparation, payment function setup, capacity building and infrastructure planning. Remote work may be used for document preparation, virtual meetings, training, follow-up and coordination with PIFS and the World Bank.

Office space and access to meeting facilities may be provided by MAMI for in-country inputs and by PIFS for inputs in Suva, subject to availability. The Advisor will be responsible for maintaining secure records of documents, correspondence and data received during the assignment and for complying with all confidentiality requirements.

The Advisor's services will be subject to periodic performance review based on the performance indicators below. Performance review will inform continuation, extension, revision or termination of the assignment, subject to contract terms and World Bank requirements.

 

Performance Indicators

The following performance indicators will be used for contract management and performance assessment. They are intended to measure timely input, quality of advisory support, documented outputs, counterpart engagement and knowledge transfer under a time-based contract:

  • Monthly timesheets are submitted on time and accurately distinguish between in country and remote input days.
  • Monthly activity notes are submitted on time and summarize work undertaken, meetings held, issues requiring decision, risks, planned next steps and counterpart engagement.
  • The Advisor maintains and updates an action tracker covering agreed activities, responsible counterparts, deadlines, dependencies and pending decisions.
  • A 12-month implementation roadmap for MAMI’s national payments function is prepared, discussed with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank, and updated as required during implementation.
  • The Advisor’s own assignment work plan is maintained and aligned with the 12-month MAMI implementation roadmap, MAMI counterpart availability and agreed priorities.
  • Payment-related IMF MCM recommendations are mapped and separated from broader central banking, governance, accounting, audit, reserve management, HR, communications and corporate services matters.
  • MAMI receives documented advice, meeting notes or working materials on the setup of payment operations and payment oversight responsibilities, including staffing, reporting lines, procedures and capacity needs.
  • MAMI is supported in preparing or refining National Payments Strategy materials, consultation inputs and implementation roadmap elements.
  • Payment infrastructure advice is documented through advisory notes, review comments or options papers that support a phased and fit-for-purpose approach to any future IPCS, without requiring the Advisor to develop systems or detailed technical specifications.
  • Payment system oversight and data work is documented through advisory notes, outlines, review comments, reporting needs, draft structures or training materials, with specialist technical or legal work referred to appropriate experts where required.
  • Stakeholder engagement is documented through meeting notes, action trackers, consultation materials or National Payment Council support materials.
  • Capacity building activities are documented through training materials, attendance records, mentoring notes or handover materials.
  • Quarterly progress notes are submitted against the agreed work plan and discussed with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank.
  • A final completion and handover note is submitted at the end of the assignment, summarizing work undertaken, outputs prepared, remaining actions, open risks and recommended next steps.
  • The Advisor maintains professional, objective and impartial advice, avoids conflicts of interest, records input days accurately, and complies with PIFS and World Bank rules on confidentiality, anti-corruption and fraud prevention.

Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

The Payments System Advisor shall comply with PIFS and World Bank policies and rules on anti-corruption, prevention of fraudulent practices, conflict of interest and confidentiality. The Advisor shall maintain confidentiality over all sensitive information obtained during the assignment and shall not publish or disclose any findings, data, reports or recommendations without prior written consent from PIFS and MAMI, and World Bank clearance where required.

Any draft reports and other documents produced by the Advisor will be discussed with and cleared by PIFS, MAMI and the World Bank before final issue. A non-disclosure agreement may be signed between PIFS, MAMI and the selected consultant and attached to the contract.

The Advisor must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest before contract signature and throughout the assignment. The Advisor shall not participate in downstream procurement activities where such participation would create a conflict of interest under the World Bank Procurement Regulations or the Project Operations Manual.

Evaluation Requirements

Mandatory Criteria

This section details the basis upon which selection of the successful candidate will be based.

These criteria must be met to be considered for this contract.

REGIONAL ACCESS TO ELECTRICITY AND INTEGRATION OF SUSTAINABLE ENERGY

RAISE - Regional Access Increase and Sustainable Energy (P515184)
ECOWAS - THE GAMBIA - TOGO

Request for Expression of Interest - REOI 

Financing: World Bank / IDA

Countries: The Gambia and Togo

Name of Project: RAISE - Regional Access Increase and Sustainable Energy (P515184)

Assignment Title: Owner's engineering services for works supervision in The Gambia and in Togo

Reference No.: NG-ECOWAS-DEM-568125-CS-QCBS

The Republics of The Gambia and Togo have received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Access Increase and Sustainable Energy Project (RAISE Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include works supervision in The Gambia and in Togo as briefly summarized:

  • Preparation and Mobilization Phase;
  • Technical Review and Approval of Execution Documents;
  • Works Supervision and Quality Control;
  • Contract Administration;
  • Contract Management System;
  • Environmental, Social, Health and Safety Monitoring;
  • Testing, Energization, Commissioning and Acceptance;
  • Defects Liability Period and Final Acceptance;

The period from mobilization through construction, testing, commissioning and provisional acceptance shall not exceed eighteen (18) months in either The Gambia or Togo. A separate defects liability monitoring period of up to twelve (12) months shall follow provisional acceptance for each relevant works contract. The indicative maximum duration is therefore thirty (30) months for each country contract.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/za97oz4il597a8jl1zx3o/AETqwBMWx01U9G5exEcKE0A?rlkey=m2h9dcc9q2edb5988zr0tqowl&st=mqw79del&dl=0

The ECOWAS Commission in Abuja, on behalf of the countries of The Gambia and Togo now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  • The consultant shall be a legally constituted and independent engineering consulting firm, or joint venture of consulting firms, specializing in electrical power infrastructure, with substantial experience in the design review, construction supervision, contract administration, testing and commissioning of medium- and low-voltage electricity distribution systems and associated substations;
  • At least 15 years of general experience in engineering consulting services for electricity, energy or comparable infrastructure projects, withproven ability to mobilize and manage large multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed supervision teams;
  • At least three similar assignments involving design review and construction supervision of MV/LV distribution networks.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained at the address below from Monday to Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. UT:

E-mail :ecowas-reap@ecowas.int ; with copy to lkouassi@ecowas.int; banwone@ecowas.int; gouoba@ecowas.int 

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in both French and English languages, in a written form by September 30, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. to the following address: ecowas-reap@ecowas.int ; with copy to  lkouassi@ecowas.int ; banwone@ecowas.int ; gouoba@ecowas.int

Located at Former Ecowas Commission, 101, Yakubu Gowon Crescent, Asokoro,  Abuja, Nigeria; 2nd Floor, Door 204A.

CEDEAO - GAMBIE - TOGO

Intitulé de la mission : Mission d'ingénieur-conseil pour la supervision des travaux d'électrification en Gambie et au Togo

Référence : NG-ECOWAS-DEM-568125-CS-QCBS

Les Républiques de Gambie et du Togo ont reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet d'accroissement de l'accès régional et d'énergie durable (Projet RAISE) et ont l'intention d'utiliser une partie de ce financement pour des services de consultants.

Les services de consultants (« les Services ») comprennent la supervision de travaux en Gambie et au Togo, comme résumé ci-après :

  • Phase de préparation et de mobilisation ;
  • Revue technique et approbation des documents d'exécution ;
  • Supervision des travaux et contrôle de la qualité ;
  • Administration des contrats ;
  • Système de gestion des contrats ;
  • Suivi environnemental, social, sanitaire et sécuritaire ;
  • Essais, mise sous tension, mise en service et réception ;
  • Période de garantie et réception définitive ;

La période allant de la mobilisation jusqu'à la construction, aux essais, à la mise en service et à la réception provisoire ne devra pas dépasser dix-huit (18) mois, que ce soit en Gambie ou au Togo. Une période distincte de suivi de la garantie, d'une durée maximale de douze (12) mois, suivra la réception provisoire de chaque marché de travaux concerné. La durée maximale indicative est donc de trente (30) mois pour chaque contrat-pays.

Les Termes de référence (TDR) relatifs à l'étape principale de passation des marchés pour la mission peuvent être consultés au lien suivant : https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/za97oz4il597a8jl1zx3o/AETqwBMWx01U9G5exEcKE0A?rlkey=m2h9dcc9q2edb5988zr0tqowl&st=mqw79del&dl=0

La Commission de la CEDEAO a Abuja, pour le compte de la Gambie et du Togo invite à présent les cabinets admissibles (« Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt pour la fourniture des Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

Les critères d'établissement de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

  • Le Consultant doit être un cabinet de conseil en ingénierie juridiquement constitué et indépendant, ou un groupement de cabinets de conseil, spécialisé dans les infrastructures électriques, et possédant une solide expérience de la revue de conception, de la supervision de travaux, de l'administration des contrats, des essais et de la mise en service de réseaux de distribution d'électricité moyenne et basse tension ainsi que des postes associés ;

  • Au moins trois missions similaires portant sur la revue de conception et la supervision de la construction de réseaux de distribution MT/BT, dont au moins deux missions comprenant.

L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.15 et 3.16 du Règlement de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le FPI, édition de septembre 2025 (« Règlement de passation des marchés »), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

Les Consultants peuvent s'associer à d'autres cabinets afin de renforcer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l'association prend la forme d'un groupement et/ou d'une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d'un groupement, tous les membres seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de l'ensemble du contrat, s'ils sont retenus.

Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection fondée sur la qualité et le coût (SFQC), décrite dans le Règlement de passation des marchés et précisée dans la Demande de propositions.

Des informations complémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous, du lundi au vendredi, de 9 h 00 à 15 h 00 TU :
