TERMS OF REFERENCE

Technical supervision for the Civil Works under “Construction of a museum near the Dvin archaeological site” & “Restoration, conservation, landscaping, and visitor infrastructure improvement works at the Dvin archaeological site”

TRIP-CQS-TS-01

1. PROJECT BACKGROUND

The Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project (TRIP) aim to boost Armenia's tourism potential through targeted infrastructure and soft investments in several regions. It will support seven of the twenty identified tourism clusters, focusing on wine, wellness, adventure, culture, education, and ecotourism across Ararat, Vayots Dzor, Shirak, Tavush, and Syunik regions. The project will improve connectivity to these clusters and enhance tourism site infrastructure. It also seeks to elevate Armenia’s natural assets and human resources, improving business and professional skills in nearby communities to maximize the job creation. Additionally, TRIP aligns with the World Bank’s approach to attracting private investment in these tourism clusters.

Infrastructure investment component of TRIP include construction of new public buildings including museum buildings, restoration and preservation of historical monuments, urban regeneration of old towns and villages, including restoration of building facades, public spaces, museums, roads and enhancement of cultural and natural heritage sites, including access and presentation.

Overall management and coordination of implementation and supervision of Project will be executed by the Armenian Territorial Development Fund (CLIENT).

The present terms of reference describe consulting services for supervision of civil works under TRIP sought by the CLIENT.

The consulting services ("the Services") include daily supervision of the civil works. The civil works contracts to be supervised will include a variety of works, such as construction of new and restoration of existing buildings and cultural heritage monuments/sights, touristic infrastructure, as well as municipal water/wastewater systems, lighting, local roads and utility services.

2. OBJECTIVES

The purpose of construction supervision is to execute technical supervision over the civil works to ensure high quality of the civil works, adherence to the terms of work execution provided for in the construction contracts in compliance with the detailed design and specification requirements, to ensure the reliability, long-term sustainability and efficient operation of the civil works.

The main objective of the assignment is the daily supervision of the  construction or/and rehabilitation works, as the Technical Supervision Consultant (Consultant) on behalf of the CLIENT in accordance with the provisions of the signed contracts between CLIENT and Contractors in order to ensure the following:

a) High quality of construction in adherence to the valid standards, regulations and laws of Armenia and international standards and best practices; 

b) Adherence to the requirements of valid design (draft, detailed), specifications and performance standards by implementation of the provisions of the technical specifications and other provisions of the works contracts;

c) Adherence to the national environmental, social and labor legislation and regulations, and the World Bank’s ESF, and relevant Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs) applicable to TRIP,  as well as the site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) to be prepared for subprojects;

d) Completion of works in accordance with the works schedules and  contracts price.  

The tentative duration of this assignment is 30 months, plus defects liability period  after completion of each civil work  contract.

3. SCOPE OF SERVICES

  • Overall, the administration, execution and oversight of the “Civil Works to be implemented under the TRIP” will be organized via contract in three standard roles: Employer, Contractor, and Technical Supervision Consultant   
  • ATDF acts as the Client carrying out the overall and contractual coordination of the Project.
  • The Contractor executes the construction works.
  • The Consultant carries out daily technical supervision.

The Consultant shall review, assess, and provide recommendations on all engineering matters and technical decisions necessary for the efficient, timely, and successful implementation of the civil works contract, for the consideration and approval of the Employer.

The Consultant is directly responsible for daily supervision and immediate contacts with the works Contractors. Consultant will closely liaise with the Project Implementation and Supervision and Technical Supervision Departments of ATDF (CLIENT) to solve issues.

Consultant should ensure strict adherence of Contractors to the requirements of detailed designs, technical specifications, site-specific EMSPs, and Resettlement Plans (RPs).

The Consultant is responsible for mobilizing a team in compliance with the requirements and phases outlined below. The obligations include: providing all necessary personnel on site (engineers, supervisors, quality inspectors, environmental and social specialists, occupational health and safety (OHS) etc.) for the supervision of works, inspection and installation of the equipment, testing of construction materials, and monitoring the implementation of ESMPs and reporting.

Within ten (10) days after the signing of the Civil Works Contract the Consultant shall submit the detailed work plan of the technical supervision services (including scope of duties of each specialist of Consultant’s team) for Client’s approval. The Work Plan shall be aligned with the construction phases and tentative implementation schedule as well as a cost estimate indicating anticipated input (workday) of each specialist and covering all the costs related to supervision services.

Before the approval of the design documentation conduct a comprehensive, critical review of the proposed designs for each component by validating the necessary information obtained through Cadaster, local municipality, respective utility companies, etc. and via visiting the location of the contract site physically – and present written recommendations in the Inception Report regarding any necessary design changes or design aspects, which may pose implementation problems or unintended results during works.

 4. GENERAL AND SPECIFIC TASKS

4a. General Task

The tasks of the Consultant will include but not be limited to the following:

  1. Preparing a construction supervision work program to be prepared early during the Consultant’s contract commencement.
  2. Throughout the construction period, the Consultant shall undertake technical inspections and measurements to verify work quantities, maintain records of civil works, and certify completed works in accordance with reporting formats approved under the Contract.
  3. On a monthly basis, the Consultant shall prepare and submit to the Employer a report on quality-related issues, test results, non-compliances, identified defects, corrective actions and their resolution/implementation status.
  4. Reviewing the Contractors' payment certificates and giving respective feedback to CLIENT prior to approval by the latter;
  5. Verify the compliance between quantities and quality of executed works with the design and technical specifications; supervising adherence to the program and schedule of works to be executed by the Contractors;
  6. Supervising progress of preparation works (in accordance with the RA Construction Norms (RACN) 13-05-2026 "Organization of Construction Operations" and Order No. 09-A of the Chairman of the Urban Development Committee of the Republic of Armenia, dated 9 February 2023) to be executed by the Contractors, including construction of temporary structures in compliance with the work execution program and adherence to the terms provided for in the schedule; check and ensure that the Contractor has obtained all necessary permits and approvals from state and local governments, as well as utilities providers; and reporting, in writing, to the CLIENT.
  7. Check the safety of the works, property and personnel, and public in adherence to RACN regulations and TRIP site-specific E&S  instruments.
  8. Checking the compliance certifications of the construction materials used in construction (cement, aggregates, additives, reinforcement, metal constructions, precast concrete, bitumen, asphalt concrete elements, mineral materials, electrical cables, and water supply pipes,etc.), checking compliance of manufacturers’’ factory sample analysis and laboratory testing data with requirements of technical specifications and RACN;
  9. Reviewing and approving that installed equipment meets the specifications defined under the detailed design;
  10. Inspect compliance of as built drawings submitted by Contractors (endorsed by signature and sealed) with the executed works;
  11. Maintain a daily technical supervision register of works, implemented by the Contractor  making appropriate entries in the Construction Log maintained by the Contractor, recording observations, identified defects, and the measures taken for their rectification; receiving and concluding the phases of completed works with proper documents (certifications for hidden  works, tests and other documentation);
  12.  Conduct daily photography and video recording of construction activities performed, including these materials in the monthly reports and providing these materials upon Employer’s request. ;
  13. Certify completed stages of the Works in accordance with the format developed by the Consultant and approved by the Employer.
  14. Subject to the Employer’s approval, organize and supervise any additional unforeseen independent testing required to verify the final quality and compliance of the Works executed by the Contractor;
  15. In case of detecting defects or deficient works, compile a punch list setting deadlines for their rectification, immediately notify the Client in writing and monitor the rectification of these deficiencies.
  16. Observing and reviewing sampling, measurements and tests conducted by the Contractor (such as pressure tests for leaks) ensuring that the relevant records are prepared, for any works that are about to be covered or put out of view. In the event of identification of non-conformity with the RACNs, design requirements and/or specifications, prohibit the continuation of the works or the use of the materials, document such cases through appropriate formal records/acts and notifying the Employer in writing.
  17. Ensuring that Contractors have a good command of the requirements laid out in ESMPs, tracking adherence of Contractors’ performance with the ESMPs, and advising on and following the  implementation of the corrective actions in case of identified environmental and social non-compliances;
  18. Supervise Contractors’ compliance with labor management requirements, including enforcement of Codes of Conduct and the functioning of the workers’ grievance mechanism (GM) in line with Project Labor Management Procedures (LMP).
  19. Reviewing and making recommendations to the CLIENT Supervision Engineer for any requests for variation or change orders, and Contractors’ claims.
  20. Submitting periodic reports to the CLIENT in accordance with the requirements outlined in the Chapter on “Reporting” and Chapter on “Preparation of Reports and Submission Dates” of these TOR.
  21. Check and monitor the implementation of occupational safety briefings conducted by Contractors (in accordance with Inter-state Standard GOST 12.0.004-2015).

 

4b. Specific Tasks

The Consultant shall provide the following services under the direct guidance of the CLIENT:

  1. Inspect Contractors’ camps and temporary structures/buildings, storage areas, equipment and machinery to verify compliance with the applicable RACNs and detailed design requirements;
  2. Inspect quality and quantity of earthworks and foundation preparation: dimensions of foundation pits, trench’s cross sections, sand bedding, backfilling, quality of compacted fills, levels; gravel beds; lean concrete layers and etc;
  3. Supervise progress of concrete and reinforced concrete works. Inspect formwork dimensions, installation accuracy, quality, location of reinforcement and embedded parts, review of mix design, proper placement of concrete and testing resultant concrete strength, compliance of welded joints with the applicable RACNs;
  4. Supervise installation and repairs to the precast reinforced concrete constructions as well as inspection of dimensions, quality and placement of reinforced concrete elements, joint fillers, pads, water stops and other materials;
  5. Inspect reconstruction-restoration of buildings (architectural and structural parts); check conformance of supplied materials to the design requirements, specifications, and quality standards; inspect the workmanship of architectural and decorative elements of buildings; ensure application of the specified and approved technologies and materials; supervise strengthening of fundaments, supporting structures, seismic belts, change of roofs, building façade improvement containing brick finishing, plastering, changing of cornices, etc., rehabilitation of wooden, metallic and concrete balconies; rehabilitation of roofs (tile; soft roof, metal), rehabilitation of doors and windows, masonry works;
  6. Supervise and inspect road’ rehabilitation works: roadway pavement (different materials) layout of sidewalks, curbs, trails street furniture and etc.;
  7. Inspect installation of power cables, electrical equipment, lighting of streets, squares and parks;
  8. Inspect installation works of pressure and gravity pipelines (water supply, sewage, storm water) constructed of various materials (steel, cast iron, r/concrete, PE, PVC, etc.) including inspection of gradients, joints, fittings  and other accessories in accordance with construction codes and contract specifications and verify the conduct and availability of the observance and certification of pressure and other tests, including laboratory testing where applicable, to ensure that leakage, if any, does not exceed limits as provided under the technical specifications;
  9. Supervise progress of installation, mechanical and electrical equipment; after completion of interim phases of construction, test equipment together with Contractors and the CLIENT’s Supervision Engineer and certify that the tests met the requirements of the technical specifications;
  10. Inspect construction of water supply headworks, pumping stations, raw water treatment and wastewater treatment plants including start-up and commissioning of electrical and mechanical equipment; prior to the commissioning stage, review and approve the updated/detailed functional testing method and schedule submitted by the Contractor in line with the design specifications ; checking the results of functional tests;
  11. Check the installation of the pressure and gravity pipelines (waterlines, sewage, storm water) and laboratory/pressure test reports in accordance with the RACN;
  12. Inspect certificates of construction materials and equipment used during construction (electrical and mechanical equipment, pipes, valves, fire hydrants, flow meters, fittings, cement, inert materials, admixtures, reinforcement steel, metal-ware, pre-cast reinforced concrete elements, wooden and ceramic materials, road pavement materials and etc.); correspondence of data on sample analysis (carried out by the manufacturer in the factory) and laboratory tests to the requirements of the technical specifications and correspondence of construction materials used for restoration/conservation of physical cultural resources to the specifications and technological requirements of such works;  
  13. Monitor implementation of E&S mitigation measures in line with site-specific ESMPs in the course of works at each construction site; promptly notify the CLIENT on any deviations/violations of ESMP requirements, on any complaints from local communities related to ongoing works, and on any unforeseen issues affecting environment and/or cultural heritage which may emerge in the course of works; recommend remedial and/or corrective measures to the CLIENT and follow up on their application upon the CLIENT’s approval;  
  14. Oversee temporary on-site storage and final disposal of construction waste to the formally assigned sites or landfills and on the reinstatement of work sites upon completion of activity at any given one;
  15. Support effective implementation of Project Feedback and Grievance Redress Mechanism (FGRM) at the local level in accordance with the Project Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and notify Project Coordinator on any issues appeared at the site.
  16. Inspect and oversee the implementation of by Operational Health and Security (OHS) measures, at the construction site, including the safety of structures used for work at heights and the proper use of appropriate PPE in accordance with site-specific ESMPs.
  17. Oversee implementation of community health and safety measures in accordance with site-specific ESMPs, including site safety, access control, traffic management, and ensure that community complaints related to health, safety, and nuisance are properly recorded, addressed, and reported through the FGRM.
  18. Verify that site-level information disclosure measures are in place, including appropriate signage and FGRM contact details, and verify that any access restrictions and safety requirements are clearly communicated to nearby residents in accordance with site-specific ESMPs.
  19. Promptly inform the Client about any accident and incident related to the project within 24 hours, that may have adversely affected the environment, communities, public or workers, for instance labor or transport related accidents that might result in serious injuries etc; participate in incident investigations and related reporting, as required by the Client, in line with the ESCP and applicable incident reporting procedures.

 

5. REPORTING

At the outset of the contract commencement, the Consultant shall elaborate a reporting system (systematic registration and submission of the appropriate documents) CLIENT to provide regular, complete and detailed information to the CLIENT on progress and quality of civil works.

The Consultant shall submit to the Client  the following reports:

  • Monthly Progress Report summarizing progress with the construction activities, problems encountered, updated planning, status of ESMP compliance and any outstanding issues deemed important by the Consultant. These reports shall have appended to them the daily technical supervision register of works (See item 13 of General Tasks) and filled out monthly environmental and social monitoring forms, as well as the physical and financial progress report for each CW site, along with the forecast for the next period.
  • Special reports as may be required if there are one or more problems that require immediate attention of the CLIENT.
  • Quarterly report on the period of work indicating progress on each subproject, course of activities, implementation of ESMPs, and any proposed changes to the work plan;
  • As built-drawings prepared by Contractors and confirmed by Consultant;
  • Final Project Completion report including Civil work contract data, contract variations, a table of actually completed works and disbursed funds by month, photographs, general comments on the Contractor's performance, an environmental and social final report, the results of the Acceptance Commission's work.

5a.Preparation of Reports and Submission Dates

          The above reports shall be presented in according to the following requirements:

  • All reports shall be prepared in Microsoft Word and Excel, and presented to the CLIENT as bound documents according to agreed quantities (see table hereafter), in both hard copies and electronic files.
  • Drawings will also be provided in hard copies and electronic forms (AutoCAD or compatible software). Reports should have attachments such as video and photo materials about the activity progress as evidence. 
  • The reports should be submitted in Armenian and English languages.

 

Reports (English and Armenian)

Date

  1. Monthly report

Within 7 days of next month

  1. Quarterly report

Within 7 days of  month next to each quarter

  1. Final Completion Report including confirmed as-built drawings

Within 7 days after receiving the signed hand-over/acceptance protocol

 

6. INPUT BY CLIENT

 

The CLIENT shall provide the Consultant with detailed design documentation, technical specifications, Project Environmental and Social Instruments, including the ESMPs, and other available documents needed for proper implementation of construction supervision for each subproject.

ATDF will appoint its own specialists/engineers for each subproject, who will work closely with the Consultant and perform contract management and final decision-making functions.

procnotices.contact_address: DRC

procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO

 

MINISTERE DE L’ENTREPRENEURIAT ET DEVELOPPEMENT DES PETITES ET MOYENNES ENTREPRISES

 

Unité de Coordination du Projet

 

PROJET D’AUTONOMISATION DES FEMMES ENTREPRENEURES ET MISE A NIVEAU DES PME POUR LA TRANSFORMATION ECONOMIQUE ET L’EMPLOI

« TRANSFORME-RDC »

 

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

(Sélection de Consultant Individuel)

 

RECRUTEMENT D'UN SPÉCIALISTE EN PASSATION DES MARCHÉS POUR LE PROJET TRANSFORME

 

N° Avis : AMI N°ZR-TRANSFORME-571547-CS-INDV

Source de financement : Banque mondiale (Crédit n°7101-ZR& Don E0280-ZR)

Date de publication : 14 Septembre 2026

Date de clôture : 13 octobre 2026

 

  1. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie nationale de développement des PME, le Gouvernement de la RDC a sollicité et obtenu de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) un crédit et un don pour financer le « Projet d’Autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi », TRANSFORME RDC en sigle. L’objectif de développement de ce projet est d’améliorer la croissance et la création d'emplois des MPME nouvelles et existantes, en particulier celles appartenant à des femmes, dans des zones géographiques sélectionnées. Le projet devrait permettre d'atteindre l'objectif de développement en s'attaquant à trois contraintes critiques pour les emplois du secteur privé et la transformation économique : (i)capacités des entreprises ; (ii) accès au financement ; et (iii) environnement des affaires.

 

  1. L’objectif de la mission du Spécialiste en Passation des marchés est d’assurer le bon déroulement de toutes les activités de passation des marchés du projet TRANSFORME. A ce titre, il réalise ou supervise toutes les activités relatives à la planification, la conduite du processus de passation des marchés des biens, travaux, services non consultants et services de consultants dans le cadre dudit projet.

 

  1. L’UCP-TRANSFORME invite les candidats (« Consultants Individuels ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services.

 

  1. Les critères de qualification pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

 

  1. Être titulaire d’un diplôme d’études de niveau Bac + 5 ans minimum en droit, économie, ingénierie, gestion, passation des marchés ou dans une discipline jugée équivalente ;
  2. Disposer d’une formation complémentaire ou une certification pertinente en passation des marchés selon les procédures des institutions financières internationales, constitue un avantage ;
  3. Avoir une expérience globale minimale de 10 ans dont au moins trois (03) ans au poste de Spécialiste en passation de marchés ou cinq (05) au poste de Chargé de passation des marchés dans des projets ou programmes financés par des institutions financières internationales ou des partenaires techniques et financiers. Une expérience récente et démontrée de l’application du Règlement de passation des marchés de Banque mondiale est un atout majeur.
  4. Avoir une bonne connaissance des procédures de la Banque mondiale pour la passation des marchés et des accords de financement ; avoir une bonne maîtrise de l’informatique et logiciels de base de données et de bureautique,
  5. Avoir une maîtrise des procédures de passation de marchés de l'Etat ainsi que celles des collectivités locales,
  6. Être capable de travailler en équipe et sous pression ;
  7. Avoir une parfaite maîtrise du français ;
  8. Avoir une maîtrise du Système électronique de gestion des marchés sur financement de la Banque mondiale (STEP : Systematic tracking of exchanges in procurement) est un atout majeur ;
  9. Une bonne capacité de rédaction, d’analyse et de communication en français est requise. La connaissance professionnelle de l’anglais est un avantage.
  10. Avoir la maîtrise de l’outil informatique et avoir une connaissance des logiciels standards (Word, Excel, Power Point, …).

 

  1. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projet d’investissement (FPI) », édition de septembre 2025, relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables.

 

  1. Un (e)Consultant (e) sera sélectionné (e) selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultant Individuel (SCI), telle que décrite dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projet d’investissement (FPI) », édition de septembre 2025 en vertu du Nouveau Cadre des Marchés Publics (NCPM), et les « Lignes Directrices »  de la Banque mondiale sur la Prévention et la Lutte contre la Fraude et la Corruption dans les projets financés sur les Prêts de la BIRD, et les crédits et les subventions de l’IDA (datant du 1er juillet 2016), ainsi que les dispositions stipulées dans l’Accord de financement applicables au projet.

 

  1. Les Consultants (es) intéressés (es) peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires, notamment sur les termes de référence, à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes de 9 à 16 heures locales (TU+1) ou sur le site web « www.transforme.cd ».

 

  1. Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites, en langue française, doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous, par courrier physique ou par courrier électronique (e-mail), au plus tard le mardi 13 octobre 2026 à 16 heures (heure locale à Kinshasa) et porter clairement la mention ci-dessous : AMI N°ZR-TRANSFORME-571547-CS-INDV « Recrutement d'un spécialiste en passation des marchés pour le projet Transforme ».

 

 

 

À l'attention : Monsieur le Coordonnateur National du Projet TRANSFORME

Projet d’autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi « TRANSFORME-RDC »

Sise, Avenue Lemarinel n°9-11, (en face du Collège Boboto),

Téléphone (+243) 830 833 833

Email : transforme@transforme.cd ; cpm@transforme.cd.

procnotices.notice_text:
Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements Project (VARS)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

Individual Selection of Consultant

Assignment Title:

ESMASP Applications Officer

Duty Station:

PMU, Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources,

Port Vila, Vanuatu

Date of Publication:

15th September 2026

Deadline for submission:

29th September 2026 at time: 1400 Hours.

Reference Number:

VU-MLNR-568292-CS-INDV

1. BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT:

The Elol Etas Subdivision Marketing, Allocation and Sale Process (ESMASP) is the government-led process for the transparent marketing, allocation and sale of residential lots in the Elol Etas (Etas Gardens) Subdivision. It is implemented by the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources (MoLNR), with operational and administrative support from the Project Management Unit (PMU) of the Vanuatu Affordable and Resilient Settlements (VARS) Project, financed by the World Bank. The ESMASP Office operates visibly as a MoLNR function, reinforcing that the subdivision is a Government of Vanuatu-led project.

The ESMASP is delivered by a three-person core implementation team — the ESMASP Manager, an ESMASP Project Officer and an ESMASP Applications Officer — supported by the VARS PMU and MoLNR and complemented by a defined set of allied in-house resources drawn from the PMU and the Ministry: nominated outreach leads, a pool of PMU interns providing outreach and intake support, in-house database, web-administration and IT support staff, and PMU vehicles. Public awareness, marketing and community engagement are delivered in-house by this team; no external NGO delivery partner is engaged. Applications are received through a single, controlled channel — in person at the ESMASP Office, where they are entered directly into the application system by ESMASP staff (subject to Project Steering Committee confirmation of the in-person-only channel). Given anticipated oversubscription in the order of 20:1, the integrity of the selection process is the single most important deliverable of the ESMASP, and all positions carry explicit transparency, conflict-of-interest, and documentation obligations.

The ESMASP Applications Officer holds the application-management role within the team and leads the ESMASP Office as the single point of application registration. The position was restored as a dedicated role in recognition of the application-management workload implied by the anticipated 20:1 oversubscription and the sustained reserve-list reallocation function that runs through to settlement. Under the in-house delivery model, the Office carries a larger share of the applicant-facing workload than previously planned, and the Officer supervises the interns assigned to Office reception, application terminals, data entry and scanning. The role also provides internal separation between application processing and the outreach and grievance-intake functions held by the Project Officer, in support of the segregation-of-duties controls in the Implementation Manual.

2. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

To manage the receipt, screening, and administration of ESMASP applications and applicant data through the ESMASP Office application desk, supervised applicant terminals and Help Desk, as the single controlled application channel and to operate the reserve-list and reallocation function through to settlement, with complete, accurate and secure records that withstand independent audit.

4. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

Qualifications and Experience

  • Required: A diploma or bachelor's degree in business administration, information management, ICT, accounting, records management, or a related field; or a secondary school certificate (Year 12/13) combined with at least three years of demonstrated experience in data entry, records administration, registry work or customer/client service systems.
  • Desirable: Certificate or formal training in database administration, records/information management or data protection; bookkeeping or accounting basics (relevant to the Sales and Purchase Agreement and deposit records function); or experience with government registry or banking back-office systems.

Essential

  • Demonstrated accuracy in database administration and data handling, with sustained attention to detail under high volumes.
  • Demonstrated confidentiality and sound judgement in handling personal or sensitive data.
  • Competence with online systems, databases, and the Microsoft Office suite — particularly Excel and other relevant programs, including data entry, validation, and reporting.
  • Strong record-keeping and filing discipline, including scanning, document control and audit-trail maintenance.
  • Ability to supervise and organise junior support staff or interns in a busy public-facing office, including rostering, checklist-based procedures, and quality checks.
  • Good communication skills in Bislama and English for the application desk and Help Desk function, including managing queues and applicant expectations calmly under pressure.
  • Integrity and willingness to sign and comply with the ESMASP Conflict-of-Interest Declaration, the Office intake controls and documentation disciplines.

Desirable

  • Experience with application, registry, customer, or beneficiary management systems, or with donor-financed project record-keeping.
  • Experience in front-desk or help-desk service delivery to the public, including high-volume intake or registration exercises.

5. REPORTING:

The Applications Officer reports to the ESMASP Manager, who leads the ESMASP implementation team within the VARS PMU. The Officer works alongside the ESMASP Project Officer; supervises interns assigned to Office and data functions, in rotation agreed with the Project Officer and the PMU; liaises on system matters with the in-house database, web-administration and IT support staff under the direction of the ESMASP Manager; and draws on VARS PMU operational and administrative support (including surge support during peak periods). The Officer receives from the Project Officer the schedule of Office intake days announced at settlement sessions and advises the Project Officer and ESMASP Manager daily during the application window on intake volumes and terminal capacity.

6. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT:

Approximately fifteen (15) months (full sales and marketing process), full-time; possible reduced-capacity extension through close-out

7. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS:

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing – Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (INDV) Method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Interested applicants may obtain further information including a detailed Terms of Reference from the Ministry in person or by e-mail to the address given below during office hours from 8.00 a.m.– 5.00 p.m. Monday to Friday.

Deadline: Expressions of interest and CV must be delivered to the address below by hand, mail, or email on or before 29th September 2026 at 14:00 Hours Vanuatu Time.

THE UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

                                                                                MINISTRY OF WORKS

                                                                        TANZANIA NATIONAL ROADS

                                               TANZANIA TRANSPORT INTEGRATION PROJECT (TanTIP)

                                                                            PROJECT ID: P165660

 

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR CONSULTING FIRM FOR UNDERTAKING ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL AUDITING FOR LUSAHUNGA - RUSUMO ROAD AND CERC PROJECTS UNDER TANZANIA TRANSPORT INTEGRATION PROJECT (TANTIP) Tender No;        TR36/2026/2027/C/22

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

  1. The Government of the United Republic of Tanzania has received the financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Tanzania Transport Integration Project (TanTIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for eligible payments under the contract for Consultancy Services for undertaking Environmental and Social Auditing for Lusahunga - Rusumo Road and CERC Projects under Tanzania Transport Integration Project
  2. Project Location and Description

The Lusahunga – Rusumo road section (92 Km), forms part of the T3 (Central Corridor Highway) which connects the Dar es Salaam port with the land locked neighboring countries of Rwanda and Burundi. The project road starts at Lusahunga centre through Nyakasanza and ends at Rusumo Border (Tanzania and Rwanda). The Lusahunga – Rusumo road was upgraded in 1985 to bitumen standard for a design life of 15 years. The road consists of 27 box culverts 52 steel pipe culverts and 8 reinforced concrete culverts. Out of 92 Km of the project road 63 Km are located in Biharamulo district and the remaining 29 Km are located in Ngara District.

The Project Road traverses through four villages in Biharamulo district namely Lusahunga, Kikoma (Lusahunga Ward), Ngararambe and Nyabugombe, (Nyakahura ward) while on the Ngara district side there are two villages of Kasulo (Kasulo ward) and Rusumo (Rusumo ward). Currently, the road is under construction after had deteriorated drastically due to pavement aging despite the efforts that had been carried out by TANROADS - Kagera Regional Manager, to maintain and repair. Typical road defects include severe potholes, rutting, deformation, corrugations, extensive cracking that collected for rehabilitation (alligator cracks) and depressions.

Similarly, the CERC projects are scattered over 21 regions (Dodoma, DSM, Morogoro, Arusha, Singida, Mwanza, Njombe, Mbeya, Simiyu, Tanga, Manyara, Kigoma, Rukwa, Sumbawanga, Iringa, Mtwara, Lindi, Ruvuma, Coast, Mara and Geita); most of CERC projects that are implemented includes; construction of road embarkments, bridges and culverts with drainage system which was affected by El-NiNo rainfall that occurred in FY 2024/2025. The construction of CERC projects (road embarkments, bridges and culverts with drainage system) are rated to have minimum E&S impacts to the surrounding environmental and social set-up, hence the remedial measures under emergency scenarios were designed to each CERC subprojects to minimize the adverse impacts under emergency response in order to provide the roads transport access which was affected in most part of the country. Therefore, in order for TANROADS to comply with the WB -ESF requirement and ESCP under emergency response mechanism, the engagement of Consulting firm to undertake the E&S Auditing is hereby required to assess the magnitude of the E&S impacts during the implementation of the CERC sub-projects and assess compliance requirements in order to recommend on the way-forward to any future similar events. The E&S Auditing shall be undertaken and completed by October, 2026.

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective of this consultancy is to design, develop, and support the initial implementation of a robust, comprehensive, and fit-for-purpose Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) for TANROADS. This system will enable the agency to manage E&S risks and impacts systematically and effectively across all its activities, ensuring compliance with national regulations and alignment with international best practices.

  1. Specific Objectives

The specific objectives of the assignment are to:

  1. Conduct a comprehensive diagnostic review and gap analysis of TANROADS' existing E&S management policies, procedures, institutional capacity, and practices against Tanzanian legal requirements and the standards of key international financing institutions (IFIs);
  2. Develop a high-level corporate Environmental and Social (E&S) Policy Statement that articulates TANROADS' commitment to sustainable development and responsible infrastructure delivery;
  3. Design a detailed ESMS framework, including a complete set of operational procedures, tools, guidelines, and templates for managing the entire E&S risk lifecycle (from screening and assessment to monitoring and closure);
  4. Propose appropriate institutional arrangements, including clear roles, responsibilities, and reporting lines, to ensure effective implementation and governance of the ESMS at corporate, regional, and project levels;
  5. Develop a comprehensive, multi-year capacity-building and training plan to equip TANROADS staff with the necessary skills and knowledge to implement the ESMS, and to conduct initial Training of Trainers (ToT) sessions; and
  6. Develop a phased, costed, and time-bound Implementation Roadmap for the full rollout and operationalization of the ESMS across TANROADS.

 

  1. Scope of Services

The Consultant's work shall be structured into the following four distinct but interconnected phases. The Consultant is expected to work in close collaboration with a designated TANROADS Counterpart Team throughout the assignment. The four phases are:

  • Phase 1:    Inception and Diagnostic Assessment (Approx. 1 Months);
  • Phase 2:    ESRMS Design and Development (Approx. 2 Months);
  • Phase 3:    Institutional Arrangements and Capacity Building (Approx. 2 Months); and
  • Phase 4:    Implementation Roadmap and Finalization (Approx. 1 month)
  1. The Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS), now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

    1. Eligibility, at least ten (10) years of international experience in providing advisory services on environmental and social risk management;
    2. Demonstrable experience in developing and implementing ESMS or similar E&S management systems for 3 (Three) large public sector agencies or private corporations, preferably in the infrastructure sector (roads, energy, transport);
    3. Proven track record of successfully completing at least three (3) similar assignments in the last seven (7) years;
    4. In-depth knowledge of the E&S standards of the World Bank and IFC; and
    5. Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa is required; experience in Tanzania is a strong asset.

SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

Invitation for Bids (IFB)

 

 

Project: Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development Project

Contract title: Improvement Works at Alajo Drain

Country: Ghana

Credit No.: IDA-64100

RFB No: GH-MWH-219660-CW-RFB

Issued on: September 19, 2026

  1. The Government of Ghana has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for the Improvement Works at Alajo Drain. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.
  2. The Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources invites sealed bids from eligible contractors for the improvement works at Alajo drain. The works involve two main interventions:
  1. The construction of a covered reinforced concrete culvert parallel to the Eastern Railway Line (Railway drain), aiming to improve flood management in the Alajo urban area. The new infrastructure consists of a 1,596-meter-long rectangular box culvert with internal dimensions of 5.00m by 2.00m, designed with a constant invert slope of 0.3% to ensure optimal hydraulic performance and prevent water stagnation.

The proposed drain alignment passes through densely urbanized areas, cultivated plots, and near existing structures, requiring the relocation or demolition of some buildings, careful excavation work including vertical sheet piling and retaining walls where needed, as well as connections with secondary drainage. Special attention is given to the crossing under the Eastern Railway Line, where the culvert will be placed at a depth of 1.4 meters to prevent interference with the rail infrastructure. The culvert discharges into the Odaw River with an outfall designed at a 45-degree angle to the river flow.

Secondary drainage connections are included, with inspection manholes spaced every 50 meters and fitted with sediment traps and grates to manage solid waste. Additional protective works include, especially in proximity to agricultural land.

  1. The refurbishment/reconstruction of primary/secondary channels of the Alajo Urban Drainage Network. The Alajo urban area has a surface of around 270 hectares and it is enclosed by the existing railway at the North side, by the Onyasia drain at the East side and by the Nsawam road at the West side. The main Odaw river flows within that area, bounding the Alajo area on the West side. The confluence between the Odaw and Onyasia is located at the southern limit of this area, at Caprice.

The existing drains consist of open/covered rectangular concrete sections, varying in size from 0.4m (width) x 0.4m (height) for the smallest drains to 1.5m (width) x 1.5m (height) for the largest ones. The slope of these drains ranges from 0.2% to 1.5%, except in a few cases where the slope approaches zero. The current drainage network is insufficient, as many existing drains are in poor condition or completely absent in some areas.

The new designed drain network consists of rectangular cast-in-situ concrete box culverts, with dimensions ranging from 1.0m (width) x 1.0m (height) to 2.0m (width) x 1.5mm (height). Installation of flap gates at each new outlet in the main channels and inspection manholes are included in the scope of work, along with the complete reinstatement of roads affected by construction.

The project is scheduled for completion within 18 months and includes site preparation works, excavation, concrete construction, steel fittings, backfilling, and reinstatement of affected road and pedestrian infrastructure.

 

  1. Bidding will be conducted through National Competitive Procurement using Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th Edition September, 2025 (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.
  2. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources, Mr. Daniel Kusi, email: dkojokusi@gmail.com and inspect the Bidding document during office hours (9:00 Hrs GMT-16:00 Hrs GMT) at the address (2) given below.

The method of payment will be cash. The document will be sent by Courier at an additional cost of GHC 100.00.

Bids will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend at the address (3) below on on November 3, 2026 at 10:00 HRS GMT.

MINISTÈRE DE LA PLANIFICATION ET DE LA PROSPECTIVE

COMMISSION NATIONALE DES TIPPEE

SECRÉTARIAT PERMANENT                                                                                                                            

 

AVIS D’APPEL D’OFFRES OUVERT INTERNATIONAL

(Processus d’appel d’offres à deux enveloppes sans préqualification avec critères notés)

AAOI n° : 02-2026/CW/CNT/HISWACA

 

Pays                :   Gabon.

Projet             :   Projet Régional d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique Centrale, Série de Projet 2 (HISWACA - SOP2).

Financement  :   BIRD, Prêt n° 9661-GA / id : P180085.

Objet              :   Travaux de construction du siège de l'Institut National de la Statistique du Gabon (INSTAT GABON).

Réf. STEP     :   GA-CN TIPPEE-566029-CW-RFB.

Émis le           :   11/09/2026.

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République Gabonaise a obtenu un prêt de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d'Harmonisation et d'Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique Centrale et de l'Ouest, Série de Projet 2 (HISWACA - SOP2) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements relatifs au marché des travaux de construction du siège de l'Institut National de la Statistique du Gabon (INSTAT GABON).

Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera pour les paiements, la méthode de décaissement intitulée « Paiement Direct », telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour les Financements de Projets d’Investissements.

Le projet est mis en œuvre par le Ministère de la Planification et de la Prospective à travers l’Institut National de la Statistique (INSTAT GABON), Maître de l’ouvrage et par la Commission Nationale des Travaux d’Intérêt Public pour la Promotion de l’Entreprenariat et de l’Emploi (CNTIPPEE), Agence fiduciaire.

2. La CNTIPPEE, agissant pour le compte de l’INSTAT GABON invite, par la présente, les Soumissionnaires à présenter leurs Offres sous pli fermé, pour la réalisation à Libreville des travaux susmentionnés en un lot unique.

Ces travaux se composent comme il suit :

Composants

Caractéristiques

Bâtiment principal

R+6 / 13.456 m² SHON / 10.351 m² utiles / Capacité 400 agents / Fondations profondes sur pieux.

Data Center

395 m² / Climatisation de précision InRow / Extinction gaz Novec 1230.

Réhabilitation mur de clôture existant

Réhabilitation complète de la clôture périphérique existante d’une longueur d’environ 400 m avec portails d'entrée.

Aménagements extérieurs

Voiries / Espaces verts / Éclairage public / Assainissement pluvial.

VRD

Réseaux d'eau potable, d'électricité, de télécommunications et d'assainissement.

Travaux hydrauliques

Raccordements aux réseaux publics et dévoiement des canalisations existantes

Certification EDGE

Obligatoire / Objectifs : Énergie -20%, Eau -20%, Matériaux -20%.

Site de construction

Localisation Oloumi ; Libreville ; Superficie : 6.787 m² - Clôturé.

Coordonnées géographiques approximatives du centroïde : latitude 0°22' N, longitude 9°26' E, altitude ≈ 12 m NGG.

Durée estimée des travaux

Trente-deux (32) mois.

3. La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence internationale en utilisant un Appel d’Offres (AO) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation de Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteur de Projets d'Investissement (FPI) », 7ème édition, septembre 2025, accessible à l'adresse www.worldbank.org et ouvert à tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.

La procédure est un processus à deux enveloppes (technique et financière) avec application de critères notés.

4. Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres. Les pondérations suivantes s'appliqueront :

Critères

Pondération

Facteurs techniques et autres que le prix

50%

Coût de l'Offre

50%

5. Les Soumissionnaires éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires auprès de la CNTIPPEE et examiner le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres durant les heures de bureau (9h00 à 17h00) à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.

6. Le Dossier d'Appel d'Offres complet en français peut être obtenu par tout soumissionnaire éligible intéressé en formulant une demande écrite (par lettre ou par courrier électronique) mentionnant ses coordonnées complètes à l'adresse ci-dessous, contre un paiement non-remboursable de Deux Cent Mille (200.000) FCFA ou son équivalent en euros (environ 305 Euro), payable par virement bancaire ou chèque de banque à l'ordre de la CNTIPPEE (IBAN : GA21 4000 1090 7010 1046 0020 119).

Le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres sera adressé par voie électronique ou retiré sur place.

7. Les Soumissions doivent être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 26 octobre 2026 à 11h00 (heure locale du Gabon, GMT+1). L’appel d’offres par voie électronique n’est pas permis. Toute Soumission reçue en retard sera écartée. Les enveloppes extérieures de l’Offre marquées « ORIGINAL DE L’OFFRE », et les enveloppes intérieures marquées « PARTIE TECHNIQUE » seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne qui souhaitent assister à l’ouverture des plis à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous. Toutes les enveloppes marquées « PARTIE FINANCIÈRE » demeureront non-ouvertes et seront conservées dans un lieu sûr par le Maître d’Ouvrage jusqu’à la seconde ouverture publique des Offres.

8. Les Soumissions doivent être accompagnées :

a. d’une Garantie bancaire d’offre pour un montant de Cent Trente Cinq Millions (135.000.000) FCFA (ou son équivalent en euros). Cette garantie doit être placée dans l'enveloppe marquée « PARTIE TECHNIQUE ». L'omission de cette garantie entraîne le rejet de l'Offre ;

b. d’une Déclaration relative à l’Exploitation et aux Abus Sexuels (EAS) ;

c. d’une Déclaration d’Engagement de main d’œuvre locale.

9. Veuillez noter que le Règlement de Passation des Marchés exige que l’Emprunteur divulgue les informations sur les propriétaires effectifs du Soumissionnaire attributaire, dans le cadre de l’avis de Notification d’Attribution de Marché, en renseignant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs inclus dans le dossier d’appel d’offres.

The Government of the United Republic of Tanzania, through the Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS), is implementing the Tanzania Transport Integrated Project (TanTIP) with financial support from World Bank. The project includes the rehabilitation and improvement of the Mtwara – Mingoyo – Masasi Road (201 km) to bitumen standard.

The Mtwara – Mingoyo – Masasi road is a major, primarily paved, trunk road in Southern Tanzania. It runs through Mtwara Region, with some segments potentially bordering Lindi Region. Based on the route and nearby locations, the road traverses through the following districts and administrative areas.  Mtwara Municipal (Start point), Mtama DC, Mtwara District Council and Masasi District (End point). The road traverses from Mtwara town through Mikindani towards Mingoyo, then west to Nanganga and Masasi. Through the following centre; (Magomeni/Mikindani).

The road corridor passes through the Mikindani Town which is one of the significant historical Cultural Heritage Site recognized for its rich in cultural heritage, historical buildings, archaeological sites and intangible cultural values. In compliance with the national legislation and international safeguard requirements, measures have been developed to protect and manage cultural heritage resources during project implementation as presented in the Mikindani Cultural Heritage Management Plans (CHMP) and ESMP.

The Government, through Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS) intends to apply part of the credit proceeds to eligible payments under Contract for Consultancy Services for Engagement of Individual Consultant for Monitoring of Cultural Heritage Management under the Tanzania Transport Integrated Project (TanTIP) at Mikindani Cultural Site in Mtwara Ragion.

procnotices.notice_text:
Request for Expressions of Interest

 

Country: The Republic of the Gambia

Project Title: The Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills and Equity Project RISE

Grant Number: P1729233

Assignment Title: Consultancy to develop the National Nutrition Regulation and Guideline for NaNA

Procurement Method: Individual Consultant Selection (INDV)

Reference No.: GM-CPCU - MOFEA-556550-CS-INDV

 

Background:

The Gambia is a small country with a total area of about 10,690 square kilometers.  It is surrounded on all sides by the Republic of Senegal, except in the West by the Atlantic Ocean. The population is estimated 2.42 million with a high population growth rate of 3.1 percent per year (Census, 2024). The 2017 Human Development Index shows the country rank at 174 out of 189 countries. Efforts to fight poverty have also proven ineffective with poverty levels remaining unchanged in the past decade (the percentage of households living below the poverty line of 1.25 $/day is 48.65 per cent in 2015 (HIS 2015/2016). The average GDP growth of 3 per cent per annum has barely kept up with population growth of 3.1 per cent. Data from the 2019/20 Demographic Health Survey (DHS) showed encouraging results for U5MR having dropped to 34 per 1,000 down from  54 per 1,000 live births in 2013, Maternal Mortality Ratio estimated 189/100,000 down from at 433/100000 live births in 2013.

Micronutrient deficiencies are widespread and continue to pose serious public health risks. Anaemia affects 44.8% of children, and only 10.8% of households consume adequately iodized salt even though 77% do consume iodized salt. Vitamin A deficiency affects 18.3% of children under five (MICS 2018). These figures highlight the urgency of interventions such as supplementation, iodization, fortification, and biofortification, supported by regulatory frameworks like the Food Fortification Regulation (2020). Despite these efforts, gaps in coverage and compliance persist, particularly in rural and underserved communities. Strengthening supply chains, enforcement mechanisms, and public awareness campaigns will be essential to improving micronutrient outcomes.

Infant and young child feeding practices show mixed progress. While 98% of children are breastfed, only 36% of mothers initiate breastfeeding within one hour of birth and 53.6% of children are exclusively breastfed. Complementary feeding remains inadequate, with just 15% of children receiving a minimum acceptable diet. The prevalence of malnutrition has improved with the DHS 2019/20 estimating stunting at 17.5% from 25% in 2013, wasting 5.1% from 12% and underweight 11.6% from 16%. These indicators reflect broader food and nutrition security challenges. The country produces only 50% of its food needs and over half the population (60.2%) do not have enough to meet their food expenditure, according to the Integrated Household Survey (IHS 2022). Climate change, low agricultural productivity, and population growth exacerbate these conditions, prompting national strategies focused on climate-smart agriculture, diversified and increased local food promotion and integration of nutrition into broader development efforts.

Non-communicable Diseases (NCDs) are on the rise, driven by poor diets, sedentary lifestyles, and urbanization. Hypertension affects 47% of adults, and obesity is significantly higher among women (20.2%) compared to men (3.9%) (WHO STEPS Survey 2019). Only 6.6% of the population meets WHO physical activity guidelines, reflecting lifestyle shifts associated with urbanization, poor dietary habits and sedentary lifestyles. The Fill the Nutrient Gap analysis 2025 shows that only 29% can afford a healthy diet. National responses focus on prevention by adopting appropriate dietary guidelines and lifestyles through social and behaviour change communication, and multisectoral collaboration. However, implementation remains fragmented, and greater investment in community-based prevention and promotion of healthy behaviours is needed.

As a cross cutting issue, the improvement and implementation of nutrition interventions and programme requires a strong coordination mechanism to avoid duplication and gaps. The National Nutrition Agency (NaNA) was established in 2000 as a semi-autonomous government institution strategically placed under the Office of The Vice President through an Agency Board with the legal mandate to coordinate nutrition and nutrition-related activities and advocate for the mainstreaming of nutrition into the macroeconomic and sectoral policy frameworks, implement nutrition activities, monitor nutrition interventions and programmes, mobilize and manage resources in The Gambia.

The Agency became a legal entity in 2005 through an Act of the National Assembly (Food Act 2005) which is now repealed and replaced by the Nutrition Act 2024. This ensures effective coordination of nutrition interventions across sectors. The Agency serves as the Secretariat to the National Nutrition Council (an inter-Ministerial body chaired by the Vice President), the country Scaling Up of Nutrition (SUN) Movement and the National Alliance for Food Fortification (NAFF).

The Agency was charged with the overall coordination and implementation of the policy with the following core mandates:

  1. Coordination of policy implementation
  2. Implementation of nutrition activities
  3. Secretariat of the National Nutrition Council
  4. Nutrition policy analysis, research and indicative planning
  5. Monitoring of nutrition interventions and programmes
  6. Mobilisation, management and coordination of resources

Following the enactment of the Nutrition Act 2024, there is need to develop a regulation that is critical for establishing and  formalising the multisectoral governance structures that ensure food and nutrition security and better help to understand and implement the Nutrition Act 2024. The regulation will also translate political commitment into actionable, accountable and sustainable interventions. To work on the development of a Nutrition Regulation, The Gambia, Resilience, Inclusion, Skills and Equity (RISE) Project  has sought the expertise of a Legal Expert for the task.

Objective of The Assignment:

The objective of exercise is to review and develop comprehensive nutrition regulation.

Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities:

The scope of the work will cover the following:

  1. Inception meeting to identify areas of focus for the development of the regulation
  2. Map out which provisions of the Nutrition Act 2024 require secondary legislation particularly focusing on:
    1. Establishment of the Nutrition Fund (modalities, management tea composition and areas of usage)
    2. Reference intake of vitamins and minerals in food sources
    3. Prescription of fortification mix
    4. Establishment of fortification coordination platform (NAFF)
  3. Draft a Nutrition Regulation
  4. Conduct consultative meetings to seek the views of the stakeholders on the new draft Nutrition Regulation
  5. Incorporate views and comments in the draft Regulation
  6. Conduct a national validation of the draft regulation
  7. Facilitate review by the Ministry of Justice
  8. Finalize the Regulation and submit for approval by the Minister responsible for Nutrition

The Draftsman will require close collaboration with the NaNA for continued guidance.

4.  Individual Consultant Qualifications and Experience

Given the high level of technical rigor required to carry out the exercise, which is a succinct and analytically sound comprehensive Nutrition Regulation, dedicated human resource capacity is required in terms of time and technical expertise in conducting such a task. National Expert will objectively review the implementation and coordination mechanisms established by the Nutrition Act 2024 and any other relevant mechanisms. Hence an appropriate experienced expert, who is familiar with the development context in The Gambia and having good working experience of drafting regulations will be preferred. The Expert should possess the following qualification and experience:

  • MSc in Law or equivalent
  • At least 5 years’ experience in legal drafting
  • Familiarity with Gambian law and with food, nutrition, or public health legislation
  • Excellent spoken and written English
  • Knowledgeable in computer

Full TOR Availability Notice

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) will be made available upon request. Please send your request via email to the address provided below. The contract duration is 3-6 months.

Submission of Expressions of Interest:

The National Nutrition Agency (NaNA), through the Central Project Coordination Unit (CPCU) of the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs, now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated February 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Duration of Assignment

This is a part-time work assignment, in line with the project timeline; A contract (part-time with a total of 144 days in and year and a maximum of 20 days per month) will initially be signed for two years with a performance based extension every two years thereafter, until 2030. The CC’s services shall be subject to an annual performance evaluation based on performance indicators specified in the Terms of Reference below. Performance evaluation shall be the basis for the extension or termination of the services. The selected CC is expected to work in his/her home country and will be supported by the PMU based in Suva, Fiji.

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges, and foster collaboration and cooperation in the pursuit of shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.  The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

Participating Countries

The Pacific Island Countries (PICs) participating in the regional project comprise Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu

Overall Project Objective

The Project development Objective is to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries

Project Length

August 2024 to September 30 2030

2. Project Background

The Pacific Island Forum Secretariat (PIFS) is expecting to receive financing from the World Bank (WB) Group’s International Development Association (IDA) for a proposed project to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in Pacific Island Countries (PICs).  The PICs covered by the proposed regional project (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) include diverse island economies facing similar correspondent banking relationship challenges.

PICs range in size and topography – from small island states such as Samoa, with two principal inhabited volcanic islands, to large archipelagos such as the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), with 29 atolls spread over 2 million km2 of ocean. Population sizes vary from 11,300 people in Tuvalu to 930,000 people in Fiji.

The economic landscape of PICs is equally diverse, marked by different growth drivers, poverty rates, and growth trajectories. The average GDP growth across PICs decelerated to 3.5 percent in 2023 after a historically high of 7.9 percent in 2022, in a rebound from the COVID-19 crisis. However, medium-term growth prospects have worsened, with output growth expected to be significantly below the pre-pandemic trend of 4.7 percent between 2014 & 2019. Given low growth and limited employment opportunities in the island economies, labor migration to neighboring countries and the resulting remittances are critical drivers of living standards.

The United States, New Zealand, and Australia account for 94 percent of the Pacific diaspora. Trade and tourism are vital for many PICs, providing revenue and employment opportunities. Remittances, equivalent to more than 40 percent of GDP in some PICs, are a buffer against income shocks and an important source of finance for essential household consumption and human capital investment.

Financial systems in PICs are characterized by low levels of financial access and an uneven development of national payment systems. Both domestically owned and multinational commercial banks dominate the financial sector in all PICs.  In several PICs, much of the population lacks access to basic transaction accounts, limiting households and businesses’ ability to send and receive payments, save, invest, and respond to climatic and economic shocks. The financial market infrastructure is underdeveloped, in part due to limited competition and the lack of economies of scale. The level of national payment system development is uneven across PICs, and regional efforts to improve the efficiency of cross-border payments are limited in scale and scope.

PICs are uniquely vulnerable to the withdrawal of the correspondent banking relationships (CBR) that underpin international trade, tourism, remittances, and humanitarian financial flows. Correspondent banking is an arrangement under which one bank (correspondent) holds deposits owned by other banks (respondents) and provides payment and other services to those respondent banks. CBRs are an essential feature of the global payment system – they enable individuals, businesses, and governments to make and receive cross-border payment services related to remittances, e-commerce, trade, and official sector flows. The cross-border transactions enabled in PICs are in various currencies, primarily the US dollar, Euro, and Australian dollar.

The withdrawal of CBRs, a well-documented global phenomenon affecting many emerging markets and developing economies, has adverse consequences and negative externalities for Pacific Islanders, including seasonal laborers, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and vulnerable populations. Based on publicly available data, the number of active correspondents for Pacific banks has declined significantly since 2011 to levels that put the Pacific financial system overall at risk.

In order to mitigate the issues identified above, the WB will provide funding to the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) to implement the proposed “Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project”.  The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges and foster collaboration and cooperation in pursuing shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources, and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members' shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance, and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.    The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions, and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

The project will have two components: (1) Temporary correspondent banking services and (2) Enabling environment and regulatory harmonization.  The proposed project will be implemented by a Project Management Unit (PMU) within the PIFS with strategic project oversight provided by a Project Steering Committee (PSC) comprised of representatives of participating Pacific Finance Ministers. While the PMU will be responsible for day-to-day project activities, it will need to ensure close collaboration and coordination with participating Ministries of Finance, which will oversee project activities and approve work plans through the PSC.

Comprising of Secretaries of Finance or other officials from the participating PICs finance ministries and the PIFS Director (Programs and Initiative), the PSC will meet on a quarterly basis and be responsible for the approval of key project activities as needed. The PSC will report to Pacific Finance Ministers annually at the Forum Economic Minister Meeting (FEMM) to ensure that strategic guidance and orientation are provided over the project activities. At the technical level, each participating PIC will be required to nominate a competent   government official as a Country Focal Point (CFP) responsible for project coordination at the national level, who will be designated as the point of contact with the PMU and the WB team.

The competent government official in each PIC will be complemented by a country coordinator (CC) based in-country, recruited through the PMU, and responsible for coordinating service delivery at the individual country level.

The PIFS is now seeking qualified and competent national consultants from each member country to be the country coordinator (CC) for the PMU and based in the respective participating Pacific Island countries (PICs).  The required positions are expected to be selected by the PIFS in accordance with the WB’s ‘Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers’ (Procurement Regulations), Seventh edition, September 2025, and as amended over time.

3. Objective of the Position

The main objective of the CC would be to provide on the ground support to the PMU in managing and coordinating the full range of project, country specific activities. The CC will be funded by the project (through the PMU) and report to the PIFS/ PMU Coordinator.  In addition, he/she will work closely with the specific Country Focal Point (CFP), a government official appointed by the MOF of that particular PIC.

 

 

4. Scope of Services

The CC will be required to adopt a flexible approach to coordinate and facilitate the required country specific project activities and report on tangible outcomes in terms of project implementation progress. The CC will be required to work in a pro-active manner, and to help ensure effective implementation of activities and delivery of outputs in a timely manner.

The selected CC will undertake the following services:

  1. Liaising with PICs Ministry of Finance’s CFP and Central Bank on country specific project related activities, including follow up on the Project Steering Committee (PSC) meetings and preparing meeting minutes as required;
  2. Work in close coordination with the CFP in developing the annual country specific activities, budgets to be submitted to the PIFS/PMU;
  3. Follow up closely on all country specific procurement activities to ensure that there are no delays in the selection process;
  4. In coordination with the CFP, identifying problems/impediments promptly as they arise during project implementation and take timely remedial actions;
  5. Monitoring, with assistance of the PMU M&E specialist, the progress of the country specific project activities and its results indicators;
  6. Follow up closely on all country specific financial management activities to ensure that there are no delays in the payment process;
  7. Follow up closely on the country specific activities and report to the CFP and the PMU Project Coordinator;
  8. Work closely with the CFP and review reports/outputs prepared by selected consultants and provide inputs to the CFP as required;
  9. Prepare the required documentation for the payment of outputs prepared by the selected consultants, obtain CFP approval and submit documents to the PMU for payment;
  10. Work closely with the CFP in preparing annual reports on country specific activities to be submitted to the MOF and PIFS; and
  11. Any other activities as requested by the CFP or the PMU Project Coordinator.

 

5. Reporting Obligations

The CC will attend scheduled virtual meetings with the PMU and provide weekly reports on work done.

6. Institutional Arrangements

This is a part-time work assignment, with the Consultant expected to be based in in their home country. The Consultant will be supported by the PIFS PMU based in Suva, Fiji but will work closely with and report to the country focal person in the first instance. The CC is expected to show flexibility in working arrangements as time inputs will fluctuate based on country requirements. The work will be part-time, averaging approximately 12 days per month (with a total of 144 days in and year and a maximum of 20 days per month) for the next six years. A contract will initially be signed for two years with a performance-based extension every two years thereafter. Performance evaluation shall be the basis for the extension or termination of the services. Facilities such as office space, intercom telephone facilities, personal computers, printing facilities, Internet access and stationery shall be the responsibility of the Country Coordinator.

 

7. Performance Indicators

The following performance indicators shall be used for performance assessment:

  1. Positive progress and good performance of the entrusted project activities, as per the TOR;
  2. Ensuring that WB processes and procedures are complied with in all activities and in accordance with the POM;
  3. Provide and maintain strategic engagement, networking and collaboration with key stakeholders;
  4. Ensure the utilization and management of project funds are in compliance with the Financing Agreement;
  5. Ensure the collection of all data required to track project progress;
  6. Ensure the project monitoring and reporting timeline is adhered to;
  7. Prepare and compile periodic semi-annual and annual reports on project activities
  8. Compile proposed annual workplan for the following year with budget and procurement plan;
  9. Positive evaluation of performance by the PIFS and the WB team;
  10. Effective management of other experts engaged by the PMU; and
  11. Support in implementing any capacity building agendas related to the Project as required.

 

8. Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

The CC undertakes to comply with PIF’s and WB’s policies and rules with regard to anti-corruption and prevention of fraudulent practices, conflict of interest and confidentiality. The CC shall maintain confidentiality on all sensitive information obtained during the assignment and shall not publish wholly or in part the findings or such information, without prior written consent by the PIF. Any draft reports and other documents produced by the consultant will be discussed and cleared with the PIF and the WB before their final issue. A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) will be signed between the PIFS and the selected candidate to be attached to the contract.
