procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

NIGERIA

DISTRIBUTION SECTOR RECOVERY PROGRAM (DISREP)

CREDIT NO: 9206-NG

PROJECT ID No. P172891

Date: 14th September, 2026

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: Consultancy Services to Guide DisCos Submission of End-to-End Feeder Upgrade Project for DISREP

REFERENCE NO.: DREP-CQS-7A, 8A, 9A & 10A

The Federal Government of Nigeria has applied for financing from the World Bank through the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Distribution Sector Recovery Program (DISREP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. This assignment is to support DisCos in the preparation of technically sound, financially viable end-to-end feeder upgrade project submissions under DISREP. Qualified firms shall be invited to bid for services specified under. Firms may bid for all the lots, but no firm can win more than one lot.

The assignment is divided into the following lots;

  • Lot 1: Abuja, Kaduna and Kano
  • Lot 2: Jos and Yola
  • Lot 3: Eko, Ibadan and Ikeja
  • Lot 4: Benin, Enigu and Port Harcourt

The consulting services (“the Services”) include:

  • Feeder portfolio review and ranking based on Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA)
  • Standardized Technical Specifications and Bill of Engineering Measurement and Evaluation (BEME)
  • Costing and Benchmarking

The approximate effort level for the assignment is Four (4) Calendar months.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be accessed at TCN website.

The Transmission Company of Nigeria-Project Management Unit (TCN-PMU) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. General Experience: The Firm’s general experience and overall competence, including the relevance of the firm’s area of core business to the assignment envisaged;
  2. Relevant Assignment Experience: Firm’s experience implementing loss reduction and performance improvement projects for at least one Nigerian power distribution company.
  3. Technical and Institutional Capacity: Firm’s experience developing standardized frameworks, templates and toolkits for project preparation and review.
  4. Managerial Capacity: Firm’s experience managing large multi-year consulting assignments with multiple stakeholders.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th Edition (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultants Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 0900 to 1700 hours].

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 28th September, 2026

CONTRATAÇÃO DE CONSULTOR PARA ESTUDO ECONOMÉTRICO SOBRE DINÂMICA EMPRESARIAL E EMPREGO FORMAL EM MOÇAMBIQUE (CEMPRE, IAE E FUE)

  1. O Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE) recebeu uma subvenção da Associação Internacional de Desenvolvimento (AID), instituição do Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto Regional de Estatísticas da SADC (PRESADC), e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para a contratação de um(a) Consultor(a) Individual – Especialista em Análise Econométrica de Dinâmica Empresarial e Emprego Formal.
  2. Os serviços de consultoria (“Serviços”) visam analisar econometricamente os determinantes da geração de emprego formal em Moçambique, com base na dinâmica das empresas formais identificadas no Censo de Empresas (CEMPRE 14/15 e 2025/26), no Inquérito Anual às Empresas (IAE) e no Ficheiro de Unidades Estatísticas (FUE), reforçando a capacidade técnica do INE em análise e modelação econométrica, em apoio ao processo de tratamento e análise de dados dos sectores institucionais das Contas Nacionais. Mais detalhes sobre os serviços e as responsabilidades da consultoria encontram-se nos Termos de Referência (TdR).
  3. Os requisitos de qualificação incluem: formação académica ao nível de Mestrado ou Doutoramento em Economia, Econometria, Estatística ou áreas afins; experiência comprovada em análise económica, com particular enfoque em dados microeconómicos, empresariais ou administrativos; familiaridade com o uso de estatísticas oficiais; produção científica relevante em áreas relacionadas com inflação, preços ou economia do desenvolvimento; domínio de ferramentas como Stata, EViews, R ou SPSS; e experiência em transferência de conhecimentos e capacitação técnica.
  4. O Contrato terá duração de 7 (sete) semanas, a partir da data de celebração do contrato.
  5. Os(as) candidatos(as) interessados(as) e com o perfil requerido deverão submeter os seguintes documentos: Carta de Manifestação de Interesse, Curriculum Vitae, em língua portuguesa, cópias dos diplomas ou certificados de habilitações académicas, lista de publicações e/ou relatórios técnicos relevantes, e indicação de três (3) referências profissionais que poderão ser contactadas no processo de avaliação.
  6. As candidaturas deverão ser entregues até às 15:00 horas do dia 29 de Setembro de 2026 no endereço Instituto Nacional de Estatística – Avenida 24 de Julho nº1989, Piso 09- Sala 0901, Cidade de Maputo. Email: presadc.concursos@gmail.com
  7. O consultor será seleccionado de acordo com os procedimentos do Banco Mundial definidos no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projectos de Investimento, 6.ª edição, Fevereiro de 2025, particularmente os parágrafos 7.36 – 7.37 sobre Selecção de Consultores Individuais. Os interessados devem prestar particular atenção na Secção III, parágrafos 3.15 a 3.17 do mesmo Regulamento, política sobre conflito de interesse.
  8. Os Termos de Referência e outros detalhes sobre a consultoria poderão ser obtidos no endereço acima e também estão disponíveis em www.ine.gov.mz/concursos. Somente o(a) candidato(a) mais qualificado(a) será convidado(a) a apresentar proposta técnica e financeira e a proceder à negociação do contrato.

                                                   (CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR ENGAGEMENT OF MONITORING BIODIVERSITY MANAGEMENT FOR THE ON-GOING CONSTRUCTION OF IRINGA – MSEMBE ROAD (104 KM) AND LAKE MANYARA AIRPORT UNDER THE TANZANIA TRANSPORT INTEGRATED PROJECT (TANTIP) SUB PROJECT; Tender No.; TR36/CCP/P165660/2026/2027/C/18

The Government of the United Republic of Tanzania has received a credit from the World Bank towards the cost of the Tanzania Transport Integration Project (TanTIP) which amongst others, comprises the upgrading of Iringa – Msembe (104 km) road and rehabilitation and improvement of Lake Manyara Airport. The Government, through Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS) intends to apply part of the credit proceeds to eligible payments under Contract for Consultancy Services for undertaking monitoring of the implementation of the Biodiversity Management Plan during construction works of the Iringa – Msembe road and Lake – Manyara Airport for which these Terms of Reference are issued.

The ongoing infrastructure development projects (road and airport) pass through or are adjacent to Biodiversity Important Areas with critical habitats for wildlife bird species of ecological importance. Thus, a qualified individual consultant or a firm is required to undertake biodiversity monitoring and management for ongoing construction works for the upgrading and rehabilitation of Iringa – Msembe road (104 km) and rehabilitation and improvements of Lake Manyara Airport.

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment are available on the following website www.tanroads.go.tz.
  2. The Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS) an Executive Agency of the Ministry of Works and Transport hereby invites Applicants to show their interest in delivering the Services described in the Terms of Reference.
  3. This Request for Expressions of Interest is open to: Individual Consultants.
  4. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Such information may include updated detailed CV duly signed and copies of academic, testimonial, and professional certificates. The interested Consultants should have the following qualifications and experiences
  5. Education
  6. He/She shall be a holder of first degree in Ecology, Wildlife Conservation or Forestry Conservation or Natural Resource Management or Conservation Biologist or any other related discipline. A postgraduate qualification in Ecology or Wildlife Management or Natural Resources Management is an added advantage.
  7. Professional experience
  8. He/she must have a minimum of Ten (10) years of cumulative experience related to Biodiversity Monitoring Management and Natural Resource Management Conservation.
  9. Regional experience and Language and requirements
  1. He/she must have at least three (3) years working experience in Developing Countries; and
  2. He/she must be proficient in both written and spoken English and Swahili Languages.
  1. Government employees under Short-terms or Permanent Contract need not apply, as they are not eligible to participate in the selection process. Expressions of Interest from government employees will be eliminated from the selection process.
  2. The attention of interested individual consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seven Edition, September, 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  3. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seven Edition September, 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”) and Public Procurement Act No. 10 of 2023 and Public Procurement Regulations GN No. 518 of 2024 on “procedures for selection and employment of consultants.
  4. Expressions of Interest must be submitted through National e-Procurement System of Tanzania (NeST) (www.nest.go.tz) on or before 25th September, 2026 at 10:00 Hours East African Time. The Client shall not be held liable for any delays due to system failure beyond its control. Even though the system will attempt to notify the Consultants of any updates, the Client shall not be liable for any information not received by the bidder. It is the Consultants’ responsibility to verify the website for the latest information related to this selection process. Expression of Interests will be opened promptly thereafter through NeST.
  5. Any request for clarification with regard to this assignment shall be addressed through NeST not less than five (5) days before submission deadline. The Employer shall respond to clarifications received within three (3) working days from the date of receipt of the query. Expression of Interest not received through NeST shall not be evaluated irrespective of the circumstances
  6. Interested Applicants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours: 08:30 -16:30 local time on Mondays to Fridays inclusive except on Public Holidays.

procnotices.project_name: Fiji Tourism Development Program in Vanua Levu
procnotices.bid_description: TLTB Capacity Building Program
procnotices.contact_address: Levels 2 and 3, Victoria Parade Suva
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Name of Project

Fiji Tourism Development Program in Vanua Levu or ‘Na Vualiku’

Loan Number

IDA-73690

Assignment Title

Consulting Services for Institutional Capability Development and Operational Strengthening for iTaukei Land Trust Board

Reference Number

FJ-MTCA-545892-CS-QCBS

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

The Government of Fiji through the Ministry of Finance, Strategic Planning, National Development and Statistics has received financing from the World Bank (“WB”) for the Fiji Tourism Development Program in Vanua Levu or ‘Na Vualiku’ and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will support the Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation (“MTCA”) as the lead Implementing Agency, in technical partnership with the iTaukei Land Trust Board (“TLTB”) as the beneficiary institution, to undertake comprehensive institutional capability development and operational strengthening.

The primary purpose of the assignment is to strengthen the institutional capacity, operational readiness, and technical effectiveness of TLTB in those areas most relevant to tourism-related iTaukei land development in the Northern Division so that TLTB is equipped to manage the increased volume and complexity of work the project will generate, and to do so in a way that is efficient, transparent, and genuinely beneficial to iTaukei landowners.

The Services are expected to commence in February 2027 for an assignment duration of Sixteen (16) Months. The lump-sum contract will be signed with payment against acceptance of clearly defined milestones/ deliverables.

The detailed Terms of Reference (“TOR”) for the assignment is available by contacting Mr. Akshay Chand on Akshay.chand01@mtca.gov.fj or clicking the below link.

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vyoixSfW-Yi13ddZIJGaJ0m3J8NGoNFM/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=116864177158872071295&rtpof=true&sd=true 

The MTCA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The shortlisting criteria are:   

1. Technical experience in institutional/organizational development, functional reviews, capability development and operational strengthening - The firm shall demonstrate at least eight years of relevant corporate experience in carrying out institutional/organizational assessments or functional reviews, capacity development, institutional strengthening or closely related advisory work. The firm shall also demonstrate successful completion of at least three assignments of comparable complexity during the last ten years, incorporating a combination of capacity development, institutional diagnostic work, and preparation of practical operational tools.

2. Experience in land administration and customary land governance - Demonstrated experience in land administration support, land agencies, lease systems, land records, cadastral or spatial data functions, customary or communal land institutions, or similar land governance environments.

3. GIS, land information systems, and systems planning experience - Relevant advisory experience in reviewing spatial data environments, preparing systems roadmaps, and developing technical requirements for future systems enhancement.

4. Stakeholder engagement and context-sensitive delivery - Evidence of effective work in settings requiring structured consultation with Government, statutory bodies, community stakeholders, customary institutions, women, vulnerable groups, and other actors, preferably in Fiji, the Pacific, or similar small-island contexts.

5. Local Delivery - Firms must demonstrate a credible approach to local delivery, whether through a permanent presence in Fiji, locally-based experts, or formal arrangements with local partners that ensure sustained field engagement in Suva and Vanua Levu throughout the assignment.

6. Project management, quality assurance, and multidisciplinary delivery capability - Firms shall demonstrate internal quality assurance arrangements adequate to support multidisciplinary delivery, timely reporting, and consistent technical standards across all outputs.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (“QCBS”) method set out in the Regulations and based on the criteria set out in the TOR. Further information can be obtained at the address below.  This TOR is subject to further discussion and refinement in consultation with stakeholders to ensure comprehensive coverage and alignment with project objectives.

Expressions of interest must be uploaded using the below link before by 9th October 2026:

https://forms.gle/xmHMigphP3tifAsB6

The Consultants are advised to consult the following Guidance Note including EOI template available here:

 

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pYH1rOHTestn9nKWUpx-yXlcgNE1j1N8?usp=sharing

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES

Conducting B2B export promotion missions for Moldovan SMEs to the United Kingdom

 

REPUBLIC OF MOLDOVA

MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES COMPETITIVENESS PROJECT

Sector: General industry and trade sector

IDA Credit No. 71740

IBRD Loan No. 94230

Project ID No. P177895

Reference No. MD-CEP-566791-CS-CQS

 

The Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Competitiveness Project (MSME) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The objective of the assignment is to support the Government of the Republic of Moldova and Invest Moldova Agency in contracting a UK-based consulting firm to organize and implement 3 (three) sector-specific export missions for at least 25 (twenty-five) Moldovan SMEs with export potential in light industry, wines, and agri-food products.

The assignment aims to facilitate market entry and export growth of Moldovan SMEs through structured B2B meetings and visits in the UK with buyers, distributors, importers, retailers, specialized wine importers, fashion buyers, food retailers, HoReCa operators, and other relevant market actors. The sectors reflect UK demand for Moldovan clothes, beverages, fruit and vegetables.

The assignment will be implemented in the period November 2026 – March 2027 and shall be aligned with the export missions calendar provided in Tabel 1 from below. The Consultant shall develop and submit, at the technical and financial proposal stage, a detailed work plan to ensure the accomplishment of the proposed missions calendar.

Table 1 Target sectors, timeline and number of participants

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Project Implementation Unit of the MSME Competitiveness Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (required qualifications and experience of the firm, but not individual experts’ bio data).

This assignment requires a Consultant, which may be a consulting firm or a consortium of consulting firms, with proven local presence and operational capacity in the United Kingdom, that meets the following requirements:

  • Has a minimum of eight (8) years of relevant professional experience in export promotion, organization of B2B meetings, trade missions, and market research, demonstrated through similar assignments implemented;
  • Has demonstrated competence and experience in international trade and export promotion, including the design and application of modern export promotion instruments and tools, with a strong focus on the UK market and comparable European markets;
  • Has proven experience in the implementation of at least three (3) similar assignments during the last five (5) years, involving the organization of export missions, B2B matchmaking, and cooperation with foreign buyers and partners;
  • Has demonstrated experience in organizing study visits, company visits, and sector-specific business programs for foreign SMEs, including coordination with local companies, clusters, business associations, and relevant institutions;
  • Has sound knowledge of the economic sectors of the Republic of Moldova and their export potential, reflected through practical experience in working on SME development, export facilitation, and trade-related projects;
  • Has a team of qualified experts with relevant professional experience in export promotion, trade facilitation, B2B matchmaking, and business development;
  • Has proven prior experience in the implementation of donor-funded and/or International Financial Institutions (IFI) financed projects, including compliance with reporting and procedural requirements.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the „Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection” method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications; but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The Expression of Interest shall clearly state the name of the Consultant (individual Firm, Joint Venture or sub-consultancy). The Consultant shall provide relevant references (assignment name, Client, time frame, the role of the firm (main Consultant/Partner in JV/sub-consultant, contract amount, tasks performed etc.) to confirm its experience and qualifications.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by September 28, 2026, COB.

 

Project Implementation Unit of the World Bank MSME Competitiveness Project

180, Stefan cel Mare Ave., office 815, MD-2004, Chisinau, Republic of Moldova

Tel:  + 373 22 296-723

E-mail for submission of the clarifications: piu@mded.gov.md

E-mail for submission of the EoIs: procurementmgf@gmail.com   

Only the notification of EoI submission must be sent to piu@mded.gov.md

 

 

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Conducting B2B export promotion missions for Moldovan SMEs to the United Kingdom

(support to Invest Moldova Agency under World Bank MSME Competitiveness project)
 

A.   Background & Project Description

The Government of the Republic of Moldova (GoM) is pursuing a policy agenda aimed at supporting export-led economic growth. The MSME Competitiveness Project aims to increase the competitiveness of Moldovan enterprises by reducing the regulatory burden they face, improving access to finance, and strengthening MSME development and export competitiveness. The Project supports the digitization of government-to-business (G2B) services, which is expected to reduce compliance costs and administrative burdens for enterprises. In addition, improvements in quality infrastructure increase the availability of accredited laboratory services and reduce costs for enterprises, thereby facilitating increased exports. These measures contribute to enhancing MSME competitiveness in both domestic and international markets. The Project also provides funding for partial credit guarantees to improve MSME access to finance, as well as support for enterprises to upgrade their products and services. As a result, access to finance is expected to improve, contributing to MSME survival and growth, job creation or retention, and increased competitiveness and export performance.

The World Bank has supported the Government’s competitiveness and reform efforts through two Competitiveness Enhancement Projects (CEP I and CEP II), which were successfully completed and focused on: (i) regulatory reform; (ii) access of small and medium-sized enterprises to business development services and quality certifications through a Matching Grant Facility (MGF); (iii) access to finance through a line of credit (LoC) for exporters; and (iv) quality infrastructure, including equipment and institutional reforms in the areas of metrology, standards, testing, and quality.

Against this background, and under the support of the MSME Competitiveness Project, the Government through Invest Moldova Agency (IMA) is seeking the services of a consulting firm with proven experience in export promotion, organization of B2B meetings, supplier–buyer matchmaking, foreign market analysis, and logistical support for the organization of B2B export missions in the United Kingdom (UK).

The MSME Competitiveness Project development objectives (PDO) are to: (i) reduce the regulatory burden, increase access to finance, and enhance the export competitiveness of Moldovan enterprises; and
(ii) respond promptly and effectively in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

The PDO will be achieved through a set of activities aimed at: (a) digitizing government-to-business services and inspections, streamlining permissive documents, and strengthening national quality infrastructure; (b) supporting access to finance through credit guarantees and enhancing the capacity of the Credit Guarantee Facility (CGF); (c) supporting MSME development and enhancing export competitiveness; (d) supporting project management; and (e) supporting the Government’s response in the event of an emergency.

Context of export-led growth for Moldova

A key challenge facing the Government of the Republic of Moldova is the need to promote sustainable economic growth and job creation driven by robust private sector activity, exports, and increased investment. Export-led growth has historically delivered higher productivity, increased employment, improved trade balances, and enhanced financial stability. In line with its development agenda, the Government aims to steer the economy toward export-oriented production activities and better leverage the country’s strategic geographic position.

Against this background, and under the support of the MSME Competitiveness Project, the Government through Invest Moldova Agency (IMA) is seeking the services of a consulting firm with proven experience in export promotion, organization of B2B meetings, supplier-buyer matchmaking, foreign market analysis, and logistical support for the organization of B2B export missions.

 

C.        Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to support the Government of the Republic of Moldova and Invest Moldova Agency in contracting a UK-based consulting firm to organize and implement 3 (three) sector-specific export missions for at least 25 (twenty-five) Moldovan SMEs with export potential in light industry, wines, and agri-food products.

The assignment aims to facilitate market entry and export growth of Moldovan SMEs through structured B2B meetings and visits in the UK with buyers, distributors, importers, retailers, specialized wine importers, fashion buyers, food retailers, HoReCa operators, and other relevant market actors. The sectors reflect UK demand for Moldovan clothes, beverages, fruit and vegetables.

Table 1 Target sectors, timeline and number of participants

Total number of export missions: 3

Total estimated number of participating SMEs: minimum 25 companies

 

D.        Tasks to be performed by the Consultant (Scope of Work)

To achieve the objectives of the assignment, the Consultant shall perform the tasks described below, structured in two phases.

Phase I – Not applicable under this Contract

All Phase I tasks (assessment to identify export-ready Moldovan SMEs, workshops, market intelligence notes for selection, call for participation, eligibility and selection criteria, evaluation and selection of SMEs, and preparation of SME company profiles) shall be implemented under a separate contract with a local consulting firm in the Republic of Moldova.

At the same time, it is expected that the international contractor will provide expert input, guidance, and review throughout Phase I, particularly with regard to foreign market requirements, international buyer expectations, sector-specific trends, and market-specific insights that may not be fully available at local level.

The international contractor shall therefore support the local consulting firm through strategic advice, validation of approaches, and review of key deliverables, ensuring that the selected SMEs and prepared company profiles are aligned with the realities and standards of the targeted foreign markets.

Phase II (Organization and Implementation of Export Missions in the United Kingdom)

  1. Plan and schedule three (3) sector-specific export missions to the UK, ensuring the participation of a minimum of 7–10 SMEs per mission, based on the validated list of companies provided by the Invest Moldova Agency.
  2. Identify and engage UK-based companies and institutions relevant for each sector, including importers, distributors, retail chains, wine importers, fashion buyers, food retailers, HoReCa operators, logistics companies, and business associations.
  3. Provide Invest Moldova Agency with a list of UK partners per mission, submitted for validation at least six (6) weeks prior to each export mission. The list shall include company profiles and contact information.
  4. Organize structured B2B meetings and study visits for participating SMEs, including visits to potential partner companies, retail and distribution centers, and sector-relevant hubs.
  5. Develop and submit detailed B2B agendas and study visit schedules no later than four (4) weeks prior to each mission.
  6. Prepare and provide participating SMEs with individual information packages, including partner profiles, meeting agendas, and itineraries.
  7. Conduct pre-mission briefings covering UK business practices, sector trends, regulatory requirements (food safety/labelling, wine trade rules, textile labelling/product compliance, customs procedures, and rules of origin, where applicable), cultural aspects, mission logistics, and rules of conduct.
  8. Facilitate the implementation of export missions, ensuring a minimum of five (5) structured business interactions per SME.
  9. Organize post-mission feedback sessions and assist SMEs in identifying follow-up actions.

This work shall be carried out in close cooperation with the ODA internationalization program. The Invest Moldova Agency shall coordinate closely with ODA, as applicable, in line with export readiness programs, the Matching Grants Facility (MGF), and supplier linkage initiatives.

E.        Outcomes and Goals

The following outcomes and goals are expected to be achieved through the implementation of the assignment:

  • Successful organization and implementation of three (3) export missions to the UK;
  • Participation of at least 7–10 Moldovan SMEs per mission;
  • Structured B2B meetings and study visits for all participating companies;
  • Minimum five (5) business interactions per SME;
  • At least 15% of participating SMEs initiating export transactions within 12 months after mission completion;
  • Increased visibility and market presence of Moldovan companies on the UK market.

F.         Deliverables

The Consultant is expected to develop and submit the following deliverables:

  • List of UK companies identified and validated as potential B2B partners for the export missions, incluing company profiles and contact information;
  • Concept notes, agendas, presentations, and information kits for pre-mission briefings, focusing on business practices and opportunities on the UK market;
  • Individual B2B meeting schedules and information packages for each participating Moldovan SME, including profiles of UK partner companies and tailored itineraries and study visits;
  • Post-mission reports summarizing the implementation of each export mission, including qualitative feedback and assessment of results;
  • Results of participant satisfaction surveys conducted after each export mission;
  • Confirmation that no promotional or branding materials other than those provided by the Invest Moldova Agency are used or distributed during briefings, or B2B meetings.

G.        Inputs from key players

Invest Moldova Agency, in coordination with the Organization for Entrepreneurial Development (ODA), shall provide the following support to the Consultant:

  • Provide the validated list of participating SMEs and their company profiles (English), prepared under the separate Phase I contract;
  • Ensure overall institutional coordination and oversight throughout the preparation and implementation of the export missions;
  • Review and validate the list of UK partners and key deliverables.

The beneficiary companies participating in the export missions shall be responsible for covering the following costs:

  • International and local travel costs to and from the country of destination;
  • Accommodation and per diem expenses for the duration of the export missions.

The Consultant (UK consulting firm) shall be responsible for covering the following costs and activities:

  • Identification, engagement, and coordination with local business partners, including importers, distributors, buyers, clusters, and relevant institutions;
  • Organization and facilitation of structured B2B meetings and study visits for participating companies;
  • Provision of local logistical support, including coordination of meeting venues, site visits, and mission-related activities;
  • Organization of conference and meeting spaces for briefings, including all necessary equipment (laptops, multimedia projectors, screens, microphones, etc.), as well as coffee breaks, where applicable;
  • Preparation of reports, documentation of results, and provision of follow-up support to participating companies.

 

H.        Reports & Reporting Arrangement

The results of the assignment will be presented in a series of reports related to the export missions covered under this contract, containing a detailed description of the fulfillment of the tasks foreseen under Clause D (Scope of Work).

The Consultant shall produce the following reports:

1st Progress Report. This report shall present the Consultant’s progress, findings, and deliverables related to the preparation and planning activities under Phase II, including the list of UK partners submitted for validation. The report shall be submitted within six (6) weeks after the contract effectiveness.

2nd Progress Report. This report shall present the Consultant’s progress and deliverables related to finalization of B2B agendas, schedules, information packages, and pre-mission briefing preparation under Phase II. The report shall be submitted within eleven (11) weeks after the contract effectiveness.

3rd Progress Report. These reports shall cover the Consultant’s progress and deliverables related to the implementation of export missions, including B2B meeting schedules, organization of study visits, information packages for participating SMEs, and the report on each conducted export mission. Reports shall be submitted for each export mission conducted, as applicable.

4th Progress Report. These reports shall present the assessment of results achieved, participant feedback, and follow-up activities implemented after each export mission, in line with the Scope of Work. Reports shall be submitted after the completion of each mission, as applicable.

The Invest Moldova Agency, ODA, the World Bank project team, and other relevant stakeholders may provide comments on the submitted deliverables, which shall be addressed by the Consultant accordingly.

All deliverables shall be provided in electronic format, and in hard copy upon request. The working languages for all reports shall be Romanian and English.

The Consultant will act under the supervision of and shall coordinate the progress status with the Invest Moldova Agency and the PIU. The Consultant shall coordinate the reports/deliverables with the Invest Moldova Agency, the PIU and other stakeholders as applicable.

I.          Period and terms of the Assignment 

The assignment is expected to be implemented in the period November 2026 – March 2027 and shall be aligned with the export missions calendar provided in Tabel 1 of these ToRs. The Consultant shall develop and submit, at the technical and financial proposal stage, a detailed work plan to ensure the accomplishment of the proposed missions calendar.

J.         Requirements for the assignment

This assignment requires a Consultant, which may be a consulting firm or a consortium of consulting firms, with proven local presence and operational capacity in the United Kingdom, that meets the following requirements:

  • Has a minimum of eight (8) years of relevant professional experience in export promotion, organization of B2B meetings, trade missions, and market research, demonstrated through similar assignments implemented;
  • Has demonstrated competence and experience in international trade and export promotion, including the design and application of modern export promotion instruments and tools, with a strong focus on the UK market and comparable European markets;
  • Has proven experience in the implementation of at least three (3) similar assignments during the last five (5) years, involving the organization of export missions, B2B matchmaking, and cooperation with foreign buyers and partners;
  • Has demonstrated experience in organizing study visits, company visits, and sector-specific business programs for foreign SMEs, including coordination with local companies, clusters, business associations, and relevant institutions;
  • Has sound knowledge of the economic sectors of the Republic of Moldova and their export potential, reflected through practical experience in working on SME development, export facilitation, and trade-related projects;
  • Has a team of qualified experts with relevant professional experience in export promotion, trade facilitation, B2B matchmaking, and business development;
  • Has proven prior experience in the implementation of donor-funded and/or International Financial Institutions (IFI) financed projects, including compliance with reporting and procedural requirements.

 

 

K.        Terms of payment

The Contract will be a lump-sum contract for small assignments in accordance with the World Bank procedures. The tentative payment schedule is as follows:

  • 15% of the contract amount, upon acceptance of the 1st progress report;
  • 20% of the contract amount, upon acceptance of the 2nd progress report;
  • 50% of the contract amount, upon acceptance of reports for each completed export mission, including B2B meetings/visits;
  • 15% of the contract amount, upon acceptance of the 4th progress report.

The payments under the contract will be made by the PIU upon approval of the reports by the Invest Moldova Agency.

  1. The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (GoB) has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the ACCESS – Bangladesh Phase 1 Project, under which the remaining activities of the Bangladesh Regional Waterway Transport Project-1 (BRWTP-1) are being implemented by the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) of Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA) under the Ministry of Shipping, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
  2. The consulting services (“Services”) involve the engagement of a single Consultant to take over and complete the supervision, as Project Manager, of six remaining works contracts at sixteen sites: Pangaon Cargo Terminal, Narayanganj and Chandpur Passenger Terminals, and thirteen landing stations/launch ghats (estimated works value Tk 36,275.86 Lac). The Services cover construction supervision, contract administration, quality assurance, and environmental, social, health, and safety supervision. The Services will last 18 months, are expected to commence in January 2027, and will not extend beyond 30 June 2028.
  3. BIWTA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience. The shortlisting criteria are: (a) General experience of the firm (core business and years in business) in the construction supervision of civil engineering works; (b) relevant experience in supervising works of similar nature, size and complexity (waterway terminals, ports, jetties, landing stations or comparable marine infrastructure) as Engineer/Project Manager under FIDIC or comparable conditions, including environmental and social supervision, preferably in Bangladesh or comparable riverine conditions on development partner-financed assignments; and (c) technical and managerial capability of the firm. 4. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Fourth Edition, November 2020) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. 5. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications, and should indicate clearly the form of association. In a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. In the case of an association, the consultants must explain in their EOI submission: (a) the rationale for forming the association; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each joint venture member in carrying out the assignment, thereby justifying the proposed inclusion of each member in the association. Failure to provide this explanation in the Expression of Interest may result in the association not being shortlisted for the assignment.

1.1. Context

The Regional Organization for Conservation of the Marine Environment of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden (PERSGA) is an intergovernmental organization established since 1995. PERSGA institutional framework is based on the Regional Convention for the Conservation of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden Environment (Jeddah Convention 1982), which joins seven member states, including Djibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, and Yemen. Rational use of marine resources and the protection of coastal marine environment from pollution and overexploitation are central objectives of Jeddah Convention (1982) and its derived Action Plan Regional Protocols and Action Plan. PERSGA runs regional programs and projects that support regional capacities and coordination to achieve these objectives.

This consultancy is carried out in the framework of the implementation of the regional project “Sustainable Fisheries Development in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden”, referred to hereafter as SFISH project. The project is financed by the World Bank (WB), and executed by PERSGA for its regional component. In accordance with the M&E policies and procedures of WB, a Final Evaluation of the SFISH project is required.  The project has started on August 2022 and is approaching its closing by March 2027. This TOR sets out the prospect for the project Final Evaluation.

1.2 Background on SFISH project (Regional Component)

PERSGA is executing the SFISH project Regional Component, which composes the subject of this Final Evaluation TOR. This Component aims to strengthen regional collaboration in management of marine fisheries and aquaculture in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Its focus is to improve and sustain regional collaboration through further development of PERSGA’s capacities for monitoring, assessment, knowledge management and sharing to support science-based management of fisheries in the RSGA. It supports the development of a regional platform for coordination of policies, legislation, management plans and measures for responsible fisheries and aquaculture and use of ecosystems approaches. It also supports regional level capacity building and technical assistance program on management of living marine resources responding to both anthropogenic and climate induced changes. This would include training, providing technical guidelines, support the development of policies, legislation, management plans and completion, ratification and implementation of relevant regional conventions, action plans and protocols. The project regional component interventions were designed to be through the following interlinked subcomponents:

  1. PERSGA Regional Information Management System (RIMS), monitoring network and institutional capacity. This subcomponent aims to strengthen the capacity of PERSGA, as a regional organization, to compile fisheries and related data collected or received from the countries and make this information available to all member states. It provides goods and services to improve IT hardware and software of the RIMS housed in PERSGA, and networking to allow it to perform integrated functions. The subcomponent also supports PERSGA system capacity for monitoring marine environment, including on climate change impact in the RSGA area, tracking pollution spills, and coordination of emergency response that have implications to protection of fisheries and their critical habitats. It also supports updating PERSGA institutional guidelines as needed, such as for finance and procurement policy and procedures, project cycle management, and environmental and social risks assessment and management.
  2. Regional platforms for capacity building and regional coordination of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in the regional management mechanism. This subcomponent supports capacity development, technical assistance and setting up of platforms for effective coordination on fishery management at the regional level. It supports PERSGA to develop technical manuals for cost-effective approaches of harmonized fisheries data and information collection and management adapted to the region, incorporating supplementary guidelines for monitoring, and assessing IUU fishing, fish stock status etc., and a regional mechanism to share information with member states on fishery statistics and knowledge. It will also support PERSGA to develop technical guidelines to promote capacities to effectively coordinate efforts for fisheries management, policies, and legislation; protection and restoration of critical fish habitat; environmental and biosecurity best practices in aquaculture, building climate resilience and regional mechanism to interact with relevant international efforts. The activity will also include support to PERSGA in developing a Regional Plan of Action for combating IUU fishing (RPOA-IUU), and other specific action plans concerning conservation of vulnerable non target species such as sharks, turtles, seabirds and marine mammals. These action plans would provide an umbrella mechanism for cooperation and coordination of measures to combat IUU fishing, and other conservation measures related to RSGA fisheries.
  3. Enhanced knowledge management, communication strategies and awareness for citizen, private sector and development partner engagement in the regional sustainable fishery mechanism. This subcomponent includes technical assistance, consultations, and operating costs for supporting citizen, private sector and development partner engagement and raising awareness through effective communication on regional cooperation actions, including improved activities that demonstrate cooperation and coordination among the regional countries. It also supports the development of special awareness activities, including production and dissemination of educational materials (videos, media toolkits, brochures, pamphlets, etc.) addressing fishery issues due to anthropogenic actions and climate change, and communication workshops to enhance their engagement.

Further detailed information on the project, and related project documents can be reached at the following link: https://sfish.persga.org/

  1. Consultancy

2.1 Objectives of the Final Evaluation (FE)

The objective of the FE is to provide an independent assessment of the project’s achievements, outcomes and potential longer-term impacts. As an end-of-project evaluation undertaken during the final implementation period, the FE will assess performance over the implementation period up to an evaluation cut-off date agreed during inception, with material implementation developments and final results updated through completion of the evaluation where any evidence becomes available. It will consider forward-looking in capturing lessons learned and providing evidence on the nature and extent of results, their likely sustainability, and implications for future programming.

The evaluation will thus assess the project design, scope, implementation and achievements. It will collate and analyse lessons learnt, challenges faced and best practices obtained during implementation, which will inform the next programming strategy in response to its priorities, and make recommendations regarding the specific actions in this regard. These should emphasize, for example issues to be addressed in the future follow up interventions, significant outcomes and success stories for potential expansion and replication. 

2.2 Scope and Approach of the FE

The FE should provide evidence-based information that is credible, reliable and useful. The consultant is expected to follow a participatory and consultative approach ensuring close engagement with the Project team at PERSGA, and government counterparts of the member countries including PERSGA Focal Points, National Coordinators of the project, and key stakeholders. The review consultant is expected to conduct a field mission to view project interventions and achievements, and partake in meetings and workshop organized in the framework of the FE process. Interviews will be held with the following organizations and individuals at a minimum:

    • PERSGA staff who have project responsibilities;
    • Project National Coordinators
    • Stakeholders, including the beneficiaries in at least two of the Participating Countries,

The consultant will review all relevant sources of information, such as the project documents, project implementation progress reports, financial reports, activities’ reports, strategic and legal documents, World Bank aide memoires from support meetings, outputs and products and any other material that he / she considers useful for this evidence-based review and evaluation.

The FE shall review and validate the project's Theory of Change (ToC). In this connection, the evaluation shall assess whether the assumptions and causal pathways underlying project design remained valid during implementation, and examine the extent to which project interventions, outputs, and intermediate results contributed to the achievement of intended outcomes and development objectives. The assessment should identify key enabling factors and constraints that influenced results achievement and sustainability.

The Project FE will assess the effectiveness of the implementation strategy and the results. This will include the implementation modalities, responsibilities and co-financing roles, coordination and partnership arrangements, institutional strengthening, beneficiary participation, training and workshop attendance and outcomes, replication and sustainability of the project outcomes. The evaluation will include review of the project design and assumptions made at the beginning of the project development process; project management including the implementation strategies; project activities, so as to assess the extent to which the project results have been achieved, partnerships established, capacities built, and cross cutting issues of mainstreaming development issues. It will also assess whether the project implementation strategy has been optimum and recommend areas for improvement and learning for future programming interventions.

To achieve the FE objectives following relevant World Bank and PERSGA guidelines, the consultant will consider the following categories of project performance. For each of the Relevance, Efficacy and Efficiency categories, and for the overall assessment, the consultant is required to apply the rating scales set out below. The sustainability and risks to development outcomes will be assessed descriptively, i.e. rating is not required; however, the main risks and enabling factors should be clearly identified and prioritized.

      1. Relevance

The FE will assess the extent to which the project objectives, design and focus are relevant to the identified problem and needs. It will also assess how the project interventions approached are realistic, appropriate, and responsive to changes for achieving project objectives. Thus, the Relevance of objectives assesses: (i) the alignment with the partnership framework of the World Bank and PERSGA  and pertaining development strategy at the time the operation is closed; (ii) appropriateness of the PDO given the client’s implementation capacity; and (iii) the extent to which the PDO was responsive to the changing circumstances. The explanation of the alignment of the PDO includes a description of the development problem the project sought to address and how this problem was addressed through the project’s interventions given the context and existing capacity.

Rating:  Considering the above, the Relevance of PDO will be rated using a four-point scale, including High, Substantial, Modest, and Negligible, as follows

 

High:

Full alignment with the priorities of the regional framework and development strategy; PDO was appropriately pitched and responsive to changing circumstances 

Substantial:

Largely aligned with the priorities of the regional framework and development strategy, with minor shortcomings in appropriateness or responsiveness.

Modest:

Partial alignment with the priorities of the regional framework and development strategy, or notable shortcomings in appropriateness or responsiveness

Negligible:

Very limited alignment with the priorities of the regional framework and development strategy, with major shortcomings in appropriateness or responsiveness

2.2.2 Efficacy

Assessing the project Efficacy is the core section in this Final Evaluation, as well as in the Learning and Results Note (LRN) for Investment Project Financing Operation of the World Bank. Efficacy is defined as the extent to which the project objectives were achieved, or are expected to be achieved, and that achievement is attributable to the activities or actions supported by the project, or to what extent the project’s activities contributed to the achievement of the objective(s). The PDO statement conveys the benefits (changes) expected to flow to the beneficiaries, expressed in terms of development outcomes, rather than stating financed activities and outputs.  Thus, to examine the project Efficacy, the FE will consider several aspects, such as:

  • Achievement of the Project development objectives: including through Results Framework (RF) Indicators, outputs and outcomes assessments. The RF can provide logical information to measure achievement of each expected outcome in the PDO statement through examining data on indicators document, observed achievements and compare them to baselines and targets.  However, it is important to assess efficacy at the level of expected outcomes rather than just presenting data of the project’s results indicators. It will be useful to also look beyond the Results Framework to any other available data and evidence. Where applicable, the efficacy section would also discuss here achievement of cross-cutting and corporate objectives, such as contribution to institutional strengthening and other development objectives (e.g. relevant SDGs
  • Project management performance by PERSGA: including through assessing management processes and appropriateness in supporting implementation and delivering results; Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) quality assessment; implementation strategies; responding to the needs of the beneficiaries; involving stakeholders; adaptive management to overcome obstacles/challenges, or grasping opportunity to upscale/ expand results;

Rating:  Considering the above, the project Efficacy will be rated using a four-point scale, including High, Substantial, Modest, and Negligible, as follows:

High:

The Project fully achieved or exceeded its objectives (or intended outcomes) or is likely to do so

Substantial:

The Project almost fully achieved its objectives (or intended outcomes) or is likely to do so

Modest:

The Project partly achieved its objectives (or intended outcomes) or is likely to do so

Negligible:

The Project barely achieved its objectives (or intended outcomes) or is likely to do so

2.2.3 Efficiency

The FE will assess the efficiency of the project implementation with regard to:

  • Utilizing the fund resources, where actual/ expected results justify costs incurred;
  • Synergy and coordination with other overlapping and similar interventions (funded nationally and /or by other donors);
  • Considering collaboration with the national institutions and development partners;
  • Management structures, procedure and accountability;
  • Performance in project management, coordination, procurement and financial management, reporting, stakeholder engagement, and responsiveness to implementation challenges.

Rating:  Considering the above, the project Efficiency will be rated using a four-point scale, including High, Substantial, Modest, and Negligible, as follows:

High:

Efficiency exceeds expectations

Substantial:

Efficiency is what would be expected in the project/ operation’s sector.

Modest:

Efficiency is below expectations in the project/ operation’s sector.

Negligible:

Efficiency is very low in comparison with both the benefits (if any) and with recognized norms in the project/ operation’s sector.

2.2.4 Overall Outcome

This FE will assess the Overall Outcome in a very brief (1-2 sentences) description. This will be based on the integrated assessment of Relevance, Efficacy, and Efficiency above.

Rating:  Overall Outcome rating is derived by combining the assessments of Relevance, Efficacy, and Efficiency, using a 6-point scale, as follows:

Highly Satisfactory:

There were no shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

Satisfactory:

There were minor shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

Moderately Satisfactory:

There were moderate shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

Moderately Unsatisfactory:

There were significant shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

Unsatisfactory:

There were major shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance.

Highly Unsatisfactory:

There were severe shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

2.2.5 Sustainability and Risks to Development Outcomes

The FE will assess how sustainability issues were considered in the project design, planning and implementation, examining:

  • The extent that the benefits of the project are likely to be sustained after the completion of this project; exit strategies, and approaches to phase out assistance provided by the project including contributing factors and constraints
  • key risks that may affect maintenance of project outcomes after project closure, including institutional, financial, technical, and regional cooperation risks
  •  Key factors that will require attention in order to improve prospects of sustainability of Project outcome
  • Success stories and potential for their replication/ scaling up of the approaches and outcomes
  • Sustainability of capacities built at the individual and organizational level including a focus on IT systems, data collection and analysis and sustainability of regional data sharing.
  • The extent to which technical manuals, guidelines, and training programs developed under the project incorporate and promote principles of resource efficiency in living marine resources, fisheries and aquaculture management.
  • Assessment of Environmental and Social Performance: the Final Evaluation shall assess the extent to which project implementation complied with the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and relevant Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), including the integration of ESF requirements into project regulatory procedures, implementation, and management. The assessment should review the effectiveness of stakeholder engagement and consultation processes, operation of grievance redress mechanisms, management of labor and working conditions risks, and the extent to which technical assistance activities were designed and implemented in a manner consistent with ESF principles and requirements. The evaluation should identify any environmental or social implementation challenges encountered, assess how they were addressed, and document lessons learned for future operations, main lessons and recommendations for harmonizing or comparable/ interventions in future, e.g. comprehensive proposals for future interventions based on the current evaluation findings.
  • Document cross-cutting outcomes: Assess contributions to institutional strengthening, regional cooperation, capacity building, climate resilience, private sector engagement, and other relevant cross-cutting objectives supported by the project.

 

2.3 Key Evaluation Questions

Articulating the above, the following core questions can guide assessments in the FE. The consultant may refine, add to and operationalize for the inception report and evaluation matrix, which will be subject to agreement with PERSGA:

  • Theory of Change and contribution: To what extent did the project’s assumptions and causal pathways remain valid, and how did project interventions contribute to observed outcomes?
  • Relevance: To what extent did the project objectives, design and interventions remain aligned with regional fisheries and aquaculture priorities, World Bank and PERSGA strategic priorities, beneficiary needs and changing circumstances?
  • Efficacy: To what extent were the PDO and intended outcomes achieved, or are likely to be achieved by project closure, based on the Results Framework and other credible evidence?
  • Efficiency: How efficiently were financial, human and institutional resources, implementation arrangements, procurement, financial management and partnerships used to deliver results?
  • Implementation and management performance: How effective were project governance, coordination, M&E, stakeholder engagement, adaptive management and regional cooperation arrangements?
  • Sustainability and risks: How likely are project benefits, institutional capacities, regional platforms, data systems, partnerships and other results to be sustained after project closure, and what are the principal risks?
  • Environmental, social and cross-cutting performance: To what extent were relevant ESF/ESS requirements and cross-cutting objectives, including institutional strengthening, climate resilience, capacity building and private-sector engagement, effectively addressed?
  • Lessons and future programming: What evidence-based lessons, scalable practices and recommendations should inform future regional fisheries and marine resource management interventions?

3. Expected Deliverables

The following deliverables are expected (see schedule of deliverables below):

3.1 Inception report

The FE consultant will prepare an inception report, which details his/her conception of the assessment, the approach and how the evaluation questions will be addressed. This is to ensure that the evaluator and the stakeholders have a shared view of the assessment. The inception report will include an evaluation matrix summarizing the evaluation design, methodology, questions, data sources, collection and analysis tools, and measures by which questions will be evaluated. The report will include the scope of work, work plan, timeframe after starting the evaluation process. The inception report should include a proposed schedule of tasks; activities and deliverables, with clear responsibilities for each task or product. The inception report will be discussed and agreed upon with PERSGA and project stakeholders.

3.2 Draft assessment report

The FE consultant will prepare a draft Project Assessment Report, cognizant of the proposed format of the report and checklist used for the assessment (outlined in 3.3 below). The draft report will be submitted to PERSGA for review and comments by its review panel and stakeholders, and to validate that the evaluation considered all relevant information and meets the required approach and quality criteria. The report will be produced in English. PERSGA is responsible for ensuring timely arrangement for the review and validation of the report involving stakeholders’ remarks within the allocated time-frame. Within undertaking the assessment and preparation of the draft report, the consultant is expected to carry out field mission to the region in order to collect and confer data and information.

The assessment report should provide extra detailed information as annexes, such as tables with Indicator> Baseline> Target> Actual> Assessment of Achievement, and other similar data. The appraisal should also discuss whether indicators were appropriate measures of the intended outcomes.

3.3 Final FE Report and regional workshop

The consultant shall consider above comments on the draft report to develop the final assessment report. The content and the structure of the final analytical report with findings, recommendations and lessons learnt should cover the above scope of the evaluation and should meet the requirements of M & E for PERSGA and World Bank. Following clearance of the assessment report, the consultant will be invited to participate and present assessment findings and recommendations in the project FE regional workshop.

The content is expected to include (at least) the following:

  • Executive summary (2-4 pages)
  • Introduction (1-2 page)
  • Description of the evaluation approach and methodology (6-8 pages)
  • Project context and rationale (4-6 pages)
  • Achievement of outcomes against objectives
  • Analysis regarding the project progress and achievements of the objectives, outputs and outcomes; challenges, impacts, etc., considering the scope outlined above (10-12 pages)
  • Analysis of opportunities and options for guidance in relevant future interventions (6-8 pages)
  • Other key findings; practices, lessons learned and potential success stories (4-6 pages): Lessons should be evidence-based, actionable, and relevant for future regional fisheries and marine resource management operations, with clear implications for successor interventions.
  • PERSGA performance (2-4 pages)
  • Conclusions and recommendations (4-6 pages)
  • Appendices (charts, tables, terms of reference, itinerary, people interviewed, documents reviewed, further readings, etc)

3.4 Tentative schedule of the consultancy Deliverables

Deliverable

Time Frame

Inception Report

Within one week after signing of contract

Review and agreement on Inception Report

Within one week after submission of the report

Draft Assessment Report (including field mission)

Within six weeks after approval of the inception report

Review of Draft Assessment Report

Within two weeks after submission of the draft report

Final Report with review comments addressed

Within two weeks after receiving PERSGA comments on draft report

Presentation of the key findings and recommendations in FE regional workshop

Within a month from clearing the Final Report

4. Management, Coordination and PERSGA Inputs

4.1 Supervision and review of deliverables

The consultant will report to the designated PERSGA Project Coordinator/official responsible for the SFISH Regional Component. PERSGA will designate a review panel for the assignment and will provide consolidated comments on deliverables within the review periods stated in Section 3.4. Acceptance of deliverables will be based on conformity with this TOR, the agreed inception report and evaluation matrix, and applicable PERSGA and World Bank requirements.

4.2 PERSGA inputs and facilitation

PERSGA will facilitate the assignment by providing or arranging timely access, subject to applicable confidentiality requirements, to relevant project documentation and data, including the Project Appraisal/implementation documents, Results Framework data, progress and financial reports, procurement information, M&E records, aide-memoires, activity reports, technical outputs and other relevant project records. PERSGA will also facilitate contact with National Coordinators, Focal Points and other key stakeholders and support coordination of mission meetings and the regional workshop.

4.3 Independence, confidentiality and conflict of interest

The consultant shall conduct the evaluation independently, impartially and with professional integrity. Any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest shall be disclosed promptly to PERSGA. Information obtained through the assignment shall be treated confidentially where appropriate, and stakeholder views shall be presented in a manner that protects respondents where confidentiality has been requested. Evaluation findings and ratings shall be evidence-based and shall remain the professional responsibility of the consultant.

5. Type of contract, duty station and payment

This contract falls under short-term consultant category system of PERGSA. It is on a lump sum basis, and payment will be in instalments linked with deliverables as specified below.

The consultant will work from homebase, where he/she has access to the relevant technical literature, to prepare for the evaluation. The consultant will undertake a mission to PERSGA region to conduct field assessments and establish required arrangement and networking with review team at PERSGA, and undertaking interviews with relevant participants/beneficiaries, examine project outputs; review & update input information/data, and discuss, thematic approach, layout, analysis results, content, etc. of the draft document.

The payment instalments will be owed as follows:

  • 25% after adoption of the inception report
  • 50% after undertaking the field mission and submission of the draft assessment report
  • 25% after the approval of the final report, participation in the final evaluation workshop and submission of workshop report

6. Required qualifications/expertise and application procedure

  • Advanced degree (preferable PhD) in marine environmental policies, living marine resources/ fisheries management, marine sciences, development policies, economic planning, economics, project management or other related fields.
  • Extensive knowledge and expertise in the field of evaluation of development projects and programs, including working with international organizations and donors, relevant technical areas for at least 15 years.
  • Experience with assessment of similar World Bank and PERSGA projects is preferable. Experience and familiarity with working in the region will be an added value.
  • Knowledge and experience with result-based management and evaluation methodologies, applying indicators and reconstructing or validating baseline scenarios;
  • Demonstrable analytical and reporting skills of international standards;
  • Excellent English communication skills. Arabic and French are advantages.

 

Qualified candidates are requested to submit their updated CVs, together with expression of interest (EOI) to PERSGA in Jeddah, Kingdome of Saudi Arabia, at the email address: sourcing@persga.org. Deadline for receiving application is 26 September 2026.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Sri Lanka

Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project

Loan No.: 9290-LK

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Detailed Engineering Estimates, Environmental & Social Screening Reports (ESSRs) and Environmental & Social Management Plans (ESMPs) Preparation for 720km Rural Roads

Reference No: LK-RDA-567082-CS-QCBS

The Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka (GOSL) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") include engaging a qualified national consultancy firm to prepare Detailed Engineering Estimates (DEEs), Environmental and Social Screening Reports (ESSRs), and Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) or Codes of Environmental and Social Good Practice (CESGPs) for the rehabilitation and improvement of approximately 720 kilometres of rural roads across eight (8) districts in five (5) provinces under the Post-Disaster Recovery Additional Financing component of the ICDP. The Services shall also include conducting a comprehensive economic analysis of the proposed rural road investments and ensuring full integration of climate-resilient design principles, geotechnical assessments, and World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) compliance. The duration of the assignment shall be eight (8) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained from the undersigned or via the following website: https://rda.gov.lk/index.php?option=com_inquiries&view=biddetail&Itemid=130&lang=en.

The Road Development Authority (RDA) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications, relevant experience, and technical capacity to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core business and years in business; relevant experience; technical and managerial capability of the firm; quality assurance systems and relevant certifications;
  2. General experience of the firm and its capacity to deploy a Team Leader; Environmental Specialist; Social Specialist; Civil Engineers; Geotechnical Specialist; Climate Resilient Expert; and a GIS Officer for the assignment;
  3. Experience in World Bank-funded Environmental and Social Screening; experience in engineering estimates and BOQ preparation; E&S screening/management assignments; Geotechnical and climate-resilient design assignment;
  4. Financial strength based on audited financials; average annual turnover and demonstrated financial capacity to undertake the assignment; and
  5. Relevant experience in Sri Lanka; and/or relevant experience in South Asian countries and/or the wider regional context.

 

Note: 

  1. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.
  2. When providing information relating to (b), it shall be made clear whether the experience of the firm was in the capacity of a principal firm (lead partner) or as an associated firm (sub-consultant/JV partner), with detail regarding the scope of the services.
  3. Firms submitting their EoI response as a Joint Venture (JV) will be evaluated individually for all of the above criteria, while only the lead firm will be evaluated in case of a submission with sub-consultancy or consortium. 

Consultants are requested to submit the following supporting documents against the above- mentioned shortlisting criteria: 

  1. Registration paper of the firm(s).
  2. JV agreement/letter of intent (if applicable).
  3. Firm’s profile / Brochure.
  4. Audited financial reports for the last three years.
  5. Service experience record (including nature, total cost, total input in terms of staff-months, employer, location of service, scope of services, etc.) 
  6. The experience of a parent company, subsidiary company, group company or associates (whatever the name) of the Applicant shall not be considered in evaluation. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.16, 3.17, and 3.18 of the World Bank’s "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" Fifth Edition, September 2023 (Procurement Regulations), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained from the office of the Project Director, Inclusive Connectivity & Development Project (ICDP), during office hours from 09:00 to 15:00 hrs at Inclusive Connectivity & Development Project (ICDP), Road Development Authority, 3rd Floor, 1st Stage, Sethsiripaya, Battaramulla. Telephone: +94 11 2885765 / +94 11 2885766; Facsimile number: +94 11 2885765; Electronic mail address: wbicdpbid@gmail.com

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by email[EB1] ). Clearly marked "Expression of Interest - LK-RDA-567082-CS-QCBS - Consultancy Services for Detailed Engineering Estimates, Environmental & Social Screening Reports (ESSRs) and Environmental & Social Management Plans (ESMPs) Preparation for 720km Rural Roads" on or before 1000 hours (UTC+5:30) on 12/10/2026.
