SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS

GOODS

 

 

Country: The Republic of Suriname

Name of Project:Suriname Competitiveness and Sector Diversification project (SCSD)

Contract Title:Remaining innovation lab goods

 

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IBRD 8985 SR

RFQ Reference No.::  SR-MEA-554782-GO-RFQ

 

1. The Government of Suriname has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the project Suriname Competitiveness and Sector Diversification project (SCSD) loan IBRD 8985 SR and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract[1] for Machines online

2. The Project Implementing Unit of Suriname Competitiveness and Sector Diversification project (SCSD) loan IBRD 8985 within the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation now invites Bids from eligible Bidders for Goods such as mentioned in table 1. All goods shall be new and unused.

 

Please note: This Invitation consists of a total of 6 items. Bids will only be accepted for evaluation if the 2 mandatory items (Item 1. Big CNC  and Item 2, 1 Fiber Laser  are fully priced. Failure to provide pricing for these 2 mandatory items shall result in the immediate rejection of the bid as non-responsive."

 

Bidding will be conducted through national competitive procurement through the procurement method RFQ as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

  1. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Project Implementing Unit, Suriname Competitiveness and Sector Diversification project (SCSD) at the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation, the procurement specialist at the email addresses:  procurement.ez@gov.srcc: cus@surinamecompete.org
  2. The bidding document can be requested through email.
  3. Bids must be delivered by email by June 18, 2026, at 2.00 PM. Late Bids will be rejected.
  4. All Bids must be accompanied by a signed Bid-Securing Declaration.
  5. The addresses referred to above are:

Attn: PIU SCSD Project

Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation

CUS Department 2nd floor unit 2.2

Frederik Derbystraat 68a

Email: procurement.ez@gov.sr and cc; cus@surinamecompete.org

 

 

 

Mandatory RFQ Conditions and Submission Requirements

Equipment FabLab – SCSD Project

 

1. Quotation Addressed To

Mr.Jean van Eenaeme, Procurement Specialist SCSD Project

jean.van.eenaeme1@gmail.com

The quotation must be prepared for the delivery, installation, commissioning, and training of the requested equipment for the SCSD project/FabLab.

 

2. Scope of Supply

The quotation must include, at a minimum:

•  Supply of the offered equipment in accordance with the requested specifications.

•  Delivery to the FabLab location in Suriname.

•  Installation and setup of the equipment.

•  Functional testing and commissioning.

•  Operator training and basic maintenance instruction.

•  Warranty and aftersales support during the warranty period.

•  All required standard accessories for normal operation.

•  Technical documentation, datasheets, manuals and warranty documentation.

Supply-only quotations, or quotations limited to shipment/delivery of boxed equipment without installation, commissioning and training, may be considered non-responsive.

 

3. Technical Compliance

The bidder shall quote in accordance with the requested specifications. Any deviation from the requested specifications must be clearly stated and explained. A technical compliance matrix must be submitted with the quotation, showing for each requirement: requested specification; offered specification; compliance status; deviation, if any; and reference to datasheet/brochure page. Offers that do not clearly identify deviations may be considered non-responsive.

 

4. Mandatory Product Information

For each offered item, the bidder must provide:

•  Brand, exact model, and manufacturer.

•  Product installed dimensions and net weight.

•  Country of origin.

•  Full technical datasheet of the exact offered model/configuration.

•  Configuration list and included accessories.

•  List of exclusions, if any.

•  Recommended spare parts and consumables list, including pricing.

Generic catalogues without clear identification of the exact offered model/configuration may be rejected.

 

5. Supplier Qualification

The bidder must provide evidence of capability to supply, install and support the offered equipment. The bidder shall submit:

•  Company registration details (KKF).

•  Confirmation whether the bidder is the manufacturer, authorized distributor, authorized reseller, or system integrator.

•  If not the manufacturer, a manufacturer authorization letter or proof of authorized supply/support relationship may be requested.

•  Details of the technical support team and local support provider.

 

6. Electrical, Utility and Site Requirements

For each machine, the bidder must provide a site preparation sheet including: required voltage; phase and frequency; maximum current; recommended breaker size; plug or connection type; grounding requirements; compressed air or gas requirements (if applicable); water cooling/chiller requirements (if applicable); ventilation/fume extraction requirements; floor space and working clearance; floor loading requirements; environmental requirements (temperature and humidity); and unloading/forklift/crane requirements. The FabLab will arrange the required facilities based on the information provided by the bidder.

 

7. Installation, Commissioning and Training

The quotation must include installation, commissioning and training. Commissioning shall include: physical installation/setup; power-up and functional testing; test run or sample output; verification of main machine functions; basic operator and maintenance instruction; handover of manuals and warranty documents; and a signed commissioning/acceptance report. Training shall cover safe operation, basic machine use, routine maintenance, and basic troubleshooting.

 

8. Warranty and Aftersales Support

The warranty period shall be a minimum of one year from the date of successful commissioning and signed acceptance. The quotation must state the warranty period, scope, exclusions, local support arrangement, and procedure for warranty claims. The bidder shall provide local support and aftersales service throughout the warranty period.

 

9. Safety Requirements

Where applicable, offered machines must include relevant safety provisions such as: emergency stop; safety interlocks; protective covers or enclosures; laser safety protection/PPE; fume extraction or ventilation provisions; safety labels and operating instructions; and user manuals with safety instructions. Laser equipment must include appropriate safety documentation and recommended PPE.

 

10. Pricing Requirements

The quotation must be priced in USD and must clearly show: equipment price; required accessories; delivery to FabLab; installation; commissioning; training; warranty/aftersales support; and optional spare parts and consumables (listed separately). Prices must be quoted inclusive of import duties and delivery to the FabLab. VAT shall be quoted at 0%. Any exemption from import duties will be determined after award.

 

11. Payment Terms

•  85% of the contract sum upon delivery of the equipment to the FabLab.

•  15% of the contract sum after successful installation, commissioning, training and signed acceptance.

 

12. Delivery Time

The bidder must state the delivery time to the FabLab, including production time, shipping time, import/customs clearance, and local delivery.

 

13. Quotation Validity

The quotation and pricing must be valid for four weeks from the date of issue.

 

14. Clarifications and Right to Reject

The purchaser may request clarifications, additional technical documentation, manufacturer confirmation, or proof of supplier capability. The purchaser reserves the right to reject incomplete quotations, non-compliant offers, offers with unclear deviations, or offers that do not demonstrate sufficient capability for delivery, installation, commissioning and aftersales support.

 

15. Evaluation Criteria

Quotations will be evaluated based on: technical compliance with the requested specifications; completeness of submitted documentation; supplier qualification and experience; delivery and installation capability; warranty and aftersales support; delivery time; and price. The purchaser is not obligated to select the lowest-priced quotation if the offer does not sufficiently meet the technical, support, documentation, or delivery requirements.

 

16. Required Technical Specifications

 

Item 1 – ShopBot PRS Standard 96 x 48 x 8 IN, or similar (Qty: 1)

•  Cut/Movement Area: 3000mm x 1245mm x 200mm

•  Collets: Includes 1/4″ and 1/2″ ER25 Collets (1 each)

•  Min Cut Speed: 150mm per second

•  Positional resolution: 0.015mm or better

•  Precision linear rail and bearings on Y-axis and Z-axis; hardened steel track on X-axis

•  Rack-and-pinion power transmission on each axis

•  Cutting speeds: 360 in/min; rapid speeds: 600 in/min

•  Emergency stop disconnect switch and spindle interlock remote pendant

•  Dust Skirt ready to connect to dust collector

•  Include CAD/CAM Software from Vectric (VCarve Pro standard; upgrade to Aspire available)

 

Item 2 – 2000W Fiber Laser Cutter, or similar (Qty: 1)

•  Laser source: Raycus Fiber min 2000W (or similar)

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE Nº 06/2026

(SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA INDIVIDUAL)

País: Brasil

Mutuário: Estado de Sergipe

Nome do Projeto: Projeto para Aceleração Digital Eficiente de Sergipe – Conecta-SE

Título do Contrato: Serviços de Consultoria Individual especialista em Data Center.

Empréstimo no 9793-BR

Referência nº : BR-SEPLAN-472988-CS-INDV

 

O Estado de Sergipe recebeu um financiamento do Banco Mundial para o custo Projeto para Aceleração Digital Eficiente de Sergipe – Conecta-SE, Acordo de Empréstimo nº 9793-BR, e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos para Contratação de Consultor individual especializado para: (i) planejar e executar diagnóstico técnico baseado em evidências da infraestrutura de data centers e dos ambientes computacionais definidos no Anexo de Escopo; (ii) projetar cenários de arquitetura-alvo e recomendar solução para horizonte de 10 (dez) anos, com análise de riscos, TCO/LCC, continuidade, segurança e sustentabilidade; (iii) auxiliar na elaboração dos artefatos técnicos da contratação subsequente; (iv) realizar transferência de conhecimento; e (v) prestar apoio técnico consultivo e independente ao processo de seleção, nos limites e produtos P1 a P6 abrangendo o site principal do Estado de Sergipe (localizado nas atuais dependências da EMGETIS e seu site-backup (antigo prédio da SEFAZ).

 

Os serviços de consultoria incluem: diagnóstico técnico e auditoria da infraestrutura atual e legada de Data Centers e ambientes computacionais; levantamento e inventário de ativos, análise de capacidade, resiliência, conformidade, segurança e governança; planejamento estratégico e modelagem de cenários de arquitetura futura, incluindo análise comparativa de TCO/LCC, continuidade operacional, riscos e sustentabilidade; apoio à elaboração de especificações técnicas e Termo de Referência para a contratação da nova infraestrutura; transferência de conhecimento às equipes do Estado; e apoio técnico especializado e independente na avaliação das propostas do processo de seleção subsequente. O escopo completo encontra-se descrito no Termo de Referência, no seguinte link: https://www.se.gov.br/seplan/conecta_se

Diante do exposto, a Secretaria Especial de Planejamento, Orçamento e Inovação – SEPLAN, por meio de sua Unidade de Gerenciamento do Programa (UGP), torna público que está aberto o prazo para Consultores Individuais manifestarem seu interesse em prestar os serviços de consultoria descritos. Os interessados deverão demonstrar, por meio de seu currículo, que possuem as qualificações e experiência relevante para desempenhar os serviços.

Manifestação de Interesse: Os interessados deverão apresentar Currículo Profissional, no qual o cumprimento dos requisitos obrigatórios e desejáveis, bem como suas qualificações e experiência relevantes para o escopo dos serviços, estejam claramente demonstrados.

Os critérios de avaliação do perfil profissional do(a) Consultor(a) Individual estão descritos no item 6 do Termo Referência (TDR) da consultoria – disponível no seguinte link: https://www.se.gov.br/seplan/conecta_se

 

O(a) consultor(a) individual será selecionado(a) através da avaliação de suas qualificações e experiências, de acordo com os procedimentos do Banco Mundial para Consultores Individuais contidos no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos, Quinta Edição – setembro de 2023, Seção VII, Parágrafos 7.34 a 7.39 (Métodos aprovados para seleção de consultores individuais).

Caso haja mais de um processo de seleção de consultores individuais em andamento no âmbito do CONECTA-SE, o profissional poderá se candidatar a todos aqueles para os quais entenda possuir as qualificações necessárias. Contudo, apenas poderá ser contratado em um deles. Assim, caso seja selecionado em mais de um processo, deverá optar por apenas um.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para os parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 da  Seção III do Regulamento que define a política do BIRD em matéria de Conflito de Interesses, bem como, as cláusulas de Fraude e Corrupção contidas no Anexo IV do Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento, edição setembro/2023.

 

Mais informações podem ser obtidas por meio do e-mail:

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(FRAMEWORK AGREEMENTS FOR CONSULTING SERVICES )

 

Lebanese Republic

Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR)

Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP)

Reference No.: FA-CS-BLDG (PARTIAL DAMAGE)

 

Assignment Title: Framework Agreemtns for the Design, structural assessment, rehabilitation and construction supervision of public buildings affected by varying levels of damage (slightly, partially damaged)

 

The Lebanese Republic (hereinafter called the “Borrower”) has received financing in the amount of US$250 million from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) (the “Bank”) toward the cost of the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP). The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), acting as the executing agency on behalf of the Government of Lebanon, intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under contracts for consulting services under Framework Agreements.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve engaging Design & Supervision Consultants under Framework Agreements for several contracts to Design, structural assessment, rehabilitation and construction supervision of public buildings affected by varying levels of damage (slightly, partially damaged  across Beirut & Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and South Lebanon

The Framework Agreements will be concluded through a Two-Stage Selection Process and the consulting services shall include the preparation of:

  • Task 1: Structural Validation and Damage Assessment
  • Task 2: Supporting the Environmental and Social Framework
  • Task 3 a - Design of Slightly Damage

            b - Detailed Design for Moderate and partially damage

  • Task 4  Support to Procurement and Contracting Process
  • Task 5   Construction Supervision

The Framework Agreement will be signed for a duration of Thirty-Six (36) months with multiple qualified engineering consultancy firms. Specific assignments will be awarded as Call-Off contracts across distinct Call-Off Modules (ranging from slight to moderate  damage levels) on an as-needed basis.

The full version of the Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found on the CDR website at: https://www.cdr.gov.lb/en-US/Procurment.aspx

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultant Brochures may also be included in the submission.

The shortlisting criteria for Stage 1 evaluation are:

1. Firm Legal Standing & Core Buisness and Years of Experience

  • Legal registration and authorization to operate in its country of incorporation, demonstrating financial soundness.
  • Legally established consulting firm (or lead member of a Joint Venture of maximum two (2) members) with a minimum of Fifteen  (15 ) years of demonstrated experience   in design and supervision services for  buildings projects. (preferably Public Building)

 

2. Specific Technical Experience :

  • Design: Experience with at least three (3) projects of building designs within the last ten (10) years, with one involving detailed assessment and structural evaluation of damaged buildings (slightly, partially), including designs, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities Of buildings.  Building Rehabilitation Design experiences have added advantage.
  • Supervision: Experience as Lead Engineer/Supervision Consultant on at least two (2) projects within the last ten (10) years involving construction supervision and contract management of Buildings
  • Proven experience with Lebanese technical/regulatory frameworks. Experience under international financing institutions (including World Bank standards and Guidelines) is considered as an advantage.

3. Key Staff Pool & Quality Management (Stage 1 Requirements):

  • Submission of an accessible Key Experts pool available on an "on-call" basis.
  • A standard Quality Management Approach and preliminary methodology

 

4. Organizational & Managerial Capacity:

  • Demonstrated organizational and managerial capacity, including adequate in-house technical resources and project management systems to deliver assessment, technical verification, rehabilitation, repair, strengthening, and design services for slightly to partially damaged public buildings, including multiple sites concurrently.
  • Submission of a Quality Management Approach (maximum ten (10) pages) describing the Firm’s standard procedures, organizational arrangements, and quality assurance and quality control mechanisms for condition assessment and technical verification; feasibility and rehabilitation studies; architectural, structural and seismic assessment and design; MEP assessment and design; preparation of technical specifications, BOQs, cost estimates, tender documents; and construction-related technical services for slightly to partially damaged public buildings.

Interested consultants are requested to keep their EOIs to a maximum of twenty-five pages.

Please note that at this shortlisting stage:

  • Technical and financial proposals are not requested.
  • Key Experts, if proposed for the assignment, will not be evaluated.
  • Requests for clarification on the REOI or TOR may not be replied to at this time, as the allocated time for submission of EOI does not permit such exchanges.

The shortlist shall comprise five (5) to eight (8) consulting firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting Services and Consulting Services, dated February 2025, setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a Joint Venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected.

Shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit their proposals, upon which a Consultant will be selected in accordance with the (LCS) described in the “World Bank “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting services” dated February 2025 and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Shortlisted Consultants will subsequently be invited to submit proposals under the Framework Agreement selection process in accordance with lcs  the Quality Based Selectionmethod described in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (February 2025).

The deadline for receiving Expressions of Interest shall be by Tuesday, September 22nd, 2026 at 12:00 noon Beirut local time.

Expressions of Interest (EOI) shall be delivered to the address below by hand or courier, including one (1) original, one (1) copy and one (1) electronic copy on CD-ROM.

procnotices.contact_address: 92J6+Q6W, Angré, ABIDJAN

procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIQUE DE COTE D’IVOIRE

                                                                                                                             Union-Discipline-Travail

                                                                                                                                  ------------------------

                                           MINISTERE DE L’EDUCATION NATIONALE, DE L’ALPHABETISATION ET DE L’ENSEIGNEMENT TECHNIQUE

                                                                                                                                     --------------------

                                                                   PROJET DU PROGRAMME DE RENFORCEMENT DU SYSTEME EDUCATIF DE BASE

                                                                                                   Volet Financement de Projet d’Investissement (IPF)

 

                                                                     AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERETS N° 020C/PRSEB-PROJET/IDA-2026-

             SELECTION D'UN CABINET DE COMMUNICATION CHARGE DE LA CONCEPTION ET DE LA MISE EN ŒUVRE D'UNE CAMPAGNE NATIONALE D'INFORMATION ET DE SENSIBILISATION SUR LE PROGRAMME NATIONAL D'AMELIORATION DES PREMIERS APPRENTISSAGES SCOLAIRES (PNAPAS)

 

I.    CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

La Côte d'Ivoire a instauré l'école obligatoire de 6 à 16 ans (loi n°2015-635 du 17 septembre 2015). Si l'accès a progressé (taux brut de scolarisation de 101% en 2022), les évaluations PASEC 2014-2019 révèlent une crise des apprentissages fondamentaux : 67% des élèves en début de scolarité et 60% en fin de primaire sous le seuil suffisant en lecture ; 83% en mathématiques en fin de primaire.

Pour y répondre, le MENAET a élaboré la SNAPAS, opérationnalisée via le PNAPAS, qui fédère plusieurs initiatives antérieures (PAPSE, PEC, PNAAF, AVSI, PALEC, ELAN-CI) et introduit : nouveaux manuels, méthode structurée de lecture par décodage, pédagogie différenciée et remédiation, encadrement de proximité renforcé, et enseignement bilingue progressif dans les écoles pilotes.

Un risque majeur pèse sur l'appropriation du programme : scepticisme de la communauté éducative (perception de « laboratoire permanent »), résistances pédagogiques de certains enseignants et encadreurs, méconnaissance du programme par les parents et les maîtres de maison/répétiteurs.

Le pilier 7 de la SNAPAS prévoit donc une mobilisation de tous les acteurs via un plan de communication de masse (SCRP et DAPS-COGES). Le MENAET/DPFC recrute ainsi un cabinet de communication pour concevoir et déployer une campagne nationale d'information et de sensibilisation sur le PNAPAS, en capitalisant sur les canaux numériques existants (page Facebook DPFC, site dpfc-ci.net, plateforme pnapas.dpfc.ci) tout en s'appuyant prioritairement sur les canaux à forte pénétration populaire : radio (68% des ménages), télévision (93%), et téléphone mobile (WhatsApp, Facebook, TikTok), ainsi que les espaces de parole informels (marchés, grins, prêches, réunions APE/COGES).

Les présents termes de référence ont pour objet de définir le cadre de sélection d'un cabinet de communication national justifiant d'une expertise avérée dans la conduite de campagnes de changement social et comportemental (CCSC) dans le secteur social, en particulier en éducation, en Côte d'Ivoire.

II.   OBJECTIF GENERAL DE LA MISSION

L‘objectif général de la mission est de susciter l'adhésion, la confiance et l'engagement actif de l'ensemble de la communauté éducative ivoirienne, acteurs institutionnels de mise en œuvre, enseignants, parents d'élèves et maîtres de maison/répétiteurs, autour du PNAPAS, afin de favoriser une application effective et durable de ses innovations pédagogiques dans les salles de classe et un accompagnement cohérent des enfants à la maison.

III.  OBJECTIFS SPECIFIQUES DE LA MISSION

  • Faire connaître le PNAPAS (justification, vision, finalité 2030, articulation avec la SNAPAS) auprès des parties prenantes ;
  • Lever les éventuelles réticences au changement chez les acteurs de mise en œuvre (chaîne de supervision et d'encadrement pédagogique, directeurs d'école, enseignants, formateurs de CAFOP) en valorisant les résultats probants déjà obtenus à mi-parcours du PRSEB et par les projets pilotes dont le PNAPAS est issu, et en démontrant la pérennité de la démarche par rapport aux initiatives antérieures ;
  • Faire comprendre et accepter les innovations pédagogiques du PNAPAS : nouveaux manuels et intrants (décodables, déchiffrables, cahiers d'exercices, planches, guides-maîtres), méthode structurée d'apprentissage de la lecture-écriture fondée sur le décodage explicite, pédagogie différenciée et remédiation, de même que les innovations dans l’enseignements des mathématiques et les évaluations régulières des apprentissages ;
  • Clarifier le rôle attendu de chaque acteur (enseignants, encadreurs pédagogiques, directeurs d'école, parents d’élèves) dans la réussite du programme, et le rôle spécifique des maîtres de maison et répétiteurs scolaires à domicile ;
  • Sensibiliser les parents d'élèves à l'importance de l'assiduité, du suivi scolaire à la maison et de l'harmonisation entre l'accompagnement à domicile et les méthodes enseignées en classe ;
  • Sensibiliser spécifiquement les maîtres de maison et répétiteurs scolaires, acteurs non institutionnels mais très présents dans l'accompagnement scolaire à domicile en Côte d'Ivoire, notamment en milieu urbain, à l'utilisation des méthodes et outils du PNAPAS, afin d'éviter que des pratiques concurrentes (par exemple une méthode de lecture différente de celle enseignée en classe) ne brouillent les apprentissages et ne perturbent les enfants ;
  • Renforcer la visibilité institutionnelle du PNAPAS et l’engagement du MENAET auprès de l'opinion publique, des médias et des partenaires techniques et financiers.

IV.  PROFIL ET QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES DU CABINET

Critères d'éligibilité du cabinet

  • Être une agence ou un cabinet de communication légalement constitué en Côte d'Ivoire (ou un groupement incluant un partenaire local), en règle vis-à-vis de ses obligations fiscales et sociales ;
  • Justifier d'au moins cinq (5) années d'expérience dans la conduite de campagnes de communication institutionnelle, de sensibilisation ou de changement social et comportemental (CCSC)
  • Avoir conduit au moins deux (2) missions similaires dans le secteur social (éducation, santé, protection de l'enfance) en Côte d'Ivoire ou en Afrique de l'Ouest francophone au cours des cinq dernières années, avec preuves à l'appui (attestations de bonne exécution) ;
  • Démontrer une expérience de travail avec des institutions publiques ivoiriennes et/ou des partenaires techniques et financiers de l'éducation, avec preuves à l'appui (attestations de bonne exécution) ;
  • Disposer de capacités de production multicanale (imprimé, audiovisuel, digital, radio communautaire) et d'un réseau de diffusion couvrant les 31 régions et 14 districts autonomes du pays (images des équipements, tout document justifiant la propriété du matériel et l’attestation de Bonne Exécution en sont une preuve) ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience au minimum de communication en langues nationales ivoiriennes (attestation de bonne exécution, spot vidéo…).

Composition de l'équipe clé

Poste

Qualifications minimales requises

Chef de mission / Directeur de la stratégie de communication

Bac+4 en communication, sciences sociales ou marketing social ; 10 ans d'expérience dont 5 dans la conduite de campagnes CCSC, Justifier au moins 3 missions de production de spots et capsules pour le grand public, y compris en langues nationales ; expérience dans le secteur éducatif souhaitée.

Expert(e) en communication pour le changement social et comportemental

Bac+3 ; Justifier d’une expérience au minimum confirmée en conception de stratégies CCSC dans un contexte de réforme sectorielle, Justifier d’au minimum deux expériences d’organisation de communication sur terrain dans les espaces publics et/ou de travail avec les relais locaux (chefferies, leaders religieux, leaders communautaires, COGES).

Spécialiste en conception graphique / directeur artistique

Bac+2 dans une filière de Formation en design graphique ; portfolio de campagnes institutionnelles.

Expert(e) en gestion des réseaux sociaux et community management

Bac+2 en communication/en sciences sociales ou informatiques. Justifier de 3 créations Expérience dans l'animation de pages institutionnelles à forte audience, avec une pratique confirmée de WhatsApp (groupes/diffusion) en plus de Facebook et TikTok.

Spécialiste en suivi-évaluation / enquêtes de perception

Bac+5 en statistique, sociologie ou sciences de l'éducation ; expérience en enquêtes CAP (Connaissances, Attitudes, Pratiques).

NB : Les CV détaillés, diplômes et certificats de travail ou Attestation de Bonne Exécution (ABE) des Experts mobilisés doivent être joints aux dossiers de soumission des cabinets/groupements de cabinets.

Evaluation des cabinets / Groupements de cabinets

Le pourcentage de la note technique minimum (NT) requis pour être admis est de 70/100.

L’expertise du cabinet comptera pour 80% et le personnel clé pour 20%.

V.    DUREE DE LA MISSION ET CALENDRIER

La mission est prévue pour une durée globale de 12 mois à compter de la notification de l'ordre de service de démarrage.

VI.  PROCEDURE POUR LA SOUMISSION DES MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERETS

La Sélection de la radio se fera selon la méthode de la Sélection fondée sur la Qualification du Consultant (SQC) et ce, conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), édition de septembre 2025 et relatif à l’acquisition de Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants.

Le dossier de soumission devra être composé de :

  • Pour la conformité administrative le cabinet devra fournir :
  • Une lettre de manifestation d'intérêt/soumission adressée à l’UGP PRSEB ;
  • Les statuts et documents attestant de l'existence légale du cabinet (RCCM, Attestation de non-faillite,…) ;
  • Les attestations de régularité fiscale et sociale (ARF, Attestation de mise à jour CNPS, Quitus de non-redevabilité de l’ARCOP pour les cabinets ivoiriens……);
  • Références professionnelles et attestations de bonne exécution pour les missions similaires citées.
  • Pour la conformité techniques le cabinet devra :
  • Démontrer sa compréhension des termes de référence et des enjeux du PNAPAS ;
  • Produire une note méthodologique détaillée par phase, incluant l'approche de diagnostic, la démarche créative et le dispositif de déploiement et de suivi-évaluation ;
  • Proposer un calendrier éventuel détaillant de la mise en œuvre ;
  • L'équipe proposée, avec curriculum vitae et diplômes des experts clés ;
  • Portfolio de réalisations similaires (visuels, liens vers des campagnes antérieures).

La date limite pour le dépôt des manifestations d’intérêts est prévu pour le 30 septembre 2026 à 10 heures. L’enveloppe du cabinet devra porter la mention « AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERETS N° 20C/PRSEB-PROJET/IDA-2026 - Sélection d'un Cabinet de Communication chargé de la conception et de la mise en œuvre d'une Campagne Nationale D'information Et De Sensibilisation Sur Le Programme National D'amélioration Des Premiers Apprentissages Scolaires (PNAPAS) ».

Les manifestations d’intérêts devront être soumis en français et en cinq (05) exemplaires dont un (1) original et quatre (04) copies (le tout dans une grande et même enveloppe) et déposées sous plis fermé à l’adresse ci-dessous ou transmis par DHL, CHRONOPOSTE, FEDEX, etc.

Les soumissions par voie électronique ne seront pas acceptées.

Les manifestations d’intérêts seront ouvertes en présence du Comité d’évaluation et des représentants des soumissionnaires présents, à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le même jour le 30 septembre 2026 à 10 heures 30 minutes à l’adresse suivante :  Unité Projet PRSEB, sise à Cocody 2 Plateaux, 7ème tranche - Ilot 252 - Lot 3039 - Téléphone : (225) 27 22 55 94 40 Adresse électronique : atmbra@yahoo.com     Cc      yeo_pefougne@yahoo.fr

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

The Government of Indonesia

Global Environment Facility Indonesia Sustainable Cities Impact Project

Grant No.: TF0B8114

 

Assignment Title: Consulting Firm Services for Strengthening Synergized Low-Carbon & Climate Resilience Development, Circular Economy, and Biodiversity Policy and Planning in Bitung City

Reference No.: ID-LH-567731-CS-CQS

 

The Government of Indonesia had received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Global Environment Facility Indonesia Sustainable Cities Impact Project (SCIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: (a) inventory data, profiling and scenario analysis, (b) developing strategies and action plans and (c) formulating practical guidelines to integrate low-carbon, climate-resilient, circular economy, and biodiversity. The Services are expected to start in November 2026 and be performed during a period of 8 months. The total estimated level of effort is approximately 67 technical/professional staff months. Further detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the following website: https://bit.ly/4inBnfx

 

The Directorate of Environmental Affairs, Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

Necessary:

  1. Preparing an action plan document related to environment indicators, city-wide masterplan development, spatial planning, and/or urban design in the last five years;
  2. Having experience working with Indonesian Government Officials at national and/or sub-national level in the last three years; and
  3. Experience working on the preparation and/or implementation of environmental and social policies of World Bank and/or other multilateral development banks.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms as a joint venture or a sub-consultant to enhance their qualifications. In the case of an association, the EOI must explicitly specify whether it is a Joint Venture (all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment) or Sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, the member firm appointed to represent it must be clearly identified. All the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Only the qualifications and experience of members of the joint venture, but not of sub-consultants, shall be considered in the EOI evaluation process.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09.00 AM to 03.00 P.M. Jakarta time (GMT+7) email: ulp@bappenas.go.id

Expressions of interest must be submitted electronically through the SPSE ICB system of Bappenas at https://spseicb.lkpp.go.id/ by September 21st, 2026, 10.00 A.M Jakarta time (GMT+7).

 

Jakarta, September 11st, 2026

procnotices.bid_description: Legal Advisor for MOCI
procnotices.contact_address:
Ministry of Finance - Shanagi District,
Mogadishu, Somalia.
procnotices.contact_organization: Federal Republic of Somalia, Ministry of Finance, Office of the Director General
procnotices.notice_text:
1. Background: In May 2025, the Federal Republic of Somalia, through its Ministry of Finance (MoF) launched the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) project. The project development objective is to promote private sector-led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance.  

The SPRING project is organized around four components (three mutually-reinforcing and one supporting): (i) Component 1: Improving the enabling environment for the private sector; (ii) Component 2: Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity; (iii) Component 3: Enhancing access to finance and resilience for MSMEs; and (iv) Component 4: Project Management. A wide range of activities will be implemented as part of this project to reach its development objective, such as improvements to regulatory/institutional frameworks, the rollout of the digital ID system, financial sector reforms, the creation of a risk-sharing mechanism, and the provision of business development services for micro, small and medium enterprises in select economic sectors, among others.

The MoF received US$105 million from the World Bank, including US$10 million from the Somalia Multi-Partner Fund to implement the SPRING project. As part of this initiative, under Component 1, MoF intends to apply for part of the proceeds from the World Bank to finance the a Senior Legal and Policy Advisor to provide strategic leadership and technical expertise in drafting, reviewing, harmonizing, and implementing priority commercial legislation and regulatory instruments under the SPRING Project.

  1.  Responsibilities: The Senior Legal and Policy Advisor will lead legal and regulatory reforms under the SPRING Project by drafting and reviewing key commercial laws, strengthening the business registration system, and ensuring alignment with constitutional, federal, and international frameworks. The role includes improving regulatory efficiency, supporting harmonization across Federal and Member State levels, providing legal and policy advice, and building institutional capacity. These efforts aim to enhance the quality, transparency, and predictability of business regulations and support private sector development

All other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link:  https://moci.gov.so/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Legal-Policy-Advisor-TOR.pdf

  1. Skills and qualifications

 Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

  • Master’s degree in Law with valid Bar license
  • At least 10 years of legal experience in commercial, public, and regulatory law
  • Strong expertise in legal drafting, research, and analysis
  • Knowledge of Somali legal systems aligned with international standards
  • Proven ability in legal advisory, policy support, and institutional reform
  • Effective communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Leadership capacity with ability to work independently and in teams.
  1. Duration: The proposed duration for the assignment is Twelve Months (12) calendar months from starts date.
  2. The Ministry of Ministry of Finance now invites eligible consulting (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services and furnish the Curriculum Vitae (CV).
  3. Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14, 3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services dated in September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.    
  4. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.
  5. Interested Consultant may obtain further information (in person or by e-mail) at the address below during office hours from 8.00 a.m. – 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday except on public holidays.
  6.   Deadline for submission: Expressions of interest should be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by May12, 2026, at 4:00pm (Somalia Local time)

Attention; Project Coordinator

REPUBLIQUE ISLAMIQUE DE MAURITANIE

 

MINISTERE DE LA TRANSFORMATION NUMERIQUE ET DE LA MODERNISATION DE L’ADMINISTRATION (MTNMA)

Projet Régional d'Intégration Numérique en Afrique de l'Ouest (WARDIP)

AVIS DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

AMI 42/C/MTNMA/WARDIP/2026

 

Elaboration des contenus e-Procurement interactifs Bilingues (AR & FR) de formations, tests et certificats pour les utilisateurs, secteur privé et société civile et animation des formations

 

Le Gouvernement de la République Islamique de Mauritanie, avec l’appui de la Banque Mondiale, a l'intention d’intégrer le Projet Régional d'Intégration Numérique en Afrique de l'Ouest (WARDIP) pour promouvoir la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de transformation numérique du Pays qui vise à développer la pénétration de l'Internet haut débit, des services financiers numériques et des services en ligne (e-Gouvernement).

Le Projet Régional d'Intégration Numérique en Afrique de l'Ouest (WARDIP) – Composante Mauritanie, (ci-après le « Projet ») à travers des actions impliquant les pays de la sous-région, vise spécifiquement à (a) créer un environnement propice au bon développement d’infrastructures numériques adéquates, (b) développer les réseaux à large bande et les services d’internet et (c) simplifier l’accès aux services en ligne.

Dans le cadre de la composante 4 « Développement et intégration du marché en ligne » » et sa sous composante 4.3 « Services gouvernementaux numériques pour l'intégration régionale  », le Projet cherche à recruter un Consultant (firme) pour assister le gouvernement mauritanien pour une « Elaboration des contenus e-Procurement interactifs Bilingues (AR & FR) de formations, tests et certificats pour les utilisateurs, secteur privé et société civile et animation des formation ».

Le Projet WARDIP-MR invite les consultants (firme), admissibles et ayant une expérience avérée dans la réalisation de missions analogues à manifester leur intérêt pour fournir lesdits services.

La méthode de passation choisie est la Sélection basée sur la Qualification des Consultants (SQC) conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés, pour les Emprunteurs Sollicitant le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (FPI)- Juillet 2016 Révisions Novembre 2017, Août 2018 et Novembre 2020.

Les consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires au sujet des documents de référence à l'adresse ci-dessous :

Projet Régional d'Intégration Numérique en Afrique de l'Ouest (WARDIP-MR)

Téléphone : +222 4524 11 02 ; TVZ, N° 099 – Nouakchott ; Courriel : wardip@mtnima.gov.mr 

  1. Les manifestations d'intérêts écrites en langue française comprenant :
  • Une lettre de motivation signée ;
  • Un acte de groupement signé par les parties concernées, en cas de groupement ;
  • La présentation du cabinet, leur organisation technique et managériale ;
  • Les références et les expériences dans le domaine

Le personnel clé n’est pas évaluée à ce stade.

  1. Seront considérées uniquement les expériences attestées par une attestation de bonne exécution du client reconnu. La liste des expériences attestées doit obligatoirement être fournie dans un document en format modifiable (WORD ou EXCEL) transmis par email ou par clé USB et présentant ces expériences sous le format ci-dessous :

Ref

  1. Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent parvenir à l'adresse ci-dessous de la Commission de Passation des Marchés Publics (CPMP) au plus tard le jeudi 10 septembre 2026 à 12h00 (GMT) à l’adresse suivante :

A l’attention de :

Président de la Commission de Passation des Marchés Publics (CPMP/MTNMA)
Ilot ZRC, lot 418, Rue Moulaye El Hacen Ould Moctar El Hacen
Nouakchott, Mauritanie
Téléphone : +222 49 72 71 70

Courriel : cpmp-mtnima@mtnima.gov.mr

  1. Toute fausse déclaration d’expérience entrainera l’exclusion de la candidature et sera rapporté à l’Autorité de Régulation des Marchés Publics (ARMP).
  2. Les candidatures envoyées par voie électronique doivent obligatoirement être suivi, au plus tard sept (7) jours après le délai de réception des soumissions, par un dossier en support papier en deux exemplaires dont une copie originale. Ce dossier doit être accompagné d’une version électronique sur flash USB ou tout autre support électronique si le dossier n’a pas été envoyé par voie électronique.
  3. Les critères d’évaluation et le barème de notation y relatif, sont :

  1. Missions générales dans la conception des contenus interactifs et de plateformes numériques

20

20

  1. Missions dans la transformation digitale de l’administration publique (Systèmes d’information, études, …)

  1. Missions, en relation avec cette mission, réalisées en Mauritanie ou dans l’Afrique de l’Ouest

10

100

(*) NB : les qualifications et les expériences des consultants (Bureaux) seront évaluées sur la base des expériences attestées.

Le consultant classé premier ayant la note maximale sera invité à soumettre une offre technique et financière. En cas de consultants classés 1er ex-aequo, le candidat ayant le plus grand nombre d’expériences similaires évalués au critère 2 et si nécessaire aux critères 3 et 4 sera sélectionné.

procnotices.project_name: GFPP Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project
procnotices.bid_description: Hiring of Environmental Specialist
procnotices.contact_address: Sainbu, Bhaisepati , Lalitpur
procnotices.contact_organization: Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board
procnotices.notice_text:
Government of Nepal

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) –

Sisneri Water Supply Project

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL)

First Date of Publication: 27th August 2026

Environmental Specialist - Ref No. KVWaSIP-IC-04-083/84

1.0 Background

The Government of Nepal (GoN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services include providing technical, procurement, financial management, environmental and social, contract management, and other professional support required for effective implementation of the Project through the Project Management Unit (PMU)

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide a detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating that they possess the required educational qualifications, professional experience, and technical competence to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria for each assignment are specified in the respective Terms of Reference (TOR), which may be obtained from the address or website indicated below

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Environmental Specialist and requests applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position.

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The overall objective of this assignment is to support the PMU in preparation of the environmental safeguard measures under KV WaSIP.

Specific objectives of the assignment are to:

  • Support the PMU in the preparation of environmental and social assessments and instruments commensurate with the project’s environmental and social risks and impacts, to ensure project readiness for appraisal and implementation.
  • Ensure compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards and the environmental requirements set out in the project’s Environmental and Social Management Framework.
  • Guide and support the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments, Environmental Management Plans, and other relevant instruments for future subprojects in accordance with the ESF, World Bank requirements, and applicable Government of Nepal legislation.
  • Support the PMU in ensuring that environmental mitigation measures, monitoring requirements, and reporting obligations are integrated into project design, procurement documents, contracts, and implementation arrangements.
  • Assist in the timely review, endorsement, and signing of key environmental and social documents required for project preparation and implementation.
  • Facilitate and follow up on all required environmental clearances, approvals, permits, and no-objection processes from relevant authorities.
  • Ensure that project activities comply with the Government of Nepal’s applicable laws, regulations, and policies related to environmental management, tree clearance, forest land acquisition, Occupational health  and safety (OHS), and downstream water use rights.
  • Lead and coordinate stakeholder mapping, consultations, and stakeholder engagement activities relevant to project preparation and implementation, ensuring that environmental and social risks and concerns are adequately identified and addressed.
  • Build the institutional capacity of the PMU, PIUs, and other relevant counterparts on environmental and social risk management, including the implementation of mitigation measures, monitoring, documentation, and reporting.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

The duties of the Specialist is mentioned in the Terms of Reference in detail.

4. Qualifications and Experience

All applications will be evaluated against the assignment’s required qualifications below.  

Candidates who comply with the minimum qualifications will be scored according to predefined criteria. A minimum of three candidates will be shortlisted and interviewed. The candidate with the highest score will be invited to negotiate a contract. Referees of the selected candidate may be contacted to verify prior experience, performance, and interpersonal skills. 

Qualifications and Relevant Experience

  • Education:
    • Master’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, or environmental management.
    • Training in environmental impact assessment
  • Work Experience:
  • At least 10 years of experience in the environmental safeguard sector.
  • Working experience with water or hydropower dam projects will be beneficial.
  • Experience in the preparation and review of safeguard documents under multilateral development bank safeguard policy frameworks and the ESF.
    • Experience in reviewing E&S policy documents will be an advantage..
  • Interpersonal Skills
    • Strong analytical and report writing skills in both English and Nepali.
    • Ability to coordinate effectively with concerned stakeholders at construction sites.
    • Willingness to undertake regular field visits, including to project areas that may be remote.
    • Familiarity with the Government of Nepal's legal framework on forest and environmental management.
    • Ability to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team.

5. Evaluation and Selection Method

The Senior Dam Specialist will be hired by the PMU using the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method following “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) Seventh Edition 2025. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations”.

6. Duration of the Assignment

The Environmental Specialist will be engaged on a full-time basis throughout the grant implementation period (approx. 17 months). Based on the performance and if the project is approved, the Environmental Specialist may continue in this role for the project implementation. 

7. Remuneration

A market-based salary package commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications will be offered.

8. Reporting

The Environmental Specialist will report directly to the Project Manager, PMU. He/she will maintain close coordination with the World Bank's Environmental Specialist and other relevant Bank team members throughout the assignment.

9. Location

  • The consultant will be based at the PMU office and may be required to travel outside the valley as needed for project-related procurement activities.
  • The Project shall provide following facilities to consultant during his tenure of service:
  • Office space
  • Email and internet access
  • Required office stationery and other materials
  • Photocopying/printing facilities

10. Application Process

Interested candidates shall submit a complete application package comprising:

  1. Up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV).
  2. Copies of academic and professional certificates.
  3. Contact details for at least three (03) professional references familiar with the candidate’s relevant work.

Applications shall be submitted electronically no later than 17.00 PM on 18th September 2026 to the following e-mail address: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com. Only complete applications received by the deadline will be considered.

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project – Sisneri Water Supply Project

Address: Jawlakhel, Lalitpur

Attention: Executive Director

Email: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com

Website: www.kvwsmb.org.np

procnotices.notice_text:
Entidade Contratante: Ministério da Justiça, Assuntos Constitucionais e Religiosos (MJCR).

Projecto: Projecto de Economia Digital e Governo Electrónico – EDGE

Designação do Contrato: Fornecimento de Material de Escritório e Consumíveis de para Equipamento Informático

País: Moçambique

ID do Projecto: P172350

Dono do Donativo: IDA-906-MZ

RFB Nº.: MZ- MJACER -552043-GO-RFB

Data de Emissão: 10 de Setembro de 2026

 

O Governo de Moçambique recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para apoiar a implementação do Projecto de Aceleração Digital de Moçambique e do Projecto de Economia Digital e Governo Electrónico – EDGE, e pretende aplicar parte desses recursos para efectuar pagamentos no âmbito do contrato de Fornecimento de Material de Escritório e  Consumíveis de para Equipamento Informático destinados à Campanha de Registo Massivo. O Mutuário processará os pagamentos através do método de desembolso por Pagamento Directo, conforme definido nas Directrizes de Desembolso do Banco Mundial para Financiamento de Projectos de Investimento, excepto para os pagamentos que, nos termos do contrato, devam ser efectuados por carta de crédito.

 

Neste contexto, o Ministério da Justiça, Assuntos Constitucionais e Religiosos (MJACR) convida os concorrentes elegíveis a apresentarem propostas seladas para o Fornecimento de Material de Escritório e  Consumíveis de para Equipamento Informático no âmbito da Campanha de Registo Massivo.

 

O processo de contratação será realizado por meio de Concurso Público Nacional, utilizando o método de Request for Bids (RFB), conforme estabelecido no documento “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, edição de Março de 2025 (“Regulamentos de Aquisições”), estando aberto à participação de todos os concorrentes elegíveis, conforme definido nos referidos Regulamentos.

Os concorrentes elegíveis interessados poderão obter informações adicionais junto da Unidade de Implementação do Projecto de Economia Digital e Governo Electrónico – EDGE, do Ministério da Justiça, Assuntos Constitucionais e Religiosos (MJACR), bem como consultar os documentos do concurso durante o horário normal de expediente, das 07h30 às 15h30, de segunda a sexta-feira, no endereço abaixo indicado.

 

Os documentos do concurso (RFB), em língua portuguesa, serão disponibilizados aos concorrentes interessados mediante apresentação de pedido formal por escrito para o endereço abaixo indicado. Os documentos serão enviados por correio electrónico.

 

As propostas devem ser entregues no endereço abaixo indicado , até 09 de Outubro de 2026, às 10:15 horas, CAT - Hora da África Central . Não será permitida a contratação por via eletrónica. Propostas tardias serão rejeitadas. As propostas serão abertas publicamente na presença dos representantes designados pelos proponentes e de qualquer pessoa que deseje assistir, no endereço abaixo indicado.

Todas as Propostas deverão ser acompanhadas de uma Garantia Bancaria, com validade de 120 dias, contados a partir da data de abertura das Propostas, nos seguintes valores:

  • Lote 1 –   400 000,00 MZN
  • Lote 2 –500 000,00 MZN

 

Chama-se a atenção para o Regulamento que exige que o Mutuário divulgue informações sobre a propriedade efectiva do Proponente selecionado, como parte do  Aviso de Adjudicação do Contrato, mediante a utilização do Formulário de Divulgação da Propriedade Efectiva incluído no documento de pedido de propostas.

 

O (s) endereço (s) acima referido (s) é (são):

REPUBLIC OF ZAMBIA

                             MINISTRY OF FINANCE AND NATIONAL PLANNING

      NATIONAL AUTHORISING OFFICE OF THE EUROPEAN DEVELOPMENT FUND

                               

                                     REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

                                    (CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Zambia

Name of Project: Irrigated and Sustainable Agriculture for Transformation (ISAT) Project (P182068)

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: E5970

Assignment Title: Consultancy services for Designing and Piloting of a Farmer-Led Irrigation Development (FLID) intervention in Zambia

Reference No. ZM-MOFNP-570604-CS-QCBS

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Irrigated and Sustainable Agriculture for Transformation (ISAT) Project Preparation and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.  The Project Preparation Grant financing is intended to support the identification, technical assessment, and preparation of priority irrigation schemes that can be taken forward under the full ISAT operation.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Designing and Piloting of a Farmer-Led Irrigation Development (FLID) intervention in Zambia.

Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to support the design of a FLID component for the ISAT project, including the design and piloting of a Results-Based Financing framework tailored to FLID.

Scope of Work

The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks:

a) Fast diagnostic (data collection, analysis): Understand the bottlenecks to scaling up FLID in Zambia and scoping for a Result Based Financing (RBF) framework around the identified irrigation schemes.

  • Characterize FLID potential at farm level (farm size, assets, affordability gaps)
  • Survey the current private sector landscape that is providing goods (supply of irrigation equipment) and services (irrigation services) to assess equipment capital and operational costs for the range of farmer types and farm sizes, understand private sector challenges and draw on private sector insights into opportunities for rapid irrigation technology uptake and expansion.
  • Understand the existing public financing structures and mechanisms for financing smallholder irrigation.
  • Explore the policy and legal barriers in the enabling environment constraining smallholder farmers in autonomously carrying out small-scale irrigation development.

b) FLID intervention and RBF Design: Translate the diagnostic into a set of feasible, scalable FLID intervention models.

  • Develop the design of potential FLID interventions within the ISAT project, providing different options and potential scenarios based on the diagnostic of farmers’ assets, willingness to pay, providers’ capacity, among others.
  • Design an RBF framework and its parameters: Key Result Indicators (KRIs), payment triggers/schedules, eligibility, verification, financial flows, subsidy/rebate, risk-sharing.

c) Piloting the Methodology: The pilot phase serves as a controlled environment to test the feasibility, scalability, and sustainability of the proposed FLID intervention. Particularly irrigation modernization, financing mechanisms, and private sector partnerships. The four sequential stages of the methodology include:

  • Elaborate a piloting methodology of the proposed interventions in Zambia accounting for the time constraint of the project preparation, outlining the process for selecting testing sites, testing financing mechanisms, partnering with irrigation equipment providers and any other intervention design aspects that might be piloted.
  • Identify 10 appropriate sites for piloting based on a set of pre-defined characteristics.
  • Onboard participants of the pilots such as providers, financial institutions, districts, farmers.
  • Define the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) framework to assess the pilot’s performance.

d) Pilot implementation and evaluation: Implement FLID interventions with continuous technical support, collect baseline, midline and end-line data, identify challenges along the implementation process to refine the model and document lessons for national scale-up. Specifically:

  • Deploy the FLID interventions and RBF mechanisms in the selected zones.
  • Execute the MEL framework.
  • Conduct a structured assessment of pilot outcomes and rank the best-performing options

Duration of the Assignment

The assignment is expected to be completed within seven (7) calendar months after signing of contract between November 2026 and May 2027.

Invitation

The National Authorising Office now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Must be a legally registered firm with a minimum of 5 years of continuous operations in providing consultancy services.
  2. Experience in similar assignments, evidence of at least three similar assignments completed in Sub-Saharan Africa within the past ten years. Experience must include:
  • At least one assignment related to Farmer-Led Irrigation Development or smallholder irrigation systems
  • At least one assignment involving performance-based or results-based contracting.

      3. Proven track record working with government agencies, private sector actors, and                          development partners (Consultant to provide copies of contracts for past assignments or                completion certificates as evidence).

      4. The firm must demonstrate strong technical multidisciplinary expertise in Irrigation and                Water Resources Engineering, Agricultural Economics, Market Systems Development and            Private Sector Engagement and Environmental and Social Risk Management

      5.  Managerial capabilities indicating the general qualifications and experience of Principals               (key staff of the firm) and the structure of the organization.

The above required relevant qualifications and experience relate to the qualifications and experience of the firm and should not be based on individual experts as this is not required at this stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on Conflict of Interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture and/or a sub- consultancy. In the case of a Joint Venture, all the partners in the Joint Venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Therefore, each member of JV shall independently meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria. The experience, technical & managerial capability of the Sub-Consultant shall not be evaluated to enhance the qualification of the Lead Firm or JV.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Interested Consultants firms may obtain detailed terms of reference (ToRs) at the address below during office hours from 08.00 to 17.00 hours Local time Monday to Friday except public holidays or visit https://nao.gov.zm/

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by 1st October 2026, at 10:00 Hours Central African Time (+2hours GMT), clearly marked “EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DESIGNING AND PILOTING OF A FARMER-LED IRRIGATION DEVELOPMENT (FLID) INTERVENTION IN ZAMBIA

The firms that will submit their EOI via e-mail must get confirmation of the receipt of their documents. In case the firm does not receive acknowledgement within two working days after sending the documents via email, they should call the numbers provided below for follow-up.

AVIS D’APPEL A CANDIDATURE POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DE DEUX (02) STAGIAIRES EN COMPTABILITE DU PROJET EDUCATION A LA COORDINATION NATIONALE

Date de l’avis : 09 Septembre 2026

Financement Projet N° P507220

Don N°E4100-KM

D’une manière générale, l'Union des Comores à travers le Ministère de l’Education Nationale, de l’Enseignement, de la Recherche Scientifique, de la Formation et de l’Insertion Professionnelle s’associe et participe à l’Approche programmatique multiphase (APM) pour promouvoir des méthodes innovantes pour favoriser l’apprentissage en Afrique de l’est et australe. L’APM proposée, intitulée « Advancing Innovative Methods to Promote Learning » (AIM4Learning) ou Favoriser des méthodes innovantes pour promouvoir l’apprentissage, intègre des approches résolument nouvelles pour offrir une meilleure éducation aux élèves.

Cependant, l’Union des Comores a subi ces dernières années des chocs et des perturbations qui ont fortement impacté le système éducatif du pays, accentué les pertes d’apprentissages, les profondes inégalités scolaires et les risques d’exclusion scolaire des groupes les plus vulnérables. Il est nécessaire de rétablir et sauvegarder l’éducation en tant que droit fondamental, vecteur de développement, facteur de réduction de la pauvreté et levier puissant pour la paix, la résilience aux changements climatiques et au développement durable.

C’est ainsi que le Gouvernement comorien a obtenu un Don de l’Association International de Développement (IDA) et du Fonds du Partenariat mondial pour l’éducation équivalent à 23,7 millions de dollars pour répondre aux besoins du pays en matière d’amélioration et du renforcement de l’éducation pour l’amélioration des Résultats en Matière de Capital Humain aux Comores.

Il est prévu qu’une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce Don sera utilisée pour effectuer le paiement à titre du contrat portant « Recrutement de deux (02) stagiaires en Comptabilité du Projet Education à la Coordination Nationale ».

Les Stagiaires seront recrutés Conformément au « Règlement de Passation des Marchés dans le Cadre du Financement de Projets d’investissements (FPI) Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants », 7ème Edition- Septembre 2026.

La méthode de sélection est la « Sélection de Consultants Individuels (SCI) ».

Tous les consultants intéressés sont priés de retirer les Termes de Référence (TDR) au site du projet : pfss-comores.org

Conditions de candidature pour le stage

Les conditions requises sont les suivantes :

  • Nationalité comorienne,
  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme de grandes écoles au minimum de Bac+3 en gestion ou diplôme équivalent ;
  • Avoir une maîtrise du français (écrit, oral)
  • Expérience professionnelle non requise,
  • Connaître les outils informatiques de base (Word et Excel),
  • Avoir de bonnes compétences en communication orale et écrite. La maîtrise de l'anglais sera un avantage.

Composition des dossiers de candidature :

Le dossier à soumettre sont les suivants :

  • Lettre de motivation adressée au Coordinateur du projet REHEMA ;
  • Curriculum vitae détaillé et actualisé ;
  • Copie du ou des diplômes et attestations de formation pertinents ;
  • Attestations ou certificats de stage ou d’expérience, le cas échéant ;
  • Toute autre pièce jugée nécessaire dans le cadre de l’avis de recrutement...

Les dossiers de candidatures peuvent être déposées au Secrétariat de la Coordination nationale ou dans les Bureaux Régionaux du PFSS à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous au plus tard le Mardi 22 Septembre 2026 à 11 heures 30 (heure locale) avec la mention suivante :

« Recrutement de deux (02) stagiaires en Comptabilité du Projet Education à la Coordination Nationale »

Pour toutes informations complémentaires, veuillez consulter les Termes de Références (TDR) dans le site Web : pfss-comores.org/ www.pfss-comores.org

for China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Projec

Name of Project: China Food Safety Improvement Project

Assignment Title: Information Technology Supervision Services

Reference No.:  GD-FSS-GAMR-CS12

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The total estimated amount for this project is RMB 1.6003 million.

(I) Scope of Services

The service scope of this project covers the full-process supervision services for four informatization sub-projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;
  4. The Capacity Building Project for Food-Related Personnel in Market Regulation.

(II) Service Content

The supervision service agency shall provide full-process supervision services for the implementation of the aforementioned four informatization sub-projects, assisting the project undertaking company and the user party in carrying out their work to ensure the achievement of the predetermined project goals. In accordance with supervision work specifications, the agency shall implement full-process control over project quality, schedule, investment, contracts, and information security. This is to ensure that the construction activities are legal, compliant, reasonable, scientific, and economical, thereby reducing project construction risks and achieving both the overall project goals and the current phase goals.

(III) Service Period

The supervision service period for this project shall commence from the date of contract signing and continue until the project closing date (March 31, 2029).

(IV) Deliverables

Reports and outcome documents shall be submitted at specified dates and frequencies, including but not limited to: Mobilization Report, Supervision Plan, Detailed Supervision Implementation Rules, Supervision Weekly Report, Supervision Monthly Report, Supervision Notice, Meeting Minutes, Special Supervision Report, Supervision Work Summary Report, Project Acceptance Report, and other materials required by the construction unit and the project implementation party.

(V) Agency Qualification Requirements

The supervision service agency must have independently undertaken no fewer than ten information system engineering supervision services within the past three years. The relevant performance records must cover core business types such as government informatization, software platform construction, system integration, and network security. These records must sufficiently demonstrate the agency's comprehensive service capability in full-process supervision and coordination for multi-domain informatization projects.
